name: 0bull
description: Control real iPhones rented from 0bull (screenshots, on-screen text, taps, typing, device commands, recorded macros, an on-phone agent) and publish videos to TikTok and YouTube Shorts from them, through the hosted 0bull Streamable HTTP MCP server plus three workflow skills. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no plugin code. Requires a 0bull account with a rented phone and browser OAuth consent (add the server with auth: oauth, then vibervnbot mcp login 0bull); no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin. Posting sends the user's video and caption to TikTok or YouTube through the phone's own apps. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; screenshots, on-screen text, anything typed on the phone (including passwords or codes you hand the agent) and your videos and captions go to 0bull.net; posts publish publicly to TikTok or YouTube; the server also exposes rental tools that spend money, which the skills tell the model never to call but ViberVN Bot does not block.

name: aave-mcp
description: Aave V3 and V4 through Aave's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.aave.com, no sign-in, no keys in config): live markets and rates on every chain Aave runs on, wallet positions and health factor, rewards, DAO governance, swap quotes, and unsigned transactions for the user's own wallet to sign. Bundles five workflow skills: safe transactions, deleverage, yield analysis, account activity and transaction confirmation. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to mcp.aave.com, which records tool usage for analytics and keeps a wallet address only as a keyed hash. The server never holds keys. Every tool is annotated read-only except submit_signed_order and cancel_order, which relay an order or cancellation the user already signed; the package marks the server untrusted, so ViberVN Bot asks before either runs and refuses them in unattended runs. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: abstract-provider
description: Abstract model provider (GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi-K3) over the OpenAI Responses API with a bundled model catalog. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); requests go to https://api.abstract.inc/v1 through ViberVN Bot' own client with ABSTRACT_API_KEY, which ViberVN Bot reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

name: account-pool
description: Run several accounts of one provider in ViberVN Bot' credential pool: `vibervnbot account <provider> <action>` adds accounts with email verification, shows live usage per account, keeps the least-used account first (fill_first + a 5-minute balance timer over every provider with accounts), parks accounts for hours or on a weekly schedule, shows which bot is on which account and its tokens at API prices, alerts on dead logins, a full pool or a runaway bot, and can start an idle account's 5-hour window with one tiny request (wake). Adapters for anthropic and openai-codex; generic commands for any pool provider. Optional Accounts page in ViberVN Bot Desktop. Linux and Windows. Disclosure — logins stay in ViberVN Bot: park holds an entry out of rotation in ViberVN Bot' pool (mark_exhausted_and_rotate, reason "parked") and unpark is reset_status; the plugin's park list holds labels, ids and times only; expired tokens are refreshed by ViberVN Bot (try_refresh_matching); sign-in, in the terminal and on the Desktop page, runs `vibervnbot auth add`; other profiles' accounts are read with read_credential_pool. It uses each account's access token as ViberVN Bot stores it for live usage and the email check (api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage and /profile, chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage, with the client headers of ViberVN Bot' usage fetcher) and for wake (a command, a page button, or the timer after the opt-in `wake auto-on`): one one-word request per account through ViberVN Bot' Anthropic client or the Codex Responses endpoint, and the account's model list. Telegram alerts through `vibervnbot send -t telegram` to the bot's home channel or a chat id kept in account-pool.json; no telemetry. Its session tracker, a post_api_request hook, runs in every profile and writes labels, ids and token counts only. `setup` writes plugins.enabled of every profile, links the plugin into every profile, removes the retired account-pool-tracker (`vibervnbot plugins remove`) and, with --timer, adds a systemd user timer (Linux) or a Task Scheduler task for the user (Windows, no admin rights). Runs systemctl --user and notify-send (Linux), schtasks, powershell.exe and taskkill (Windows), vibervnbot config set, vibervnbot auth add/remove, vibervnbot send, vibervnbot plugins remove; reads every profile's config.yaml and state.db (read-only), the gateway config (whether the Telegram bot has a home channel) and /proc on Linux. The command registers in the default profile only and provides no tools. Live usage, the email check and wake send each account's own access token from ViberVN Bot' pool straight to its vendor with Claude Code (anthropic) and Codex CLI (openai-codex) client headers. The session tracker reads the running agent's current pool account (label and id only) by scanning Python thread frames for ViberVN Bot' private _credential_pool. On the first run after 3.x it moves parked logins from account-pool-parked.json back into ViberVN Bot' pool and deletes that file.

name: account-switcher
description: Windows desktop plugin that switches which Codex login and which Claude subscription account every local ViberVN Bot profile uses, with one idle-only, verified restart of the gateway (and, on ViberVN Bot before 0.22, of ViberVN Bot Desktop). Refuses while any profile is busy, restores the previous selection if a step fails, and writes a receipt that says whether the switch took effect. Disclosure — Windows only. A switch rewrites, through ViberVN Bot's own commands, the Codex credential order in every profile's auth.json and the CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR line in every profile's .env, so every profile that has the plugin enabled spends the same selected Codex login and the same Claude login (one ViberVN Bot-owned claude-auth folder; no token is copied between profiles). It reads Codex tokens from each profile's auth.json. On ViberVN Bot 0.22 and later it stops and restarts the gateway once ViberVN Bot's own idle proof and the gateway's drain report idle, and ViberVN Bot Desktop stays open and reconnects; on earlier ViberVN Bot it also reads the Desktop backends' dashboard session token from their process environment and closes and reopens ViberVN Bot Desktop (work started in the seconds after the idle check is cut off). It sends the target Codex token to OpenAI's usage endpoint and Claude login tokens to Anthropic's OAuth profile endpoint (also when the setup screen opens); if the target Claude login has expired it first runs the claude CLI once so the CLI renews its own token, which rotates that login's refresh token. No telemetry and no automatic account rotation.

name: acedatacloud
description: Ace Data Cloud GPT models with streaming and tool calling.

name: acedatacloud-media
description: Suno music, Seedance video, HappyHorse (Happy Horse) video, GPT Image images and Nano Banana images by Ace Data Cloud; 17 selectable service toolsets and a Nano Banana image_generate backend. Each generate call spends Ace Data Cloud credits on your ACEDATACLOUD_API_KEY with no ViberVN Bot approval prompt; the model can choose costly options (pro models, 4K, up to 4 images), and prompts and reference URLs go to api.acedata.cloud. Google Search and face analysis also spend Credits. Disclosure — Each generate call spends Ace Data Cloud credits on your ACEDATACLOUD_API_KEY with no ViberVN Bot approval prompt, and the model can pick costly options (pro models, 4K, up to 4 outputs); Google Search and face analysis are billed too. Prompts, reference URLs and face images go to api.acedata.cloud. The tools are on wherever you enable their toolsets, including gateways.

name: actvox
description: Make ViberVN Bot a team member in an ActVox workspace: on a schedule it works the tasks people assign it and answers the comments that @mention it, and submits each task for a person's review. Skills actvox:actvox and actvox:actvox-inbox, a first-turn inbox line (pre_llm_call), /actvox inbox|status, and vibervnbot actvox setup|install-gate. A cron pre-run gate wakes the agent only when the inbox has work, so an empty tick makes no model call. Disclosure — ActVox is reached only through the user's own actvox MCP server (ctx.call_mcp, needs plugins.entries.actvox.mcp_allowlist) and the user's own actvox CLI (the gate runs `actvox inbox --all --json`); on the first turn of every non-cron session the pre_llm_call hook calls the server's check_inbox (up to 5 s) and adds one line saying how many tasks and mentions wait; the plugin holds and reads no credential and sends no telemetry. `vibervnbot actvox install-gate` writes one file, $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/scripts/actvox-inbox-gate.py, only on that explicit command and never over a file it did not write; gate state lives in $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugin-data/actvox/. No background work of its own: the cron job runs only after the user creates it, and from then on anyone who can assign ViberVN Bot a task or @mention it in your ActVox workspaces decides what an unattended agent run on your host works on, with that job's toolsets (dangerous commands follow approvals.cron_mode, deny by default). Unattended writes need the default trust: full on the actvox server.

name: adaption
description: Dataset import, adaptation, augmentation, translation, synthetic generation, and AutoScientist fine-tuning through the hosted Adaption MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with three workflow skills; the MCP server is added separately with OAuth (or an API key for headless use). Disclosure — skill-only, no code; the MCP tools call api.prod.adaptionlabs.ai, and launches spend Adaption credits (the skills request a cost estimate first, ViberVN Bot does not enforce it). ViberVN Bot does not prompt before those tools unless the server is configured with trust: untrusted.

name: adaptive-inference-routing
description: Opt-in background scheduling for host-known delegated sessions, supported cron execution and explicit worker profiles using an existing Adaptive Inference gateway. Interactive and explicitly classified requests retain their routing; model, tools, prompts, output limits and credentials are unchanged. Disclosure: adds only X-Adaptive-Class on an exactly configured chat-completions endpoint. No network calls, file access, processes, telemetry or credential handling in plugin code. Uses a bounded in-memory session index. Cron detection requires the newer public execution-identity capability; auxiliary routing is an explicit provider configuration, not an auxiliary middleware claim.

name: adkit
description: Manage ads on Google Ads, Meta Ads (Facebook, Instagram), TikTok, LinkedIn, Microsoft, Reddit and X Ads through the hosted AdKit MCP: launch campaigns, ad sets and ads as drafts, pull performance reports with breakdowns, browse competitor ads in the Meta, Google and LinkedIn ad libraries, and generate ad creatives. Built for people who run several ad accounts. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets (creates are drafts until you approve publishing); the package marks the adkit server untrusted, so ViberVN Bot asks before every tool the server does not annotate as read-only and refuses them in cron and headless runs. Every tool call goes to mcp.adkit.so; sign-in runs npx mcp-remote@0.1.49 from the npm registry, which stores its OAuth tokens in ~/.mcp-auth. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: adspirer
description: Create, analyze, and optimize campaigns across Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Amazon Ads, ChatGPT Ads, and Microsoft Ads through the hosted Adspirer MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with fourteen paid-media workflow skills and approval safeguards; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets; confirm-before-spend is enforced by skill instructions, not by ViberVN Bot.

name: advisor
description: A persistent second model reviews every agent turn. After each turn the plugin hands the transcript to the model you nominate as advisor and delivers its findings as advice in the same session: [NIT], [CONCERN] or [BLOCKER] notes, held back until a later review raises the same point again, so the primary agent is not interrupted by a one-off remark. It reviews, it does not act: the advisor never edits files, calls tools or changes session state, and only reads the turn transcript. This is the backend counterpart of MoA — one extra model, not a committee: the primary agent does the work and the advisor checks it. Port of pi-omplike-advisor (Petr Baudis / pasky), itself rooted in oh-my-pi (Can Boluk). Runs inside the plugin host with no dependencies beyond ViberVN Bot itself. Disclosure — once the plugin is enabled, every completed turn costs one extra completion through ViberVN Bot's ctx.llm to the advisor model (the primary agent's provider unless you allow a provider/model override under plugins.entries.advisor.llm), carrying the user message, the final reply, every tool call and tool result in the session so far (each clipped to 500 characters) and the contents of a WATCHDOG.md in ViberVN Bot's working directory if one exists; deliverable advice is queued into the CLI session as a user-role message, which starts or interrupts an agent turn; state is kept under $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/advisor/ and reviews run on one background thread; no other network, files or credentials.

name: adwhispr
description: Research competitor ads, clone the winners, and run campaigns through the hosted AdWhispr MCP. Finds brands verified to be advertising in a niche right now, their longest-running Meta and TikTok ads, Instagram content and Google keyword data; clones a proven ad into a finished image or AI video for your brand (free script approval before any credit is charged); and launches paused campaigns on Meta, Google, TikTok, X and ChatGPT Ads. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with twenty-four workflow skills; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets (always created paused, two-step confirm server-side) and renders videos that use paid credits; the AdWhispr server is marked untrusted, so ViberVN Bot asks before every write or spend tool and refuses them in cron and headless runs. Sends research queries and your brand assets to adwhispr.com; sign-in is OAuth through npx mcp-remote@0.1.49.

name: afterforge
description: Local-first regression workbench turning agent failures and corrections into reviewed, evidence-backed checks.

name: agent-analytics
description: Dashboard-only read plugin for Agent Analytics inside ViberVN Bot.

name: agent-batch
description: Parallel AI task orchestrator. Paste a task list into the desktop panel; ViberVN Bot phases it into dependency-ordered groups through the agent_batch_plan / agent_batch_phase tools (or you group it yourself in one click), then each phase dispatches one independent coding agent per task to a GitHub Actions workflow in a repo you name — own branch, own PR — and the panel tracks the runs and the PRs. GITHUB_TOKEN is the only required credential; AGENT_BATCH_REPO, AGENT_BATCH_WORKFLOW, AGENT_BATCH_MODEL and AGENT_BATCH_STATE are optional (the last is a directory override for the plan file, not a secret) and each can be set per plan in the panel instead. Disclosure — ViberVN Bot can read and rewrite the stored phase plan through the agent_batch_plan / agent_batch_phase tools, but dispatch is always a confirmed click in the panel. Each dispatch fires a GitHub workflow_dispatch with your GITHUB_TOKEN (Actions + pull-requests write) on the repo you name. The workflow you copy into that repo installs third-party coding-agent CLIs (cline by default; the others are unpinned npm packages) and runs them unattended, with auto-approve / skip-permissions, repo write access and your provider secrets. They push real branches and open real PRs, and your task text and repository code go to that runner's model vendor. LLM cost belongs to the runner: cline spends Cline Credits or a BYOK key, opencode free models need its zen relay, kilo needs an active Kilo Go subscription (keyless CI runs fail), and claude-code / codex / dsh need their own keys.

name: agent-hint
description: Give the inference engine behind each request a standard, machine-readable view of the agent session that produced it. Injects an X-Agent-Hint header (base64url JSON: session identity and call index, lifecycle state, soft priority, a cache-pinning hint, optional measured statistics) on main LLM requests, and can emit session lifecycle events out of band as local ndjson or as POSTs to a URL you configure. Request bodies are never modified, and nothing is added or sent until the plugin is enabled. Lets a scheduler pin a session to the instance already holding its KV cache, or rank a user-blocked session above background work, without teaching the engine anything about the client. Disclosure — when enabled, every main LLM request carries an X-Agent-Hint header (base64url JSON with the session id, call index, lifecycle state, priority and cache hints) to whatever provider is configured, not only hint-aware engines; with status_sink: http the same session events and usage/latency statistics are POSTed to the status_url you set, and ndjson writes them under $VIBERVNBOT_HOME.

name: agent-hold-em
description: No-Limit Texas Hold 'Em for ViberVN Bot Desktop: play with three isolated ViberVN Bot profile agents using play chips only. Agent decisions use configured models and may consume provider tokens; this is a local game, not gambling software. Disclosure — each opponent is a zero-tool ViberVN Bot agent run in-process under the local ViberVN Bot profile you select for it, using that profile's configured provider credentials and spending its tokens; reads every local profile's name, model and avatar for the picker; stores the table (including hole cards) in plugin-data/agent-hold-em/table.json.

name: agent-janitor
description: Process hygiene for agent machines — finds the background processes your agent left behind (dev servers, tunnels, watchers, nohup jobs) using evidence signals (ppid=1 reparent, port listener via /proc/net/tcp{,6}, dev-server traits, TTL exceeded) and attributes them to the originating tool call via agent-ledger's ledger when present. Dry-run by default: nothing is killed until you write policy_mode=enforce; system daemons and host/VM management agents are exempt by name, a user-editable whitelist covers your real infrastructure, and each kill re-reads the cmdline first (SIGTERM, 2s, SIGKILL with PID-reuse check). stdlib-only, fails open. Disclosure — inside ViberVN Bot it only appends terminal commands that look like they start background work (first 300 characters, which can include inline secrets) to plugin-data/agent-janitor/spawns.jsonl, and reads agent-ledger's ledger.db read-only when present. Killing is a separate CLI you run yourself (janitor_cli.py sweep): after you write "enforce" to plugin-data/agent-janitor/policy_mode it sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL to every process re-parented to PID 1 for over a minute that is not on its built-in exempt list or your whitelist, whoever started it (for example a tmux server or a nohup'd vibervnbot gateway), including other users' processes when run as root. Dry-run first; the dry-run list is the kill list.

name: agent-ledger
description: Write-ahead ledger for agent side effects, with an OWASP Agentic Top 10 posture scorer. Disclosure — records the arguments (up to 4000 chars: terminal commands, file contents, MCP args) and a 300-char result digest of every state-changing tool call in a local plaintext SQLite ledger under VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugin-data/agent-ledger/ that is never pruned; injects a warning listing this session's unconfirmed calls into the next turn's context; an optional policy engine (off by default; you add policy.json and set policy_mode) can refuse matching tool calls before they run; the optional posture_daily.py script, run from your own cron, sends a score summary to Telegram with the bot token you give it.

name: agent-log
description: Readable agent.log viewer in the desktop status bar — a live, colour-coded feed of API calls, tools, turns, fallbacks, warnings and errors, with per-call tokens/latency/cache, stats tables, and a single-dot alert for genuine non-self-healing faults. Follows app theme/language.

name: agent-mail-gateway
description: Email for your agents through a self-hosted Agent Mail Gateway: the agent-mail skill teaches reading, searching, replying and forwarding mail, attachments, sending and answering calendar invitations, how to react when the gateway's pre-send review or the operator's policies stop a message, and prompt-injection rules for email content. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only, no code, no mcp.json): you connect the gateway yourself as a remote MCP server in mcp_servers with your own key; the gateway enforces per-mailbox sender/recipient allow lists.

name: agent-run-debugger
description: Local-first evidence debugger for failed, stalled or expensive agent runs: import one explicitly selected trace and get a deterministic timeline, observed failure points, ranked hypotheses that cite their evidence, missing-evidence gaps and an inert replay of the recorded run. Disclosure — imports a trace file explicitly named by you or by the model through the rundebug_import tool and writes only under the active profile's plugin-data directory, with redaction before the store, the journal and exports; replay executes nothing (no subprocess, no network connection, no live database); no telemetry, no background capture, no stored credentials, no third-party network calls and no self-updater; the export command is operator-CLI-only and is not exposed through tool, slash or gateway routes.

name: agent-station
description: Read-only ViberVN Bot Desktop page for the focused chat: the main agent and its subagents, background commands and a Replay of file edits. Disclosure — its local dashboard routes serve the file-edit contents (Replay) and background-command output tails of the chat you view to the Desktop page; reads state.db read-only.

name: agent_memory_es
description: Self-owned long-term memory backed by the agent-memory-es service (Elasticsearch). Three agent tools — recall, retain, reflect — over episodic/ semantic/procedural tiers with hybrid BM25+kNN recall and server-enforced private/team/common visibility. Requires a running agent-memory-es instance. Disclosure — each user prompt (as a recall query), each user message and ViberVN Bot memory writes are sent to the agent-memory-es service at AMES_SERVICE_URL (default localhost:8123) with AMES_SERVICE_KEY; the model may store facts in shared team/common visibility tiers.

name: agentchat
description: AgentChat — peer-to-peer messaging for AI agents. Owns its own WebSocket; pokes the agent on inbound; the agent decides whether to reply. Send is a tool call, never automatic. Bundles the etiquette skill.

name: agentplaybooks-memory
description: Private AgentPlaybooks memory for ViberVN Bot: bounded keyword recall across personal and team sources, exact native memory-write mirroring, archive and history. Disclosure — keywords derived from each turn's query are sent to the configured AgentPlaybooks service for recall from your personal and configured team playbooks; explicit native memory writes are mirrored there. Defaults to agentplaybooks.ai over HTTPS; localhost HTTP is supported, and remote intranet HTTP requires an explicit opt-in that sends the API key unencrypted. Team and shared playbooks are configured explicitly: the agent can write, archive and permanently delete entries in configured team playbooks (shared playbooks are read-only), and teammates' entries are recalled into context.

name: agentplaybooks-tools
description: Connect AgentPlaybooks skills and hosted MCP/OpenAPI tools to ViberVN Bot, with guided setup, profile selection, permission diagnostics and an authenticated MCP check. Requires Node.js 20+ and @agentplaybooks/cli@0.7.0; the CLI is installed separately. Disclosure — skill-only; the separately installed apb CLI does the work. `apb vibervnbot setup --apply` restores complete skill trees into the chosen project and edits the selected ViberVN Bot profile's config.yaml to register those skills and a hosted playbook MCP endpoint. Local writes require --apply; setup also probes MCP initialization and tool listing using a scoped key from the process environment, without invoking tools. `doctor` checks profile credential variable names without exposing their values. Hosted operations contact agentplaybooks.ai (or an explicitly configured service); skill restore uses `apb login`, and `apb push --apply` uploads project configuration (secret references, not values).

name: agentvault
description: Search archived coding conversations and retrieve exact session revisions through the separately installed Agent Vault macOS app. Launches the app's existing MCP server through sh; reads the authorized archive through its local daemon. Vault handles storage-provider traffic. No bundled binaries, telemetry, credential-file reads, self-updater, or new background service. Disclosure — launches the separately installed Agent Vault app's own bundled Node MCP server (/Applications/Agent Vault.app or VAULT_APP_PATH) through sh with your VAULT_MCP_TOKEN binding token; that server code ships with the app, not in this repository. Its tools return archived conversations from Cursor, Codex, Claude Code and ViberVN Bot stored under ~/.vault (or VAULT_HOME) into the model's context, which is sent to your model provider. The app handles its own storage-provider traffic; the plugin adds no telemetry, network calls, credential-file reads or background service.

name: agentwalletapi
description: OpenClawCash managed EVM and Solana wallets for AI agents — thin bridge to the OpenClawCash agent API. Disclosure — payments plugin for the OpenClawCash custodial wallet service (openclawcash.com); the model can create wallets and send EVM/Solana transfers from wallets reachable by OPENCLAWCASH_AGENT_KEY with no ViberVN Bot confirmation prompt; tool arguments go to openclawcash.com, and wallet_create also sends OPENCLAWCASH_EXPORT_PASSPHRASE to that API.

name: agora
description: Self-driving multi-agent development team. Role-based workers (architect, developer, reviewer, tester, researcher, writer, devops) are each a real ViberVN Bot profile with its own SOUL.md and skills; they discuss and vote on decisions, and the adopted conclusion is executed by the same team. A "leader" profile chairs the discussions and a heartbeat cron wakes it to assess state, unblock workers and plan the next phase. Discussion and execution share one board: a motion is a sub-task of a per-project team channel task, speech and votes are `[agora:msg]` comments, the conclusion is written to task.result, and an adopted conclusion becomes execution tasks parented to the motion so context reaches workers through ViberVN Bot' own parent handoff. Ships 20 tools, 3 kanban lifecycle hooks, a dashboard tab and an `vibervnbot agora` CLI; installing writes nothing — the three bundled skills are deployed by an explicit `vibervnbot agora setup`. Disclosure — creates a ViberVN Bot profile per worker by asking core to provision it (`vibervnbot profile create --clone`, which copies config.yaml and .env into the new profile as owner-only files, never symlinks to the real credentials); spawns `vibervnbot -p <profile> chat -Q -q` subprocesses to speak in discussions and to run dispatched tasks, which execute as full agents with that profile's toolset, including terminal and file writes inside the project workdir. Those subprocesses receive `--yolo --accept-hooks` ONLY when the project opted in via `agora_start_project(allow_unattended=True)`; the default is off, so a freshly installed team can read, discuss and plan but its flagged writes and shell commands fail closed. Also reads and writes the kanban database (tasks, task_comments, task_events, task_runs, task_links) restricted to its own project boards, including a persistent team-channel task pinned in `scheduled` status, and deletes a project's own tasks when it stops or completes; registers one recurring cron job and writes its runner script to VIBERVNBOT_HOME/scripts/leader_heartbeat.sh; writes AGENTS.md into the configured project workdir; deploys three bundled skills into VIBERVNBOT_HOME/skills/collaboration/; and serves a dashboard tab plus REST routes through the ViberVN Bot dashboard. No network egress of its own — model calls happen inside the spawned ViberVN Bot subprocesses under the operator's own provider credentials.

name: ai-subscriptions
description: Your AI subscriptions and token usage in ViberVN Bot Desktop. A page with Overview, Usage and Plans tabs, plus a status-bar chip where you pick which subscriptions to keep. Quota comes from ViberVN Bot's own model.options and usage.bars RPCs; the page polls ViberVN Bot' cached windows (ViberVN Bot refreshes them in its own background threads) and only its Refresh button asks for an explicit refresh; token usage covers ViberVN Bot, Claude Code and the Grok CLI, clicking a day shows that day's per-source, per-model and hourly breakdown, and measured tokens per second are shown per model, per day and overall. Disclosure: read-only reads outside the plugin's data - ViberVN Bot state.db and models_dev_cache.json, ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl and ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl plus ~/.grok/sessions/*/*/summary.json (token counts only). No credential, .env or auth.json reads, no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.

name: ai-usage-tracker
description: Live subscription-quota windows for every AI provider ViberVN Bot can route to, as a desktop page plus a status-bar chip, with a per-profile picker — Codex, Claude, Copilot, OpenCode Go/Zen, Z.AI, Kimi, MiniMax, OpenRouter, DeepSeek.

name: aichipmunk
description: Pairs this machine's ViberVN Bot bots with the AI Chipmunk mobile app from inside ViberVN Bot Desktop — pick a bot, get the reachable host, profile and API key as a scannable code. Registers a `vibervnbot aichipmunk` CLI command, a desktop page and a dashboard API; no tools or hooks. Disclosure — on an explicit confirmed "Switch to Tailscale" it adds a persistent tailscale serve handler putting the API server's own port (plain HTTP inside the tailnet, API_SERVER_KEY auth) onto the tailnet; on a machine with no Tailscale CLI it instead runs vibervnbot config set platforms.api_server.host <tailnet IP> on the owning profile and restarts that gateway; reads API_SERVER_KEY from every profile's .env on this machine on each status poll (masked in lists, the full key only in the pairing link and QR returned to an authenticated dashboard caller, which may be the phone over a published dashboard); shells out to the tailscale and vibervnbot CLIs and probes only this machine's own /health; no third-party network calls.

name: aihubmix
description: AIHubMix — unified OpenAI-compatible access to 400+ models; /model picker filtered to tool-capable routes.

name: airlock
description: Guardrails that follow what a conversation has read. Once a session reads untrusted content (a web page, a browser snapshot, an MCP or third-party plugin's output, a customer's message), airlock seals it: messages to anyone but the owner, network writes, pushes and deploys, memory, skill and cron writes, browser input, URLs that could carry data out and code that reaches the network go through ViberVN Bot's own approval gate. Walls hold in every session: credential paths and secret files, the guard's own files and ViberVN Bot's config, shell startup files, other profiles, commands that switch approvals off. Shell commands are read the way the shell reads them, so a command that computes or hides what it runs (eval, base64 | sh, $G push, wildcards, write-then-run) is refused until written in clear. Subagents inherit the seal. It also catches an injection by its signature: recognized secrets never leave in a call; a private marker in the agent's context locks the session if it shows up in a tool call; a send to an address the untrusted content named is blocked; repeated refusals lock the session; lookalike Unicode in commands is refused. Plugin and MCP tools nobody admitted need approval. Observe mode, stop switch, `vibervnbot airlock check|demo|log`. Tested on a corpus of 251 attacks and everyday commands, and end to end in the official image. Disclosure — hooks only (pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, pre_llm_call, subagent_start, on_session_reset, post_approval_response), no tools. No network, no LLM call, runs no command. Reads the profile's config.yaml (home channels, approvals mode) and its own policy file (<VIBERVNBOT_HOME>/airlock.yaml); lists directories to expand wildcards in commands it checks. Writes under plugin-data/airlock: a journal of decisions, taints and approvals that includes tool arguments, truncated (journal.args: none leaves them out), the taint state and the stop switch. When nobody can approve (--yolo, approvals.mode: off, cron set to approve) it blocks instead of letting ViberVN Bot auto-approve (policy approvals_off: follow restores ViberVN Bot's behaviour). Install scan: caution, because the default policy and the shell reader name the patterns airlock guards against (startup files, crontab, credential commands, exfiltration shapes).

name: aistupidlevel
description: AI Stupid Level Smart Router — OpenAI-compatible; routing modes such as auto-tooling send each request to the model currently scoring best on continuously re-run benchmarks, called with your own provider keys. Disclosure — sends your prompts, tool definitions, tool results and ASL_ROUTER_KEY to aistupidlevel.info (S.C. Studio Platforms S.R.L.), which forwards each request to the AI provider it routes to using the provider keys you store on your AI Stupid Level account; model usage is billed to your provider accounts, and prompts are logged only if you enable logging for a key.

name: alans-way
description: Idle check-ins from the primary bot of a ViberVN Bot gateway on a Linux machine or a macOS guest VM: when the bound Telegram chat has been quiet for two hours, during 08:00-22:00 in the user's timezone, the bot checks in once (does one safe step and reports it, suggests one, or asks one question), backing off when unanswered. The model tool can only make check-ins quieter; more often, resume and wider hours are operator-only via /proactivity or the CLI. After install, the workspace-setup skill walks the agent through setting up Alan's Workspace (a separate desktop app for the user's computer: macOS or Windows) and Tailscale; desktop input goes only through ViberVN Bot's approval-gated computer_use tool. Disclosure — once the gateway connects Telegram, a background thread checks every 60 seconds. When the bound Telegram DM has been quiet (2 h by default, doubling per unanswered check-in, 08:00-22:00 user time), it injects an internal user-role prompt into that chat (needs plugins.entries.alans-way.allow_gateway_injection, which setup sets), so the bot runs a turn on its own and may take one "safe, reversible" step; the user still approves tool calls in Telegram. Its pre_llm_call/post_llm_call hooks see every session's turns and store the bound chat's activity timestamps in plugin state; optional cross-bot export adds the separate storage disclosed below. On first load it reads $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/companion/proactivity/proactivity.sqlite3 once, read-only. The plugin itself makes no network calls. The workspace-setup skill has the agent fetch this repo at the catalog pin into ~/alans-way-agents (or reuse a clean clone there) and hand a JSON setup plan to the human in Alan's Workspace. The app runs setup.sh through an external SSH process outside the gateway, checks the exact repoRef and desktopRef and rejects tracked checkout changes; the agent must never run setup or even --verify in its gateway terminal or bypass the lifecycle guard. Windows guests require the human's external Git Bash shell. The human pastes the app's output for review. The external setup does the following. (1) Installs long-running services (Alan's Tools: a managed Chrome/Chromium on a loopback-only debugging port, the first free port from 9223 up, plus a browser broker and an optional availability watcher): systemd units vibervnbot-alans-way-chromium, -browser and mac-watch with loginctl enable-linger where systemd is running; supervisord programs alans-way-chromium, alans-way-browser and alans-way-mac-watch, written to a conf.d file, where it is not (VM images and containers); a KeepAlive LaunchAgent on a macOS guest; logon Scheduled Tasks on Windows. When no X display is running it also installs and runs Xvfb on :99 (unit vibervnbot-alans-way-xvfb or program alans-way-xvfb, -nolisten tcp). (2) Installs packages when they are missing, only as root or with passwordless sudo, through apt, dnf or yum: Google Chrome stable (the current .deb downloaded from dl.google.com on amd64 apt hosts, which also adds Google's apt repository, so the host keeps taking Chrome updates from Google), else the distro chromium package, else Playwright 1.49.1 Chromium through npx (root only); and xvfb. It only warns, and installs nothing, for xdotool, scrot, at-spi2-core and python3-gi, which the VM desktop path needs. (3) Appends the user's computer's public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (administrators_authorized_keys on a Windows admin account) with a from= restriction to the Tailscale ranges 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48, rewriting an existing unrestricted line for the same key; pins its host key in known_hosts and adds a ControlMaster block to ~/.ssh/config for Tailscale hosts only (with a tailscale nc ProxyCommand when Tailscale runs in userspace-networking mode). (4) Adds a TimeoutStartSec=180 drop-in to the vibervnbot-gateway unit. ViberVN Bot refuses plugin file changes while a gateway is running, so setup drain-stops that profile's gateway (SIGUSR1 under supervisord, else systemctl stop or vibervnbot gateway stop), replays the refused plugin install or update, and starts it again. With --restart it restarts the gateway only if setup changed something the gateway loads (or an earlier restart never happened), detached about ten seconds after printing its summary: by SIGUSR1 drain under supervisord, else a transient systemd-run timer or vibervnbot gateway restart. (5) For the main profile and every profile with its own Telegram bot, writes a managed mcp_servers.workspace_browser block with connect_timeout: 25 seconds (removing other entries that run this router, with a backup; a re-run keeps the computer address and OS it already holds, and --mac-ssh none removes them), turns off the built-in browser toolset for Telegram and cron (--keep-browser only skips disabling it; it does not re-enable a previously disabled toolset), turns computer_use on for Telegram and cron, and sets computer_use.backend to alans-way-computer when it installed or found that provider (under the skill's --skip-plugin flow it only warns and prints the config command). It reads each profile's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN only to derive the numeric bot id. It warns, and changes nothing, when a copy of the workspace-operations skill in a profile's skills directory shadows the plugin's. The workspace router reaches the user's computer over SSH on their tailnet; on the user's computer it calls the local API of Alan's Workspace on 127.0.0.1 with that app's bearer token. The skill's moved-VM checklist has the agent read the app's preferences.json on the user's computer over the same SSH path and tell the human where the VNC password lives without pasting it. The Alan's Workspace setup page has the human run the alans-way connect script from its main branch on their own computer, and the agent may install Tailscale with its official install script. The manual --allow-desktop-actions setup flag, which the skill offers but never adds itself, adds cua:*:background entries to command_allowlist. On a ViberVN Bot without the computer-use provider API, including 0.21.5, it also exposes workspace_computer_action, which drives the user's desktop, Terminal included, with no approval. The repo also holds bootstrap-orgo.sh and migrate.sh, which the plugin, setup.sh and the skills never run: a user runs them by hand to provision a fresh supervisord Linux computer (it fetches the ViberVN Bot and Tailscale installers over HTTPS, pipes setup.sh from this repo's main branch into bash unless --repo-ref is given, installs openssh-server if absent, writes supervisord programs, and POSTs the Tailscale login URL with a shared secret to a --callback URL when one is given) or to copy ~/.vibervnbot, including .env, auth.json and state.db, to another host over SSH (it also looks up each profile's bot username at api.telegram.org with that profile's bot token). Since 0.21.0, every enabled profile also gets a default-on Telegram texting voice: an additional pre_llm_call hook reads that profile's voice mode and adds a tone note to Telegram turns, and transform_llm_output can remove a known leading assistant opener from the final Telegram reply. Messages containing backticks, quotes, indentation or silence markers are left unchanged by that polish. /tone texting|default|status and vibervnbot tone store the mode under voice in ViberVN Bot plugin state; setup.sh --tone applies it to each configured profile. It layers over the user's persona without writing SOUL.md or agent.system_prompt. Check-ins now name one concrete open thread. /proactivity now requests one immediately from the bound chat even when paused or outside active hours, without changing the settings or unanswered-check-in count. Morning briefs are off by default: /proactivity brief on (or the operator CLI) enables one daily internal user-role prompt near active_start, with 0-20 minutes of jitter, at most two hours late and skipped after recent user activity. It asks the model to consult calendar and email read-only if those tools exist. The existing proactivity tool may disable the brief but cannot enable it; settings.morning_brief and last_brief_date are stored in the existing idle plugin state. The workspace router adds a commit object to the existing browser open/action tools for purchases, bookings, sends, posts, submissions, deletions and account changes. It checks control names, selectors, refs, action-looking URLs, batches, scripts, keys and dialogs against page state; missing page knowledge needs a snapshot or explicit commit. Shared commit-name patterns allow benign Buy it again, Book a demo and Subscribe & Save labels without excusing other commit-bearing words. Tax schedule names are treated as benign labels without exempting one-on-one bookings from approval. It asks through MCP elicitation (60-second default wait, configurable with VIBERVNBOT_ROUTER_APPROVAL_MS), refuses unavailable, declined, timed-out or stale approvals, drops agent-supplied approval receipts and adds a single-use receipt bound to the approved tab and epoch. An approved commit is never replayed after a lost connection or host change. It appends commit decisions to commit-decisions.jsonl beside the mac-watch state file, creating the log with mode 0600: timestamp, bot id, page origin, decision and any supplied kind, summary, amount, currency and counterparty, or the detected target. Page/control/challenge and pending-approval state is held in memory. The same two skills now prefer ViberVN Bot web_search/web_extract for plain lookups and the user's computer for interactive search, hand CAPTCHAs to the human, poll at most every 30 seconds for up to 30 minutes, and switch sources after two challenges in ten minutes. The router stops remembering challenge pages for failover and reports changed tab ids in result metadata. The operations skill covers the app's automatic takeover after its grace period; CAPTCHA and recording holds and Take-back cooldowns still keep the bot out. It asks the agent to save only lasting general facts and preferences to memory; procedures belong in skills and project/task records in the user's chosen file or tracker, asking where if none is chosen. Existing memory is not migrated or deleted, and live tab state is never saved there. The setup skill pins the companion app source to f110115ff23367e4e21eeaf00e658a8706369652 and adds a long-chat reference: report effective compression and summary routing read-only, then only with explicit consent for each profile enable compression.proactive_prune_tokens at 48000, with 8000-character eligibility and 4096-token minimum reclaim, using the profile-scoped config CLI and keeping custom values, micro_compact and summary routing. This writes the approved profile's config.yaml and records prior values outside the repo for undo; setup.sh does not run it. A weekly time-saved report is a user-created ViberVN Bot cron recipe, not an installed job. setup.sh --verify now checks the running service manager, display, SSH ProxyCommand and managed browser's loopback /json/version endpoint, and reports noVNC reachability from its actual bind address. Manual supervisord restart guidance drains with USR1 first. The repo also adds scripts/voice_eval.py, user-run only: it sends fixed fictional scenarios and replies to Anthropic models through the SDK or claude -p for scoring and optionally writes a JSON result; the plugin, setup and skills never run it. Since 0.21.5, the plugin registers two more bundled skills, web-errands and integrations, with no new tools, hooks, commands or required environment variables. web-errands is guidance for shopping, booking, applications, filings, cancellations and claims in the workspace browser: every purchase, booking, send, submission and deletion still goes through the commit approval gate described above, CAPTCHA, sign-in and card-entry walls go back to the human, and card numbers are never stored. It has the agent record each application's company, role, date, posting URL and confirmation in the user's chosen project/task record, asking where if none is chosen. For a price, restock or status watch the user asks for or explicitly accepts, it has the agent create a ViberVN Bot cron job with ViberVN Bot's cronjob_manage tool (or ask the operator), polling no more often than every 10 minutes and stopping after three consecutive failures; cron runs cannot answer approvals, so a watch that reaches its target stages the result for the user. Watches use attach_to_session: true with no deliver override and continuity: true; each check is a fresh session, uses its prior completed output as a baseline and replies [SILENT] unless something meaningful changed, failed or reached its target. An optional safe read-only deterministic monitor URL or script can skip the model and delivery on unchanged output; probe errors still need reporting/backoff. Cron cannot pause/remove itself unless the operator enabled cron.allow_agent_scheduling. In-chat monitoring is a separate user-entered /heartbeat every command, one per conversation replacing the previous one; it runs only while idle with the chat process/gateway alive, costs a model turn per check and needs /heartbeat clear from the user. The integrations skill has the agent check that an account is connected, with a small read, before promising a task that needs it, and reuses ViberVN Bot's Google Workspace, Himalaya, Home Assistant, Honcho and X routes first. The Google route uses ViberVN Bot's own setup, whose fixed scope list includes write access; the skill says so and stops if the user declines. Only after the user agrees in chat does it guide an install: a ViberVN Bot catalog plugin (Home Assistant or Honcho), a separately reviewed Himalaya v1.2.0 binary, rclone v1.75.2 (the release zip from downloads.rclone.org, checked against that release's SHA256SUMS before extraction) or Taskwarrior 3.5.0 (a source build of upstream commit 3419d5ba1e6a780fbbb0a8d68d8fd31e675c1bf8 cloned from GitHub, after checking the CMake and Rust versions and asking before changing any toolchain), the last two into versioned directories under ~/.local/share/alans-tools/. Secrets are entered by the human in a private terminal outside the agent session, never in Telegram; where a recipe needs a secret in the agent's terminal (a mail credential, RCLONE_CONFIG_PASS), it explains the grant and adds only that variable to the profile's terminal.env_passthrough. The recipes keep rclone.conf (mode 0600) and Taskwarrior's taskrc and data under the profile's VIBERVNBOT_HOME/integrations. Scheduled reads are read-only cron jobs with a profile-local failure-count file, and pausing goes through the owner conversation or an explicitly authorized vibervnbot cron pause. API writes (send, post, delete, share) need fresh explicit approval in the live conversation, and a declined, timed-out or unavailable browser commit is never completed through another tool. Mastodon is not bundled: its recipe is human-run documentation in this repo (docs/integrations/mastodon.md) that the plugin and skills never run. None of this runs at plugin load or from setup.sh. Telegram replies, check-ins and briefs share one status-first style: concrete status, evidence or caveat, plain limits, and no tool names, file paths, scripts or job and session IDs in user-facing text unless asked. Prices, availability and policies must come from a page read this turn or be labeled unconfirmed. Multi-step browser work continues in short chunks until done or blocked, with one short start line and one-line updates only at milestones, routed-around failures or noticeable waits; routine reads, actions and transitions stay quiet, a new mid-task message is acknowledged and folded in, and ViberVN Bot's clarify buttons may be used for decisions the user owns, never for approvals; a whole checkout batch still sits under one commit. For a message of 200 characters or fewer that is wholly a recap request, greeting, thanks or acknowledgment, the voice hook appends a three-sentence limit; the check reads only the current message, with no model call, history or network. The check-in menu now ends with asking about a decision the user owns. The operations skill adds tab hygiene: the agent closes finished tabs it owns with the existing close tool, never another bot's or the user's and never one with a pending handback or recording hold. The router adds requestingBotId to tab-list replies and forwards a reply over 4 MiB unchanged, without that decoration, writing a content-free line to stderr. The skill also tells the agent to report installed versions by running vibervnbot --version, reading the plugin's install metadata, running local git describe and rev-parse on the Alan's Tools checkout, and calling the app's existing status tool. setup.sh --bind now also makes the bound DM ViberVN Bot's Telegram home by running vibervnbot -p PROFILE config set for TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL and TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID (30-second limit each; on failure it warns to send /sethome); it loads on gateway restart. setup.sh --verify exits 0 for a complete local audit, 1 for failed required checks and 2 for a partial install (warnings, or skipped browser or services). The setup skill's checkout step now initializes ~/alans-way-agents if absent and fetches the pin (depth 1) from the repo's GitHub origin, or reuses a clean clone there after two read-only local git helpers (5-second limit) confirm one recorded and effective origin URL naming this repo; for file and direct Git installs it uses the installer-recorded revision, and it never falls back to a tag when that record is invalid. Its computer-use API probe separates an absent API from a failed or timed-out probe and ends the probe's process group or tree on timeout. The setup skill also offers, each only after an explicit answer, with readback and a remembered-choice marker in the profile's config: one grouped autonomy choice for display.busy_input_mode: steer and agent.intent_ack_continuation: true, for every platform in that profile after restart. It reads effective values, including defaults, proposes changes only from stock interrupt/auto and preserves deliberate choices, custom or unknown values and unreadable config. General setup/proactivity consent is insufficient; an explicit no preserves both settings, silence writes nothing. Both keys are read back, including unchanged keys, before writing and reading back skills.config.workspace-setup.autonomy_choice as chosen or keep-current. Failed writes/readbacks leave the marker untouched; it records the answer only and never restores settings. Legacy busy_input_choice: keep-interrupt skips only the busy key; unknown legacy state is reported and skipped. agent.verify_on_stop is left alone unless the coding user requests stricter checks and one grouped Telegram question covering platforms.telegram.typing_indicator, display.platforms.telegram.interim_assistant_messages, tool_progress, notifications, long_running_notifications and busy_steer_ack_enabled, platforms.telegram.reactions, display.memory_notifications (hides the Memory updated and Self-improvement review notices on every platform in that profile), cron.wrap_response (profile-wide: removes scheduled-message headers, job IDs and footers for all delivery targets) and, as a separate city-confirmed question, timezone. Markers written through the same CLI are skills.config.workspace-setup.autonomy_choice and telegram_feel_choice; the former busy_input_choice is read but no longer written; a legacy busy_steer_ack_choice marker is only read, never written. Silence and non-interactive runs write nothing, and neither setup script writes any of these keys. When the VNC viewer binds loopback only, the skill can, with explicit consent, have the human run a temporary SSH forward to the computer's loopback (local port 16080, ends after 30 minutes) and verify it with curl from that computer. For a manual or file install, SAFE requires no scanner confirmation; setup and dependency consent remain separate. A later CAUTION revision needs review and explicit consent to the exact tree before retrying vibervnbot plugins install with --ref SHA --enable --force; --enable alone does not confirm a warning, and --force confirms CAUTION and can replace an install but cannot override DANGEROUS. ViberVN Bot's unmodified scanner reports SAFE for this plugin: 0 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM (python_subprocess: the two git helpers in skills/workspace-setup/SKILL.md) and 3 LOW (hardcoded_ip_port: the loopback forward examples in the same file). This pin also extends the existing texting-note and minimal final-opener polish to public session source tags desktop, tui and bot_room, alongside Telegram; CLI, cron, webhook and API-server sources keep their default voice. A tone-independent pre_llm_call task note asks the agent to track and verify mini goals with ViberVN Bot's todo tool or working context, continue independent authorized work through completion, recheck historical blockers against newer messages and verify every requested criterion with each item's own source before replying. It requests a short start line and milestone-only updates, keeps routine work quiet and preserves questions, approvals, failures and honest completion. Recap replies are capped at three sentences total including any detail offer. Follow-up cron jobs are saved only after the user asks or says yes, attached to this chat with attach_to_session: true and no deliver override; no later message may be promised without a saved job. A not-yet reply allows one offer at a named local time, with no saved repeat until consent, and jobs are removed when their reason ends. /goal is suggested once for a big multi-step job, not small asks. Fixed ViberVN Bot progress/error/approval messages are unchanged. Scripted tool conversations prove hook delivery; consistent real-model quiet behavior is unverified. Browser guidance starts normal work in the user's Workspace even while they are away; host vm is for explicit VM requests or router-reported outages, never login/CAPTCHA/approval errors. Existing VM tasks finish there when the computer returns; no third-tier browser is substituted. Reasoned human handbacks hold VM tabs as well as computer tabs for up to 30 minutes until Give back; a chat reply alone cannot bypass awaiting_human. Resume uses the host, tab ID and fresh epoch from one reply. The human-only Move button can carry URL/scroll and chosen drafts; cookies move only when a restore is reported, while passwords, uploads and in-memory state stay behind, and the agent has no move tool. Router changes bind approvals to exact observed page targets, reject missing/malformed action success receipts, bound recovery and owned-child shutdown, and project agent-facing replies without exposing internal approval proof. The router never replays a sent write after connector retry, timeout or host change, including writes before the first response; only reads and unsent calls can replay within their original remaining budget. Cancellation is forwarded and stale-host checks reject queued desktop input before sending it; uncertainty requires checking the outcome before any repeat. Browser and desktop replies add a content-free diagnostic, on stderr and appended to the profile's logs/workspace-router.log, with fixed tool name, serving host, default/request/fallback selection and reason, and elapsed time; it contains no URLs or page/task content. Idle direct SSH probes can discover a recovered computer sooner without moving an active VM task. Cross-bot proactivity adds the cross_bot_ask tool and pre_tool_call/on_session_end hooks; no middleware, required secrets or direct network destinations are added. Optional cross-bot proactivity is off by default, configured with the same explicit absolute shared root and designated primary in each participating profile, then enrolled per bot through /proactivity cross on (activation in a running gateway needs a restart). Only completed user/final-assistant exchanges from each enrolled bot's bound owner Telegram DM are exported: at most four recent exchanges and 2 KiB per digest, expiring after 24 hours per exchange. There is no historical backfill or export of groups, other chats, attachments, reasoning, tool history, cron, check-ins, briefs, child or imported turns. Exchanges that appear to contain credentials or payment details, or match operator redact terms, are skipped entirely before truncation; sanitization cannot detect every secret. Only the designated primary receives other enabled profiles' fresh digests during permitted check-ins, including user-requested /proactivity now; its own digest is excluded and exports are JSON-escaped as untrusted observations, bounded to 32 KiB across 16 profiles. Ordinary turns receive no digests or dispatch permit; separately consented helper results can arrive there as disclosed below. Briefs and cron receive neither. The primary may automatically schedule one read_only or draft_only cross_bot_ask with fresh target evidence per check-in into another enrolled bot's existing bound DM; replies appear there with primary attribution, and only separately consented short outcomes can return to the primary. The receiver needs its own gateway-injection permission and verified routing, observes pause/hours/busy settings, and starts no spontaneous secondary check-ins. Queued asks are at most 800 characters, expire after two hours and are deleted before injection; sent means scheduled, not delivered or completed, with no replay, delivery-receipt store or result polling. Result sharing is separately off by default, including for existing cross-bot users: /proactivity cross results on must be chosen in both bound owner DMs. Only future asks can return a sanitized Done/Blocked summary of at most 280 UTF-8 bytes, correlated to one ask, with the same two-hour expiry measured from ask creation. The private shared results.json stores up to 64 pending/running/completed records with profile identities, enrollment generations, ask IDs, timestamps, prompt/session-correlation hashes, status and summary. Results are consumed once before exposure at the primary's next ordinary owner turn or permitted check-in, as untrusted helper reports rather than independently verified facts. There is no wake, retry or delivery guarantee; a crash or helper restart can lose an outcome. /proactivity cross results off purges pending outcomes; cross off also revokes the choice. Copied outcomes can persist in chat/provider context after expiry or opt-out. Attempts are limited to four per rolling day gateway-wide, two per target and 60-minute target spacing. The plugin-owned POSIX shared directory uses mode 0700 and files 0600: digests and queued bodies, persistent enrollment/generation and eligibility/heartbeat records, body-free turn/attempt hashes retained for 48 hours, one-use check-in permits and imported-session locks expiring within 30 minutes. Session locks contain the exact session key and ask ID and survive restart until session end, expiry or opt-out. Pruning runs on activated startup, before store access and every 60 seconds while connected; offline expired files can remain until an activated profile prunes them. Dormant profiles do no cross-bot store access. /proactivity cross off immediately stops sharing, receiving and dispatch and purges that profile's digest, permits, locks and pending asks; body-free records remain until expiry and scheduler roles revert on restart. Only the operator can enable or expand sharing; the model may disable it. Launch-gateway profile routing policy is read through public configuration/home-scope APIs; no ViberVN Bot session DB or credential store is read for export. Imported sessions block terminal/code, desktop actions, delegation, messaging, scheduling, further cross-bot asks and unknown connectors; reviewed reads/drafting and existing gated browser actions remain allowed. Browser approval, CAPTCHA and ownership gates still apply; this is not universal read-only enforcement. Copied context goes through the configured model provider and target Telegram delivery and may remain in ViberVN Bot history, API-content sidecars, compaction and memory-provider records, including Honcho when configured, and model-provider retention after expiry or opt-out. The instruction not to save other bots' excerpts is model policy, not enforced deletion; the plugin performs no memory-provider writes. No new direct network endpoint or telemetry is introduced. Optional integrations use the user's selected Google Workspace API, IMAP/SMTP mail service, Home Assistant instance, Honcho API, X API or rclone cloud/WebDAV/S3 endpoint; browser errands contact user-selected sites. Honcho can receive conversation turns, derived conclusions, peer/session IDs and version/OS/plugin headers. Native tools retain their own profile-scoped credentials, including Google client/token/pending OAuth files and encrypted rclone provider tokens; the plugin does not create a separate credential store. Setup downloads also reach GitHub/raw.githubusercontent.com, the official Tailscale installer, configured distro package repositories and the npm/Playwright distribution, in addition to Google and rclone downloads already disclosed.

name: alans-way-computer
description: Computer-use provider for ViberVN Bot: the stock computer_use tool drives desktop apps on the user's computer through the Alan's Workspace app, and on the VM's own desktop when the computer is offline. Needs the Alan's Way Plugin's workspace setup. Select it with computer_use.backend: alans-way-computer (the Alan's Way Plugin's setup.sh sets this when it installs the provider; in the catalog flow it prints the command). Disclosure — starts the workspace router from the profile's mcp_servers.workspace_browser block (command and args from config.yaml, with a filtered environment plus VIBERVNBOT_WORKSPACE_ALLOW_DESKTOP_ACTIONS=1, which lets this private router child serve desktop input) as a long-running node child per session. The filtered environment passes PATH, HOME, locale and OS basics, plus DISPLAY, XAUTHORITY and DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS so the router's VM-desktop fallback finds the X display and session bus, plus VIBERVNBOT_HOME set to the bound profile's home, under which the router appends a content-free serving log to logs/workspace-router.log; no keys or tokens. It talks to the router over stdio (app lists, element trees, screenshots and input actions). The router reaches the user's computer over SSH on the user's tailnet and falls back to the VM's desktop, where it uses xdotool, a screenshot tool and the AT-SPI accessibility bus if they are installed (the provider installs none of them). On the user's Mac the provider can bring the target app to the front when the model asks for it (focus_app with raise_window, or an input action with delivery_mode foreground), and the Alan's Workspace host does so only after the user has been idle for at least 2 seconds; focus_app can also launch a named app, or open a document or folder by absolute path in its app (the host refuses app bundles, executables, scripts and off-limits apps). Every input action still goes through ViberVN Bot's computer_use approval gate, with raising and foreground input under their own approval scopes (the cua:<action>:background entries in command_allowlist that the Alan's Way Plugin's --allow-desktop-actions adds skip the prompt for background input, focus_app and launches, not for raising or foreground input). The provider itself makes no network calls. On ViberVN Bot 0.21.5, which has no provider API, it installs and does nothing. Since 0.21.0, captures keep element numbers stable across action replies on Mac and Windows, fold in changed controls and report removed numbers; a truncated list never treats unseen controls as removed. Linux keeps the whole-tree generation guard, so capture again before acting by number after a change. Action replies describe nearby changes and can mark the effect confirmed. Default som captures skip the screenshot call entirely when finite snapshot window geometry proves named controls cover at least 35%; older snapshots without geometry still fetch a screenshot to measure coverage and may omit it from the model; mode vision explicitly includes it and mode ax requests no screenshot. Replies identify the coordinate space and explain locked screens, missing permissions, unreadable or cut trees, hung apps and uncertain outcomes before a retry. Captures request generation-based snapshot deltas, validate them against the held tree and retry once for a full list on invalid or mismatched deltas; older apps may return full or unchanged lists. Once a reply identifies a window, later captures, screenshots and input stay bound to that window; capture(window_id=...) selects another. Mismatched window replies clear the target and require a fresh capture. Desktop actions carry expect_host from the observed host so a routing switch refuses input before dispatch; app IDs and element numbers must be reacquired after a switch. Element trees, generation, bound window ID, screenshots' geometry and host OS are session memory, with no new persistent provider state, tools, hooks, middleware, required environment variables or direct network destinations. ViberVN Bot's unmodified CI-pinned scanner reports SAFE: 0 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM (python_subprocess: the long-running router Popen in __init__.py and its bounded 40-second --probe subprocess) and 0 LOW. Browser commit approvals are separate from this provider's unchanged computer_use approval gate.

name: alice-voice
description: Private Yandex Alice voice input for ViberVN Bot, with replies in Telegram. Disclosure — off until you set enabled: true and allow_gateway_injection: true; then, while the Telegram gateway is connected, it listens on 127.0.0.1 (port 8788 by default) for webhooks forwarded by your own HTTPS reverse proxy. The secret URL path (ALICE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) is the only authentication: Yandex request signatures are not checked, and the skill and account IDs in the request can be forged by anyone who has the URL. Each accepted request becomes a user message in one fixed Telegram DM session and runs with that session's tools; approvals stay in Telegram and slash commands are refused. Leaving owner_user_id empty accepts any Alice account presenting the URL.

name: ample
description: Ample (ample.computer) as native tools: deploy the websites and web apps ViberVN Bot builds to public HTTPS URLs, release changes to the same URLs, read build and runtime logs, list and delete apps; bundled skill ample:web-apps. Disclosure — maintained by Ample, the hosting service it deploys to; talks to Ample's API (https://api.ample.computer); on first use downloads the pinned Ample CLI 0.1.36 from Ample's release server (https://get.ample.computer/releases/0.1.36/, SHA-256 checked, never self-updated; cli_path uses your own binary instead) and runs it as a subprocess with an allowlisted environment and its crash reports off; ample_deploy uploads the folder it is given (home, ViberVN Bot home and credential directories refused) and writes ample.toml and .ample/ into it; with no AMPLE_CLIENT_ID/AMPLE_CLIENT_SECRET or AMPLE_TOKEN set, the first deploy signs up for a free Ample account (deleted after two days unless claimed) and saves its credential in ViberVN Bot's .env. A pre_tool_call hook sends every delete (scoped to that app) and the first publish of each folder to ViberVN Bot's approval gate; only folders the user has published, recorded in plugin state, skip it. No telemetry, no background processes.

name: anatomy-museum
description: Native Anatomy community gallery with search, local favorites and explicit sandboxed standalone playback. Disclosure — when opened it fetches gallery metadata and thumbnails from a third-party GitHub repository (wheresryan22/anatomy-community, resolved at runtime from its mutable previews branch via api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com). "Open figure in ViberVN Bot" downloads that community figure's HTML and runs its JavaScript inside the Desktop SDK sandbox (opaque origin, scripts only), and "Browse Ryan's website" embeds skills.wheresryan.sh the same way. Favorites and filters stay in Desktop-local plugin storage; no credentials or ViberVN Bot data are sent.

name: ando-platform
description: Connect a ViberVN Bot agent through an existing Ando invitation and receive authorized messages. Disclosure — connects outbound to Ando (mcp.ando.so, api.ando.so, realtime.ando.so) with an agent API key stored at $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/ando/connection.json (mode 600); Ando messages from the connecting member (or members the operator explicitly allowlists) start ViberVN Bot turns and the final reply, with any files it attaches, is posted back to Ando; message attachments are uploaded and downloaded through short-lived single-use links Ando issues (up to 20 MB each; received files are cached in the profile's ViberVN Bot cache); vibervnbot ando connect edits gateway.platforms.ando in config.yaml.

name: android-emulator
description: Control a headless Android emulator from ViberVN Bot — live sidebar, app management, GPS/battery/network simulation, and ADB tools. Emulator host is Linux. Disclosure — requires a pre-installed Android SDK under ~/Android/Sdk; runs adb, emulator, avdmanager and sdkmanager on the host, and the dashboard's Create AVD action downloads Android system images from Google via sdkmanager. emu_shell runs arbitrary commands inside the emulator; emu_install/emu_push copy host files into it.

name: antenna
description: Signed messaging with paired ViberVN Bot and OpenClaw agents, with receiver-controlled live and opt-in non-YOLO headless delivery. Disclosure — runs a loopback-only Node receiver when listen_port is set (you expose only its HTTPS receive route); messages from paired peers become agent turns in the sessions you approve and may cause tool use, and opt-in background delivery runs them in non-YOLO sessions only; smart scanning sends message text through your configured provider; ClawReef Public Groups use a plaintext relay that ClawReef can read; identity keys, peer credentials, holds and receipts live in the profile's plugin-data/antenna (0700/0600) and backups contain credentials; policy and storage commands rewrite config.yaml (comments and formatting are lost).

name: antigravity-agy
description: Run ViberVN Bot on a Google Antigravity subscription through the official agy CLI, with agy as the model only: a generated custom agent removes agy's built-in tools, ViberVN Bot tools are exposed through an inventory-only MCP server with native function calling, and every tool call is handed back to ViberVN Bot. Fails closed on any non-ViberVN Bot tool step or silent agent fallback; pre-warms agy for fast tool loops. Disclosure — routes inference through Google's official agy CLI and counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to; the plugin never reads, copies or links agy's credential files. agy runs in your real HOME with the gateway's environment; by default the plugin moves the agy conversation records created by its own idle pre-warmed processes under ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/ to the trash (trash-put from PATH; ANTIGRAVITY_AGY_CLEANUP=off disables) and pre-warms up to 4 idle agy processes (~400 MB each).

name: antigravity-oauth
description: Sign in to Google Antigravity with `vibervnbot auth add antigravity-oauth` (or one command, `npx vibervnbot-antigravity-oauth`) and run ViberVN Bot on the Antigravity plan: Gemini 3.x, Claude 4.6, GPT-OSS. Every request is made by Google's official agy CLI under agy's own login. The plugin writes your ViberVN Bot SOUL.md and system prompt into agy's workspace GEMINI.md so the persona carries over. When a model reaches for an agy-native tool (run_command, view_file, grep_search, and so on) the call is re-issued as the matching ViberVN Bot tool, which then runs under ViberVN Bot approvals. agy never executes tools on the host, and unmapped native tools are blocked. Disclosure: inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin never reads, copies or uploads the OAuth token. It symlinks agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME, which is deleted on close. It also probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT). Disclosure — inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin does not read or upload the OAuth token itself; it symlinks (hard-links, or as a last resort copies) agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME that is deleted on close, probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only, and writes the full ViberVN Bot system prompt into that temp workspace as GEMINI.md each turn. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT).

name: antigravity-subscription-directsdk
description: Run ViberVN Bot on an Antigravity subscription via the official agy CLI (DirectSDK path). Streams tokens progressively, persists multi-turn trajectories via agy --conversation (up to 239k tokens), discovers models dynamically per account, maps thinking effort, reports quota in /usage, and aborts reported native tools. Disclosure — routes inference and /usage quota reads through Google's official agy CLI under your subscription (usage counts against it); links (symlink, else hardlink/copy) the antigravity-oauth-token into a per-session private temp HOME deleted on close; probes OS keyring presence (Linux Secret Service, macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager) without reading secrets; on macOS symlinks ~/Library/Keychains for CLI session reuse; never writes to vendor credential stores; strips credential-looking environment variables before spawning agy (name heuristic; ANTIGRAVITY_ENV_STRICT for an allow-list). Disclosure — the opt-in ANTIGRAVITY_DEBUG_PROMPT_DIR env var writes every outgoing prompt (full conversation text) to that directory.

name: anyapi
description: AnyAPI.ai — unified OpenAI-compatible access to 400+ models; /model picker filtered to tool-capable routes. Disclosure — sends your prompts, tool results and ANYAPI_API_KEY to api.anyapi.ai, a third-party relay (AnyAPI Inc.) that forwards them to the upstream vendor serving the chosen model; billed to your AnyAPI account.

name: anyrouter
description: AnyRouter — unified model gateway (OpenAI-compatible); /model picker filtered to tool-capable routes, first-party meta-models like anyrouter/vibervnbot. Disclosure — sends your prompts and ANYROUTER_API_KEY to anyrouter.dev, a third-party relay that forwards to upstream vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, …), on some plans through a shared pool of other members' donated free-tier vendor keys; billed in prepaid AnyRouter credits. anyrouter/vibervnbot is AnyRouter's own routing meta-model. Opt-in ANYROUTER_APP_ATTRIBUTION=1 adds ViberVN Bot attribution headers.

name: anysearch
description: AnySearch web search and extraction plus two real-time fallback chains: when a primary backend fails (Exa quota, Firecrawl timeout), the same call is served by AnySearch (1,000 free requests/day).

name: aphrodite
description: CCR compression plugin - 28-type classifier, 13 tools, opt-in context engine, TOML-driven templates. Disclosure - pre_tool_call auto-backgrounds long terminal/process commands (modify: background=true, notify_on_complete=true) and rewrites chained terminal commands when enabled. Disclosure — hook and tool logic runs in prebuilt native binaries (libaphrodite_vibervnbot + aphrodite proxy, v1.6.6) built from the public PlayForm/Aphrodite source and fetched by an explicit download.sh step checked against in-tree SHA-256 sums; register() starts a background proxy on 127.0.0.1:9797/9798 whose management routes are open to local processes unless APHRODITE_MGMT_TOKEN is set; pre_tool_call by default rewrites slow terminal commands (cargo/npm/pip/docker/curl…) to run in the background (background=true, notify_on_complete=true) and splits chained commands when enabled; aphrodite_prefetch reads files the model names into its store (refuses .env, auth.json, ~/.ssh and the ViberVN Bot home); requires its own APHRODITE_API_KEY for an upstream LLM endpoint (default api.openai.com).

name: apify
