With embeddings: on, the text of facts, and of messages and fact_store search queries that are not greetings, goes to the OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint the user configures, also after cron turns while cron_writes is on (embedding_url; https, plain http only to localhost, a private or link-local address, or a local host name such as one without a dot or ending in .local), with the key read from the environment variable the user names (embedding_key_env, OPENAI_API_KEY unless set, sent as a Bearer token to whatever embedding_url is configured, never stored in config) and no redirects followed; facts that recall would not inject, and facts and messages that look like they hold a secret (checked by pattern, best effort), are not sent; the vectors are kept in the same file (table fact_embeddings), deleted with their fact by forget / end / remove and all of them by the next writable session after the option is switched off; the provider keeps what it received under its own terms; with rerank: on, before a turn the user's message and up to rerank_top_k (40) candidate fact texts, and for a fact_store search its query and results, go to the rerank endpoint the user configures (rerank_url; https, plain http only to localhost, a private or link-local address, or a local host name), with no credentials and no redirects followed; facts that recall would not inject or that look like they hold a secret, and queries that hold one, are not sent; a failure or a slow answer gives the recall of rerank: off and pauses the endpoint (60 s, doubling to 900 s); nothing the endpoint returns is stored; the bundled language dictionaries are gzip-compressed plain-text word lists; with auto_extract on (off by default) user sentences that state a preference or decision are stored.

name: home-dashboard
description: Personalizable rice-style Home page with draggable, resizable glass widgets for ViberVN Bot Web and Desktop.

name: homeassistant-statistics
description: Read-only Home Assistant Recorder statistics tools (ha_list_statistics and ha_get_statistics). Disclosure — each call opens an authenticated WebSocket connection to the configured Home Assistant instance using the active profile HASS_TOKEN; returned statistic metadata and values become agent tool results and may reach the configured model provider. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, credential storage or direct database access.

name: honcho
description: Honcho is memory infrastructure for building stateful agents that understand changing people, agents, groups, projects, and ideas over time. Store messages and events, let Honcho reason in the background, then query peer representations, session context, search results, or natural-language insights from any model or framework. Use it managed at api.honcho.dev, run a local stack with the honcho CLI, or self-host the server yourself. Maintained by Plastic Labs; the same provider that shipped in-tree. Disclosure — conversation turns, derived conclusions and peer/session ids are sent to the Honcho API (api.honcho.dev by default, or the self-hosted base_url you configure) under your HONCHO_API_KEY; every request also carries X-Honcho-Host (ViberVN Bot version and OS platform) and X-Honcho-Plugin (plugin version) headers that Honcho records for usage attribution.

name: hopper
description: Add and manage custom OpenRouter models in ViberVN Bot without modifying the core catalog.

name: hud-teach
description: Click-through numbered marks on any live Mac window — chess, games, Photoshop, Settings — so ViberVN Bot can teach on the real UI without clicking for the user.

name: huddo
description: Huddo — group chat where people and AI agents talk in the same room. Join by invite link, read and reply, edit or unsend your own messages, react, whisper to one member, pair with your human, wait for new messages, and read or update room apps (shared mini-apps such as task lists that a room owner publishes). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — runs the Huddo MCP server locally over stdio (npx -y huddoai@0.9.11, pinned, npm provenance to this commit; Node 20+); sends and receives room messages via api.huddo.ai, readable by every room member except one-to-one encrypted whispers; when you ask it to create a room, huddo_new tells the agent to post a short summary of your conversation there; huddo_app_submit changes a room app's shared state, which every member sees (app code runs only in members' browsers, never on this machine), and app guides written by the room owner reach the agent as untrusted text; huddo_send can attach any local file the agent names and upload it to the room, huddo_transfer (and huddo_leave with to) hands room ownership to another member, and huddo_update_name/huddo_update_avatar with operator: true change your paired human's display name or avatar; ViberVN Bot does not ask before huddo_send/huddo_whisper/huddo_react/huddo_edit/huddo_unsend/huddo_app_submit/huddo_download/huddo_transfer/huddo_leave/huddo_update_name/huddo_update_avatar/huddo_rename run (the package does not set trust: untrusted); the server tells the agent to keep calling huddo_wait (up to 50 s per call) for as long as it is in a room, and, if ViberVN Bot can schedule recurring tasks, to schedule one that does the same between turns, which keeps spending model tokens until you stop it; the server also tells the agent to read the remote guide at https://huddo.ai/SKILL.md before starting (vendor-hosted, not pinned), and the skills point to npx -y huddoai@latest (unpinned) for identity export and app publishing; downloads go to ~/.huddo/downloads without overwriting; stores a guest identity (signing keys) and a local copy of your rooms' messages (used by huddo_search/huddo_show/huddo_files; huddo_sync fetches older history from api.huddo.ai) in ~/.huddo; no background process (HUDDO_DAEMON=0), no self-update, no telemetry. Room messages from others are untrusted chat content; Huddo marks the paired human with a header tag that message text cannot imitate, and the bundled skills tell the agent to get confirmation in your own ViberVN Bot chat before anything sensitive.

name: hwiki
description: Markdown wiki as ViberVN Bot long-term memory: plain files you and the agent edit together (Obsidian-compatible, git-versionable), local SQLite FTS5 search with optional qmd hybrid retrieval. Inspired by the Karpathy LLM wiki. Disclosure — reads every Markdown file under the wiki folder you set (wiki_path, outside VIBERVNBOT_HOME; untrusted_dirs, default raw/, excluded) and injects up to ~1,400 characters of matching excerpts into each turn; the agent appends dated notes only under <wiki>/<memory_dir> (default wiki/memory), and additions to ViberVN Bot's built-in memory are mirrored there by default (mirror_builtin_memory), so they land in a folder you may commit or sync; keeps an index at VIBERVNBOT_HOME/hwiki-index.sqlite and config in VIBERVNBOT_HOME/hwiki.json, and adds the wiki folder to vibervnbot backup. Cron and subagent runs get read-only recall. No network with the default fts5 backend; the optional qmd backend runs the separately installed qmd CLI (npm @tobilu/qmd, Node ≥22), whose vector modes download local models (~0.3–1.6 GB).

name: hyatlas
description: HyAtlas 5 — self-hosted 8-layer memory provider backed by a pure-Go single-binary server you run yourself (chromem-go vectors, in-process BGE-small embeddings, hybrid vector + keyword search, bitemporal knowledge graph with source citations). Embeddings, the vector index and stored memories are kept locally. Ships agent tools (hyatlas_status/search/recent/add), a `vibervnbot hyatlas` CLI, a Desktop pane with a starmap graph view, and a web dashboard. Disclosure — requires the separate hyatlas-go server, installed by the user. The plugin never downloads or bundles it, and it talks only to the configured server (default 127.0.0.1:19528). Embeddings are computed locally; stored memories leave the machine only in the LLM calls described below. Extraction is opt-in and uses an LLM you choose: `vibervnbot memory setup` asks for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, model and key, and stores the key in ViberVN Bot's .env as HYATLAS_LLM_KEY. The plugin reads that key only through ViberVN Bot's get_secret and reads no ViberVN Bot credential. A plain key file named by HYATLAS_LLM_KEY_FILE also works; the server reads it on every call, so do not point it at another program's credentials such as ViberVN Bot auth.json. The server has no default endpoint and makes no LLM call until the endpoint, the model and a key are all present; while the endpoint and model are set but no key has arrived, /api/v1/status reports llm "awaiting_key". `vibervnbot memory setup`, the repo installer and the sample launcher pre-fill an endpoint and model (and setup defaults to ultra mode), but nothing is sent until a key is supplied. A server the plugin starts gets that key in its environment; for a server started another way (the launcher, a service) that reports "awaiting_key", the plugin (at most every 10 minutes) and `vibervnbot hyatlas doctor` POST the key over plain HTTP to /api/v1/llm/key, only when the configured server host is this machine; the server accepts it only from a loopback address and keeps it in memory only, never on disk. Once configured, each turn's user and assistant text goes to that endpoint (not tool output or context summaries; capped at 12,000 characters), together with up to 5 related stored facts, 3 entity pages and 5 open intentions of that owner so the model can update them instead of duplicating them. In the default ultra mode the server also sends topic-grouped batches of up to 50 stored facts to it every 6 hours (every 20 minutes while earlier batches are still pending) and supersedes (hides but keeps) the facts the model marks merged or stale, recording a reason for each drop. It also records relations corroborated across turns in the local knowledge graph (HYATLAS_CONSOLIDATE_GRAPH=off disables that). Once a day per owner (HYATLAS_CROSS_SCHEMA_EVERY; off disables it) ultra also sends up to 40 of that owner's stored patterns to find up to 3 that hold across topics. In pro and ultra modes it also sends each owner's open intentions, recent summaries and newest facts to rewrite a short Now page, at most every 15 minutes (HYATLAS_NOW_EVERY), and, after a 30-minute pause in an owner's writes (HYATLAS_EPISODE_GAP; off disables it), up to 40 of that stretch's facts to write one episode summary. HYATLAS_RECONCILE=on (off by default) adds a second LLM call per write that sends the new facts together with similar stored ones (including those under user IDs grouped with the owner by HYATLAS_USER_ALIASES) so the model can update, replace or link them; it is meant for a local model. An optional HYATLAS_LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL, tried only when a primary call fails, receives the same text; it is sent the primary key only when it uses the same host. Turns written while the endpoint was unreachable or before a key arrived are extracted later by a catch-up pass (every 10 minutes by default, HYATLAS_CATCHUP_EVERY; rows up to 7 days old, HYATLAS_CATCHUP_MAX_AGE), sending the same text a write would have sent. `vibervnbot hyatlas doctor` sends one short test prompt ("Reply with the single word OK.") to the endpoint and writes, finds and deletes one test memory. When you replace or remove an entry with ViberVN Bot's memory tool, the plugin asks the local server to retire the matching memory (reversible); nothing leaves the machine. HYATLAS_MODE=lite makes no LLM call. Server endpoints that rewrite stored data are off unless the server runs with HYATLAS_ADMIN=on. The spawned server gets an allowlisted environment (OS essentials plus HYATLAS_*), not the agent's keys. auto_start is off by default; when on, ViberVN Bot starts the server as soon as it loads the plugin, and a server started by auto_start or `vibervnbot hyatlas start` keeps running after ViberVN Bot exits until `vibervnbot hyatlas stop`. On Windows, if a hyatlas-go.ps1 launcher is configured, `vibervnbot hyatlas start/stop` runs it; the repo's sample launcher reads no credentials (since 4.8.0 it no longer reads ViberVN Bot auth.json). No telemetry.

name: hydradb
description: Long-term memory for ViberVN Bot, backed by HydraDB. Relevant context is recalled before each turn, and completed turns are saved in the background. Disclosure — when selected as the memory provider, each turn's user message (as the recall query) and every completed user/assistant turn are sent over HTTPS to the HydraDB API (api.hydradb.com, or HYDRADB_BASE_URL) under HYDRADB_API_KEY.

name: hypd-ai-ads
description: Read-only paid-media analysis for Google Ads, Meta (Facebook) Ads, Microsoft Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Google Analytics (GA4), Search Console and Merchant Center through the hosted HYPD MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with four skills (setup, tool rules, overview, ready-made analyses). OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Read-only: never changes campaigns, budgets or ads. Disclosure — runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (downloaded from npm on first run) as a local bridge to HYPD's hosted MCP server at mcp.hypd.ai; tool arguments and the ad, analytics, Search Console and Merchant Center data HYPD returns pass through HYPD's servers; sign-in is a browser OAuth flow whose tokens mcp-remote stores in ~/.mcp-auth; read-only is HYPD's server-side guarantee, and the analysis templates the skills follow are fetched from HYPD's server at run time.

name: icarus
description: Self-memory and replacement models for ViberVN Bot agents. Remember your work. Train your replacement.

name: identity
description: View and edit the identity files (SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, USER.md, AGENT.md/VIBERVNBOT.md) from chat, switch the active profile, and see per-line usage with colour-coded staleness timestamps. Adds six tools, /identity, /identity-switch and /identity-dashboard commands, and a utilization dashboard pane. Disclosure — reads and writes the identity files and a line-utilization record inside the selected profile directory under VIBERVNBOT_HOME, and can change which profile is active; it performs no network I/O and holds no credentials. Disclosure — the model-callable identity_edit tool rewrites SOUL.md/MEMORY.md/USER.md/AGENT.md and identity_switch_profile writes VIBERVNBOT_HOME/active_profile.

name: image-utils
description: Inspect, resize, crop, rotate, convert and re-encode image files in-process with Pillow - no shell, no ImageMagick, no network.

name: index-network
description:
Give your agent someone to talk to. Index is the social layer between personal agents. It makes it possible to find the others who share your flavor of weird, no searching or posting needed.
You're already telling your agent what you're interested in, and what you're secretly tinkering on. We give personal agents the coordination protocol to socialize their humans' intents. They structure mutual intents into opportunities, negotiate on fit, learn from each turn, and surface connections between people who otherwise might've just missed each other. Disclosure — login (browser or `vibervnbot index login`) writes INDEX_SESSION_TOKEN and INDEX_API_URL to the ViberVN Bot env. When this install is the selected negotiator (under the gateway, Desktop's backend or the dashboard), a Bun child (INDEX_BUN, else PATH) runs the pinned bundle with an allowlisted environment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, LC_ALL, TZ plus names in INDEX_NEGOTIATOR_ENV_PASSTHROUGH; never the session token, no .env files) and drives your ViberVN Bot model over a loopback bridge; only with plugins.entries.index-network.settings.custom_negotiator set to true (default off) does the bundle import $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/index/negotiator.ts, when it exists, and run it on each turn before the built-in negotiator (code in that file runs with the negotiator's Index API key and model bridge); the plugin mints INDEX_API_KEY from the session if it is missing, saves it to the ViberVN Bot env and registers the Index MCP server in config.yaml. API traffic goes to protocol.index.network. If INDEX_EARLY_NETWORK_ID is set, confirming onboarding joins that Index network. Negotiation turns are saved as ViberVN Bot sessions in a Negotiations project. The 08:00 "Index morning" cron job is off until turned on; when on it wakes the negotiator once per active networked signal, spending model calls and possibly sending outreach. The desktop half ships as desktop/plugin.js and stays off until enabled.

name: index-search
description: Search one index you run and watch one saved query, with index_search, index_health and index_watch. Disclosure — Sends MEILI_API_KEY as a Bearer token to your MEILI_HOST. Over plain http that key travels unencrypted, and a master or admin key is sent as given, so use a search-only key. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways: anyone you allow on your ViberVN Bot gateway can search with your key and approve a watch. Turn a surface off with vibervnbot tools. index_watch schedule creates one cron job that runs a model turn every 15 minutes (two or more model requests when it calls the tool) with no daily cap, and it watches only the first 20 hits. The job stays after uninstall until you run vibervnbot cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. Scheduling and unscheduling ask for ViberVN Bot approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, unattended sessions and plugins.isolation: host, where the watch only posts a notice that it cannot run, on every run. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml. The watch relies on private parts of ViberVN Bot, so an update can stop it.

name: infisical
description: Secret source plugin that resolves environment variables from an Infisical secret store (cloud or self-hosted) at ViberVN Bot startup. Registers a mapped source ("infisical", inf:// references) and a bulk source ("infisical_bulk").

name: inkbox
description: Inkbox email, SMS/MMS, iMessage, voice, and A2A platform plugin for ViberVN Bot.

name: inline-platform
description: Use ViberVN Bot from Inline work-chat DMs, chats, and reply threads. Disclosure — the setup wizard can, on explicit opt-in, download https://inline.chat/cli/install.sh and pipe it to sh without a checksum, then run the vendor inline CLI login; on connect the adapter publishes your ViberVN Bot slash-command list and the names and descriptions of installed skills to the Inline server (INLINE_SYNC_COMMANDS=false disables); error telemetry is off unless a Sentry DSN is set.

name: intelligent-tool-break
description: Abort a stalled in-flight tool call with /break, send a note with /break {message}, or retry it with /again without cancelling the rest of the task.

name: intelligent_memory
description: Local-first Arabic/English intelligent memory with canonical facts, conflict lifecycle, bounded recall, and selective ViberVN Bot cloud enrichment.

name: interim-ledger
description: Local ledger of the messages models write in the middle of a turn, before their final answer (the text that comes with a tool call, which on chat platforms can arrive as messages of their own): /interim-log shows how many each model wrote, in how many turns, how many per such turn, their median length and how long ago the last one was, per model, provider, surface or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /interim-log recent lists the newest messages (ten, or up to 100 with /interim-log recent 50). Counted even where display.interim_assistant_messages hides them. Disclosure — writes message metadata (model, provider, surface, step of the turn, length in characters, 12-digit hashes of the session and turn ids; never the message text) to plugin-data/interim-ledger/interim.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot delay, change or hide a message; no network

name: invinoveritas-receipts
description: Signed, independently checkable receipts for ViberVN Bot approval verdicts and, since 0.2.0, for turns that stop on iteration exhaustion. Observe-only: a post_approval_response hook requests an invinoveritas decision receipt for each Guardian LLM verdict (or every approve/deny with scope=all); post_llm_call + on_session_end record, when a turn ends with max_iterations_reached, whether the turn's todo ledger (the last todo result or the list re-injected after compaction) was complete (turn_scope: exhausted by default, all, or off). Each receipt is a signed set of salted commitments that anyone can check for free at /verify-proof and that the holder can later open with the salt kept locally. Never approves, denies, delays, continues or blocks anything. Disclosure — one HTTPS POST per recorded approval decision or recorded turn to api.babyblueviper.com/decision-receipt (or the configured api_url) under INVINOVERITAS_API_KEY, paid automatically at 100 sats per receipt from your invinoveritas balance with no per-call confirmation (defaults: Guardian LLM verdicts, and only turns that stop on max_iterations_reached; scope: all adds every human approve/deny, turn_scope: all pays on every turn); sends a fixed question, the options, the choice, a nonce-salted SHA-256 of the context and the tool_call_id/turn_id, never the command text, todo contents or reply text; stores receipts, salts and the full contexts (including the command as ViberVN Bot passed it, and the todo ledger) in plugin-data/invinoveritas-receipts/receipts.jsonl.

name: iowap
description: Fleet control for ViberVN Bot Desktop: live statusbar chip (N/M IOWAP nodes online), a draggable fleet pane, a full fleet page (status, load, queue depth, capabilities per node, activity) and a tasks page that submits to any task-type capability on the fleet and tracks submitted tasks live (per-stage status dots, result previews, artifacts). Data stays local via the local node-cli against your own IOWAP relay; agent sessions join through an optional iowap-task bridge into a shared track store. Disclosure — the dashboard backend runs the local node-cli (the IOWAP node client from github.com/iowap-org/iowap-node) to read your relay's node list, capabilities and task results, and to submit tasks you start from the Tasks page to nodes on your IOWAP fleet. Relay health also goes through the local node-cli (`server health`) — the plugin itself makes no raw HTTP calls to the relay; node identity comes from the node's own ~/.relay state files. Tracked task ids are stored in your ViberVN Bot home under plugin-data/iowap/.

name: iteration-budget-meter
description: Status-bar chip for the focused session per-turn iteration usage (N/60), with a hover tooltip and a click popover of per-request stats.

name: ja-writing-guard
description: Rule-based proofreading for Japanese business text: finds and fixes AI-style phrasing (stock phrases, monotonous sentence endings, overused symbols and Markdown, English-calque grammar) with line, column and a fix hint. It checks wording, not authorship, and rarely flags plain model output. A transform_llm_output hook checks every final Japanese answer and only reports by default; opt-in enforce mode rewrites flagged answers with the user's own model and delivers the rewrite only if numbers, names, URLs, code and negation survive and the score drops under the threshold. Disclosure: no network calls of its own; enforce mode sends each flagged answer to the user's configured model (one extra call, a second only when the first rewrite fails the checks or stays over the threshold; extra cost and up to 25 s delay); a read-only post_tool_call hook notes turns with MEDIA: lines so attachments from other plugins are kept; reports stay in process memory on local surfaces only. Disclosure — no network calls of its own; mode report (default) only logs scores; opt-in mode enforce sends each flagged final answer (with finding excerpts) to the user's configured model via ctx.llm (1–3 calls, up to 25 s delay) and replaces the delivered and stored answer when its preservation checks pass, which do not prove meaning is unchanged; reads plugins.hook_callback_timeout via a private read-only ViberVN Bot helper; eval/ dev scripts ship in the tree but are never loaded.

name: jackal-verified
description: Typed adapter for the reproducible JACKAL v1.7.3 release: 41 catalog-derived verification tools (exact, numerical, Lean-checked bounded lanes, claim replay).

name: jekyll-hyde
description: Context optimization and execution alignment for agent sessions.

name: jet-browser
description: Verify Jet Browser startup, native input, DOM agreement, and PNG capture inside a network-isolated WPE WebKit container. Disclosure — runs `docker run` (Docker access is root-equivalent on the host) on the digest-pinned image ghcr.io/masakaai/jet-browser@sha256:540a1fec…, pulled from GHCR on first use; the container has no network and only SETUID/SETGID capabilities, but runs with AppArmor and systempaths unconfined and a seccomp profile that allows user-namespace and mount syscalls for WebKit's bubblewrap sandbox; the tool takes no arguments and loads only a built-in local test page.

name: jev
description: Explicit Jev decision sidekick via TypeSafe or Cloudflare; advisory judgments, no automatic tool gating.

name: jev-agent-router
description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (agent_route) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no ViberVN Bot tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

name: jev-approvals
description: TypeSafe's Jev decision model as ViberVN Bot' smart-approval reviewer only: it cannot generate text and refuses every other task. Supports TypeSafe direct, OpenRouter, and configurable Jev-compatible HTTPS endpoints with optional endpoint-specific authentication; validates typed answers and endpoint/redirect boundaries, redacts command credentials, and records bounded structured audit logs. Disclosure — each command routed to smart approval (redacted best-effort) and the operator's smart-policy text leave the machine for the configured third-party endpoint; provider or validation failures fail closed to ESCALATE.

name: jev-cron-gate
description: Skip agent cron runs that would do nothing: a pre-run wake-gate script asks TypeSafe Jev one yes/no question over a small state snapshot (files, changed-since-last-run, localhost URLs) and prints {"wakeAgent": false} when it is confident the run is pointless. Fail-open on every error, forced wake after N consecutive skips, stdlib only. Disclosure — each gated cron tick (and the tool's test action) sends the configured snapshot of file contents, localhost URL response bodies and change flags (≤6,000 chars) to api.typesafe.ai with your TypeSafe key.

name: jev-curator
description: TypeSafe Jev semantic governance for ViberVN Bot' native Curator: classifies relationships between complete skill packages, produces content-hash-bound, fail-closed consolidation plans, and locally guards background destructive skill_manage calls while ViberVN Bot retains control of backups and mutations. A profile-scoped 60-second lifecycle debounce coalesces skill changes into dry refreshes. Disclosure — no egress occurs by default; after allow_content_egress is explicitly enabled, redacted bounded skill content is sent to the configured TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or custom Jev endpoint and may spend provider credits. Automatic refreshes never apply mutations, and missing, stale, or incomplete evidence fails closed.

name: jev-effort-router
description: Per-turn model AND reasoning-effort routing, decided by TypeSafe Jev, which rewrites the outgoing Ollama:Cloud provider request itself via the llm_request middleware. Every other catalog router picks a model and stops, and the two entries that touch reasoning effort move it by hand; this one decides both per turn. Ollama:Cloud only — no other provider is routed, and every failure path leaves the request byte-identical to a plugin-disabled run. Disclosure — sends the current user message and up to 4 previous turns to OpenRouter's Decisions API (typesafe/jev, billed to your OpenRouter key) on every routed turn.

name: jev-judge
description: TypeSafe Jev as a judgment layer — a pre-tool gate (shadow by default, enforce escalates) on terminal, write_file and patch asking destructive / exfiltration / impact (a v2 signal set — reads_secrets × sends_outbound, blast_radius, self_advocating — is one setting away), plus a jev_ask tool for typed judgments. Thresholds in code, one JSONL line per decision with the fail-open reason, fail-open on every error path. Stdlib only, no Node; no redirects, proxy env ignored, payload capped; works with TYPESAFE_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY. Disclosure — each judged call sends the tool name and its redacted arguments (≤600 chars each, ≤12 args) to TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or your configured gateway, using your key; shadow mode only logs. With the default backend auto, OPENROUTER_API_KEY is used automatically whenever it is present and TYPESAFE_API_KEY is not, so tool names and redacted arguments go to openrouter.ai on your main-model OpenRouter key unless backend is set to typesafe or gateway.

name: jev-mcp-router
description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (mcp_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no ViberVN Bot tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

name: jev-memory-selector
description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (memory_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no ViberVN Bot tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

name: jev-model-router
description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (model_route) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Registers no ViberVN Bot tools or hooks; do not expect jev_* tools.

name: jev-skill-router
description: Names the one skill from your live roster that fits the turn, before the model call — typed routing via TypeSafe Jev (one choice over the roster plus gate booleans, then a re-read of the shortlist with per-candidate fits), with both thresholds applied in code. Says nothing when nothing fits; opt-in, fail-open, stdlib only, no Node; no redirects, proxy env ignored, payload capped. Disclosure — on eligible turns it sends your message (up to 4,000 chars) plus skill names and short SKILL.md excerpts from your local roster to TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or your configured gateway, using your key. With backend auto an OpenRouter key is used automatically when no TypeSafe key is set, and the OpenRouter route also reads ViberVN Bot' OpenRouter credential pool (auth.json) when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is absent, rotating that pool's entries through the core pool API.

name: jev-skill-router-mcp
description: Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill plus one stdio MCP server (skill_select) started with uv run from the checkout. Needs uv on PATH. Suggests at most one skill per request via the TypeSafe (Jev) cookbook pattern; roster is read live from the profile skills dir. Note: the portable loader does not interpolate env in mcp.json — JEV_TYPESAFE_API_KEY must be present in the server's inherited environment (native mcp_servers declaration works too).

name: jev-typesafe
description: TypeSafe Jev (System One) decision tools — atomic yes/no checks, routing, rubric scoring and mixed typed questions with calibrated probabilities, for triage, routing and review gating in coding agents. Disclosure — every tool call sends the model-supplied question/state together with your TYPESAFE_API_KEY to api.typesafe.ai (TypeSafe AI, an independent vendor); the catalog has not verified the plugin author's affiliation with that vendor.

name: jira-browser
description: Jira workspace for ViberVN Bot Desktop, linking tickets to ViberVN Bot Projects, worktrees, and conversations. Disclosure — reads a Jira API token from JIRA_* env vars or ~/jira-config/config.json (owner-only, read-only) and sends it only to your configured https Jira origin; agent tools are read-only but return Jira text (untrusted) to the model; Start work / Draft update create chats seeded with ticket descriptions (Draft update auto-runs a turn); PR/CI status is read through your local gh CLI login.

name: job-search
description: A private, local-first job-search assistant that finds postings, judges them against your prose preferences (no scores), and writes digests on a schedule you control.

name: jot
description: Notes, checklists and documents beside ViberVN Bot that your agent can read and update safely, with revision checks and undo for AI edits.

name: jp-address
description: Splits one Japanese address into prefecture, city, town and the remainder with address_split, built on Geolonia's address data (CC BY 4.0, from the Digital Agency address base registry). Give it a Japanese postal address as written, such as 東京都千代田区霞が関2-1-2, and it returns the prefecture, city and town as separate fields. Disclosure — Each call sends at most two HTTPS GET requests, with no API key, to japanese-addresses-v2.geoloniamaps.com or the JP_ADDRESS_BASE_URL you set (plain http only for 127.0.0.1 and localhost). The matched prefecture and municipality names go into the URL path; the house number, the lot and the building name are not sent. JP_ADDRESS_BASE_URL is read for the active profile on each call, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. The tool is on for every surface, including gateways, and asks for no approval: anyone you allow on your ViberVN Bot gateway can call it. Turn a surface off with vibervnbot tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. It writes no files and creates no cron job. A point can be coarser than the town and is not a rooftop geocode, and an address it cannot place for certain comes back as ambiguous or at the municipality instead of a guess. The publisher may change or stop the free host and suggests self-hosting for commercial use. Called from ViberVN Bot with five models in a small sample of 18 sessions (see CHANGELOG.md).

name: jp-charts
description: Bar, line, stacked and 100% band charts as phone-sized PNGs for chat replies and reports, with Japanese text, 万/億 units and a required unit and source line. Every bar, point, label and tick is read back from the finished figure and compared with the parsed data before the image is returned. Disclosure: no network calls at run time; reads a local .csv/.tsv/.txt/.json only when given its path (never hidden files or the ViberVN Bot home); writes PNGs to the ViberVN Bot image cache; a transform_llm_output hook adds a forgotten MEDIA line to replies on chat platforms and cron deliveries (setting auto_attach, on by default).

name: jp-chatwork
description: Talk to ViberVN Bot from Chatwork rooms, built on the Chatwork API: put ViberVN Bot in a Chatwork room and ask it with [To:] or a reply, like a colleague; the answer comes back as a Chatwork reply. Polls the Chatwork API (no public URL or webhook), never answers a message twice across restarts, and while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset only the token's own account can use ViberVN Bot commands beyond /help, /whoami, /new and /reset or answer approval prompts. Disclosure: talks only to api.chatwork.com with your own API token; polls every 5 s by default while the gateway runs; stores read positions and the ids of its posted messages in <VIBERVNBOT_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-chatwork/state.json. Disclosure — while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset everyone in the rooms listed in CHATWORK_ROOMS (external guests included) can prompt the agent and use its enabled tools, with ViberVN Bot commands and approval answers kept to the token's own account; talks only to api.chatwork.com with your API token, polling every 5 s while the gateway runs; stores read positions and posted message ids in <VIBERVNBOT_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-chatwork/state.json; logs each asker's name and account id.

name: jp-corporate
description: Japanese corporate lookup (法人照会): find or verify a company by name or corporate number and read its gBizINFO record (basic info, subsidies, government contracts, awards, certifications, financials, patents, workplace data). Disclosure — sends the company names, corporate numbers and prefectures you look up to api.info.gbiz.go.jp (METI gBizINFO) with your own GBIZINFO_API_TOKEN in a request header; no other host, nothing written to disk.

name: jp-edinet
description: Japanese filings on the EDINET API v2. It finds a Japanese company's annual securities report (yuho) and other financial reports filed on EDINET, and reads headline figures such as revenue and total assets from a filing. Disclosure — talks only to api.edinet-fsa.go.jp over HTTPS, and your EDINET_API_KEY rides in the URL as Subscription-Key. Each call reads EDINET_API_KEY for the active profile, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. The edinet toolset is on for every platform, including gateways, so anyone a gateway admits can call these tools with your key. With CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS unset, everyone in CHATWORK_ROOMS can call them. Turn the toolset off per platform with vibervnbot tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. There is no daily cap. The agent can call the three tools itself. A cron you add stays after uninstall until you remove it in ViberVN Bot. This plugin starts no child process and is not a sandbox. Search sends EDINET the filing date, and a download sends the document id and its type. Company name, securities code, EDINET code, and corporate number are filtered on your machine. found: false only means the figure is missing from the consolidated current-year rows the plugin reads, not that the document has no number. A past day's filing list can change. Lists, saved files, and a key fingerprint, not the key, stay at <VIBERVNBOT_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-edinet per profile after uninstall. Delete that directory to remove them. The plugin relies on ViberVN Bot internals for the write check and the data folder. If an update moves those parts, the tools refuse and do not call EDINET. Test files are not loaded at startup.

name: jp-egov-law
description: Japanese laws for ViberVN Bot, built on the e-Gov Law API: find a law by name, abbreviation or phrase, read one article as in force today or on a given date, and check amendment history and enforcement dates, with the source credit e-Gov's terms ask for. Ask for one Japanese law article, such as Article 32 of the Labor Standards Act, and it returns the official law text with the law number and the date that version took effect. Disclosure — sends the law names, article numbers, dates and search phrases you look up to laws.e-gov.go.jp (public API, no key); no other host, nothing written to disk. Registers blueprint jp-egov-law:weekly-amendments and does not create a cron job. When you create a job from that blueprint, one model turn runs once a week (default Mon 09:00, ViberVN Bot tz or the host clock if unset, not converted to Japan). A turn that calls a tool is at least two model requests, and there is no daily cap. The agent can schedule it, and scheduling it twice creates two jobs. Silence is not "no amendment". Uninstall leaves the cron until vibervnbot cron remove. Tools stay on every platform, including gateways (a guest can call them; vibervnbot tools disables one). While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. v0.21.4 and v0.21.5 load the tools and skip the blueprint.

name: jp-estat
description: Japanese government statistics from the e-Stat API: search tables and fetch figures such as population, households, wages, and prices, with estat_search_tables, estat_table_info, and estat_get_data. Disclosure — It needs a free e-Stat application ID, set as ESTAT_APP_ID in the .env of each profile. Each call sends your search words and table selections to api.e-stat.go.jp and puts ESTAT_APP_ID in the request URL. The ID is read for the active profile on each call. An HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used, and no other host is called. Nothing is written to disk, and this plugin creates no cron job. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, so anyone you allow there can call them with your ID. Turn a surface off with vibervnbot tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off.

name: jp-kokkai
description: Lists Diet meetings and returns a short speech excerpt, with kokkai_search, kokkai_speech, and kokkai_watch. Disclosure — Talks only to kokkai.ndl.go.jp over HTTPS GET with no API key. kokkai_search returns meeting metadata and the official meeting URL, and does not return speech text. kokkai_speech reads /api/speech and returns at most 10 excerpts, each at most 240 characters, with the speaker, the meeting name, the date, and the speech URL. Those excerpts are not written to plugin-data. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways: anyone you allow on your ViberVN Bot gateway, and a guest in a room with an empty allowlist, can search, read a speech excerpt, add a watch, and approve it. Turn a surface off with vibervnbot tools. kokkai_watch add creates one cron job that runs a model turn once a day, at the hour you pick in ViberVN Bot's own timezone, with no daily cap. It stays after uninstall until you run vibervnbot cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. Adding or removing a watch asks for ViberVN Bot approval every time and is refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, unattended sessions, and plugins.isolation: host. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot save seen speech IDs and says so on every run. The watch relies on private parts of ViberVN Bot, so an update can stop it. State (your watch words, seen speech IDs, and the job id) stays in plugin-data/jp-kokkai after uninstall.

name: jp-reinfolib
description: Quarterly MLIT prices for one city, via reinfolib_quarter. Use it for Japanese real estate and property prices in one city: it returns the number of recorded sales, the median trade price and the first 20 rows for a quarter. These are transaction prices, not the official land prices published as 地価公示. Disclosure — sends your REINFOLIB_API_KEY as Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key to www.reinfolib.mlit.go.jp (HTTPS, XIT001) or the host of REINFOLIB_BASE_URL. Plain http is refused except 127.0.0.1 and localhost, where the key is not encrypted. On for every surface, including gateways, so anyone you allow can call it with your key, with no approval prompt, including unattended cron, yolo, and approvals off. vibervnbot tools does not stop /jp-reinfolib. Stop the slash command with allow_admin_from, user_allowed_commands, group_user_allowed_commands, or by disabling the plugin. After a GET returns, this process waits 1 second before the next, each GET stops after 30 seconds with no bytes, and there is no retry or daily cap. Blueprint jp-reinfolib:weekly-city-check is once a week (default Monday 09:00) and calls only this tool after you schedule it. This plugin does not create a cron job or write a file. A job you schedule stays until vibervnbot cron remove and may include your MCP servers. HTTP 404 means no data for that request, not zero rows and not unchanged prices. A scheduled run is one model turn. A turn that calls the tool is at least two model requests. An empty slash allow list does not stop this tool. Registered only if register_automation_blueprint exists; else skip. A no-data week may be [SILENT] and not arrive. Data weeks are one short message. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. 「このサービスは、国土交通省の不動産情報ライブラリのAPI機能を使用していますが、提供情報の最新性、正確性、完全性等が保証されたものではありません」

name: jp-subsidies
description: Japanese subsidy search and weekly watch, built on the jGrants public API. Disclosure — Searches api.jgrants-portal.go.jp with no API key and no daily request cap; each call waits at most 60 seconds and retries at most twice, and a result is a search match, not proof that every subsidy came back. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your ViberVN Bot gateway can call these tools and change this profile's watch, and the agent can set up a watch by itself. In a Chatwork room listed in CHATWORK_ROOMS, everyone can call them while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset. The tools are on for every platform, including gateways; turn them off per platform with vibervnbot tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. The /subsidies command is outside vibervnbot tools; limit it with allow_admin_from or user_allowed_commands, or disable the plugin. The optional weekly watch is an unattended cron job that runs a script with no model call and is not a sandbox; delivering it to bot-chat instead runs one model turn on the fetched text. If delivery fails after the script runs, those subsidies are already marked seen and the text stays under cron/output/. Uninstall leaves the cron job, scripts/jp-subsidies-weekly-*.py and plugin-data/jp-subsidies/ until you run vibervnbot cron remove and delete the files. The plugin does not store the name or ID of who asked. Not tested against a live gateway, with the Chatwork plugin loaded, or for result sets of several hundred rows.

name: junie-acp
description: JetBrains Junie coding agent as a ViberVN Bot model provider over ACP.

name: jwt-ref
description: @jwt: context references that decode a JSON Web Token for the model: @jwt:<token> (or a quoted "Bearer <token>") attaches the header with the algorithm in words, every claim as JSON, the exp, nbf, iat and auth_time claims in UTC with how long ago or ahead they are, whether the token has expired and its lifetime, and notes on alg none, a missing or empty signature, a header that names its own key (jku, x5u, jwk), crit and duplicate names; encrypted tokens (JWE) show their header only; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a token as you type it. The signature is never verified. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's base64, json and datetime; no network (no key sets fetched), no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of the token, but the @jwt: reference and the decoded header and claims become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history, so decode only tokens you are willing to share with it; register() only adds the @jwt: reference provider.

name: kanban-gantt
description: One board, three views, and each answers a different question: List says what the work is, Timeline says when it happened, Graph says what hangs off what. The Graph view draws a card per task and an arrow per dependency, laid out top-down by longest path (or left to right, by status, or as a compact grid), with a transitive reduction that counts the arrows it implies instead of hiding them, links you draw, move and delete where they are drawn, and a click that lights the whole upstream and downstream lineage of a task. The Timeline renders any board as real work timestamps (created/started/review/done), with a collapsible tree column (boxed fold controls, tree connectors, per-board fold state, multi-parent links kept visible), live-activity arcs, filters, bulk actions, and a period selector from 6 hours to 7 days. The List view trades the bars for a dense table — task, assignee, status, last activity. Quick scopes (Running, Blocked, Open, All) narrow the board in all three views alike, and a lineage switch widens any of them to what leads to the selection and what follows it. Tasks are created from the page (project, workspace, skills, model override, goal mode), re-parented by drag & drop or from the drawer, and moved between boards with their children; any task with files carries a paperclip, its files listed on demand — the board payload carries only a count — and previewed by type (markdown, plain text, image, PDF, HTML in a sandboxed frame) or downloaded. Zero API keys, zero model tokens; live updates follow the plugin's /events websocket, which a gateway turns off with KANBAN_GANTT_WS=0 (the page then polls every 60 s and shows a Refresh button). Disclosure — Desktop page plus dashboard routes that read and write the local kanban boards (create tasks with workspace path, skills, model override and goal mode; re-parent; move a task, with its children, to another board — the copy is verified there before the source rows and their links are deleted; edit status, assignee and description; bulk archive and delete; read task attachment files from the board's own attachments folder for preview and download); live updates over a dashboard-authenticated /events websocket, off with KANBAN_GANTT_WS=0; no third-party network.

name: kanban-graph
description: Live, read-only dependency graph of the ViberVN Bot kanban boards in ViberVN Bot Desktop: every board as a band, tasks as cards, dependencies as arrows with implied ones folded away. Click a task to light up its whole lineage with runs, last failure and the running worker's latest tool calls; deep links open a task directly, and a stdlib CLI renders the same graph as a standalone HTML file. Zero API keys, zero model tokens. Disclosure — reads every kanban board database and, for running tasks, the assignee profile's state.db (the kanban worker session's latest assistant messages and tool-call arguments), read-only, and shows them in Desktop through its own local dashboard routes.

name: kanban-live-gantt
description: Live, now-centered Gantt timeline for the ViberVN Bot kanban boards — a slidable, persisted 72 h window (default now -24h -> now +48h; drag to move, drag the ends to resize), free wheel zoom down to hour ticks, a now line, status filtering, an optional done lane, and lifecycle rendering (dashed waiting vs solid run spans at real durations). Fork of kanban-gantt (GPL-3.0). Disclosure — the backend can transition, reassign, comment on and permanently delete kanban tasks on any board (Desktop asks for confirmation before deletes); local SQLite only, no network.

name: kanban-stream
description: Live-stream ViberVN Bot kanban worker activity to a Telegram ops channel: one edit-in-place message per task with rolling tool-call history, elapsed timer, tokens/sec, thinking indicator, and a pinned final state (done/blocked). Mid-task steering via task comments — /steer from Telegram through the bundled companion daemon, or straight from the board. Ships disabled by default; needs a dedicated ops bot (KANBAN_STREAM_BOT_TOKEN + KANBAN_STREAM_ALLOWED_USERS). Outbound calls go only to api.telegram.org; reads the kanban DB read-only; no telemetry, no self-update. Disclosure — sends kanban task titles, summaries and tool names with command/path snippets to the Telegram chat you configure via your own bot; the optional steer daemon posts allowlisted Telegram users' /steer text as task comments that reach the running worker.

name: kanban-task-threads
description: Give every ViberVN Bot kanban task a live Discord forum thread with a rewritten status card and append-only event log. Disclosure — sends task and lifecycle data to the configured Discord webhook (no host allowlist). Cards and event replies use built-in or operator-configured templates and may include identifiers, titles, status, assignment, branch and workspace metadata, relationships and blocking details, comments, event actors, reviewers, reasons, summaries, and configured dashboard links; the comment excerpt length is configurable. Fixed prerequisite announcements additionally send the prerequisite task ID, title, assignee, and up to 140 characters of its body and are not template-configurable. The absolute workspace path is off by default and requires explicit opt-in. Reads the kanban database read-only and stores thread mapping state under <kanban_home>/kanban/plugins/kanban-task-threads/. With an optional existing publisher-profile Discord bot token, reads forum and thread metadata; creates or repairs managed status tags and emojis; replaces applied tags on plugin-managed threads; renames threads; and archives or unarchives them. Discord fetches webhook avatars from the configured HTTPS asset origin. Disclosure — the avatar asset origin defaults to the author-hosted https://diegomarino.github.io/kanban-task-threads (disable with avatars_enabled: false). With the bot token the periodic metadata audit also lists the guild's active threads (filtered to the forum) and may rewrite the forum's available-tag list to add the 11 managed status tags (requires Manage Channels).

name: keenable-plugin
description: Web search and page fetching through Keenable's hosted MCP server, with search and research skills: single-site and publish-date filters, result and snippet limits, and page fetches that return only what a prompt asks for. Works without an API key; an optional KEENABLE_API_KEY lifts the keyless rate limits. Adds direct MCP tools beside ViberVN Bot's built-in Keenable web backend and leaves web_search / web_extract provider selection unchanged. Disclosure: connects to Keenable's hosted MCP server at `api.keenable.ai` and sends it the search queries, URLs and fetch prompts the agent issues, labelled with the header `X-Keenable-Title: vibervnbot-plugin`; sends `X-API-Key` only when the user adds the optional config.yaml entry with their key.

name: kimchi-acp-provider
description: The Kimchi coding harness (kimchi.dev) as a ViberVN Bot model provider over ACP stdio — spawns kimchi --mode acp keeping the harness's permission prompts on (YOLO opt-in via KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo"), the harness owns its own auth, and completed tool calls surface as inline bullets in the reply. Disclosure — every turn spawns the local Kimchi CLI (`kimchi --mode acp`, overridable with KIMCHI_ACP_COMMAND / KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS) in ViberVN Bot's working directory and hands it the conversation. The harness calls kimchi.dev with its own stored login and runs its own shell, file and web tools. Its permission prompts stay on, and ViberVN Bot cancels them, so gated tools don't run, unless you opt in with KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo", which runs them with no approval prompt (not for shared gateway or cron use). To show setup status, it parses ~/.config/kimchi/config.json (or KIMCHI_CONFIG_PATH) only to check that a key is present; the key is never stored or sent by ViberVN Bot.

name: kimchi-provider
description: Kimchi (kimchi.dev) models via the OpenAI-compatible API — live catalog from the metadata endpoint, API-key auth, gateway unknown-model 400s classified as model_not_found, and an identifying User-Agent (vibervnbot-agent/<version>) on every gateway request.

name: kimi-code-delegate
description: Delegate-only, fail-closed Kimi Code ACP integration for ViberVN Bot

name: kinocut
description: Guardrailed local video editing: Kinocut's MCP server plus two workflow skills (editing and short-form repurposing). Trim, caption, reformat and check quality with local FFmpeg. Portable Agent Plugins v1 configuration and skills, no plugin code. Requires uv and FFmpeg on PATH; launches uvx kinocut==1.16.4 over stdio. First launch downloads Kinocut and dependencies from PyPI. URL inputs download the requested media; font and model-weight features fetch assets from GitHub. Explicit Revideo dependency installation runs npm ci and may download renderer dependencies. Local FFmpeg editing and color grading need no account or API key. Kinocut's optional vision calls default off and require explicit configuration: legacy product descriptions use an Anthropic-compatible endpoint, while sampled-frame QC uses Anthropic. The README explains how to use the host's image model instead, including local models. Revideo and Hyperframes telemetry default off. Unverified Hyperframes browser previews and Docker renders require explicit telemetry consent. Hyperframes capture/snapshots disable implicit model analysis. These controls are not a network sandbox; see the plugin README for configuration and remaining network use. Disclosure — launches `uvx kinocut==1.16.4` over stdio, which downloads Kinocut and its dependencies from PyPI on first launch; edits and writes local video files with FFmpeg; URL inputs download the requested media, font and model-weight features fetch assets from GitHub, and an explicit Revideo install runs `npm ci`; optional vision features (off by default) send selected images or sampled frames to an Anthropic-compatible endpoint or Anthropic; Revideo and Hyperframes telemetry stay off unless the operator enables them.

name: kiro-acp
description: Kiro CLI (AWS) as a ViberVN Bot model provider, driven over ACP stdio.

name: kiro-provider
description: Native Kiro model provider over HTTPS with AWS Builder ID / IAM Identity Center device login. Disclosure — dynamically registers an AWS OIDC public client named `vibervnbot-kiro` during login and stores OAuth grants in ViberVN Bot' profile-scoped auth.json credential pool.

name: kiwi
description: Source suppliers and negotiate purchases through the Kiwi Buyer MCP server — an open-source A2A commerce runtime (pinned @harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.5 over npx stdio), with the kiwi-buyer sourcing workflow skill bundled. Sourcing is dual-source: Kiwi Network results come from kiwi_search, and internet e-commerce listings are reported through the host's own web tools when the session has them (a host capability, not a plugin guarantee). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js/npm on PATH. No credentials required; Kiwi never handles payments.

name: klipper-print-watch
description: Built on the Moonraker HTTP API. Cron reports klippy_shutdown, complete, error, paused (after printing), cancelled, stalled. Disclosure — Talks to the one Moonraker URL you set. Over plain http on a LAN, MOONRAKER_API_KEY is sent unencrypted. Pause, resume and cancel ask for ViberVN Bot approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off and unattended sessions. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your ViberVN Bot gateway can request a move and approve it. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml. The optional watch is a cron job (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. vision_check, off by default, sends webcam stills to your model. The plugin host cannot watch. Not tested on real hardware.

name: kokoro-tts
description: Local Kokoro-82M text-to-speech on Apple Silicon: adds the kokoro-mlx speech provider (tts.provider: kokoro-mlx) with sentence-by-sentence PCM streaming for voice mode, read-aloud and text_to_speech, 54 voices in nine languages, an optional voice per language that switches per sentence between Portuguese and English, and an optional dictionary of English words a non-English voice pronounces in English without changing voice; plus vibervnbot kokoro install, status, restart, voices, say, words and uninstall. Disclosure — vibervnbot kokoro install creates a separate Python 3.11 environment with uv (about 1.1 GB from PyPI, plus spaCy's en_core_web_sm wheel from its GitHub release, pinned by SHA-256), downloads mlx-community/Kokoro-82M-bf16 at a pinned revision from Hugging Face (about 340 MB), and installs a launchd agent (dev.vibervnbot.kokoro-tts) that keeps a local server running in the background. The server listens only on 127.0.0.1 (it refuses other addresses), runs offline, and does not log the text; the text to speak goes only to that local server, bypassing any proxy settings. Writes the environment, model cache and log under ~/Library/Application Support/vibervnbot-kokoro-tts, the requested audio files, and the profile's config.yaml only when you run vibervnbot kokoro words add or remove. No API keys, no telemetry.

name: kuma
description: Uptime-Kuma monitoring for agents: the community MCP server for Uptime Kuma v2 (pinned @0.11.18 over npx stdio) with workflow skills for incident review, status digests, and confirmation-gated maintenance. Credentials stay in host-native MCP config (portable Agent Plugins v1 package, mcp.json + skills/; needs Node.js >= 22 on PATH and a Uptime Kuma v2 instance). Disclosure — first run has npx fetch @davidfuchs/mcp-uptime-kuma@0.11.18 (single-maintainer community package) from npm; that server exposes 31 read/WRITE tools against your Uptime Kuma instance, including permanent delete tools the bundled skills never call.

name: kumiho-memory
description: Recall and save decisions, preferences and facts in your Kumiho Cloud workspace. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with hosted OAuth MCP and six skills. Disclosure — connects to Kumiho's hosted MCP at https://mcp.kumiho.cloud/mcp (OAuth at control.kumiho.cloud, tokens held by ViberVN Bot); memory queries, including an automatic topic lookup near the start of relevant conversations, and approved captures are sent there; the server is marked `trust: untrusted`, so ViberVN Bot asks before every tool not annotated read-only. The optional backfill helper reads only files the user names and writes review packets to a new folder; Dream State can create a recurring ViberVN Bot cron task when asked (read-only by default). No local server, telemetry or background process.

name: lancedb
description: LanceDB hybrid memory — embedded vector + FTS recall, workspace facts, transparent forget.

name: lancedb-suite
description: Local-first LanceDB vector memory with a strict write contract, calibrated abstention, typed relations, conflict tracking and a retrieval-quality gate. Requires local Ollama + nomic-embed-text.

name: laso-finance
description: Spend USDC in the real world from ViberVN Bot: prepaid cards, gift cards, push-to-card, Venmo/PayPal and bank payouts, through the Laso Finance API. Native plugin, standard library only. Sign-in is the OAuth device flow (link and code handed to the human, approved on any device), so there is no key to paste and it works over SSH and the messaging gateway. Every tool that moves money or mints a credential goes through the ViberVN Bot approval gate first. Disclosure — the tools move real funds from the user's Laso account and agent wallet; 19 money-moving or credential-minting tools ask for ViberVN Bot approval first, but approvals.mode off / yolo, or approvals.cron_mode/unattended_mode approve, let them run without a prompt; laso_buy_with_saved_card is not prompted in ViberVN Bot (Laso requires a passkey approval on the holder's device before an order); all traffic goes to laso.finance only; the approved key is saved as LASO_API_KEY in the profile's .env and removed when Laso rejects it.

name: ld-workbench
description: Practice Lincoln-Douglas debate. A case workbench helps a student build their own case section by section (resolution analysis, value and criterion, contentions, evidence, blocks) with a coach that gives real help and asks hard questions but never writes the case. A topic briefing maps a new resolution for both sides. A full NSDA practice round (AC, cross-examination, NC, 1AR, NR, 2AR, with prep time) runs against an AI opponent at three levels, followed by a ballot from a lay, traditional or flow judge. A fallacies guide, drill and spotter work on the student's own case and on other people's arguments. Cases are kept in a library with Word, text and backup-file export. Every model call goes to the user's own ViberVN Bot model through the plugin LLM helper. Debate Workbench is an independent community plugin. It is not made or endorsed by the National Speech & Debate Association. Disclosure — one network call of its own: when the user adds a topic source link, it fetches that one public web page (http or https, public addresses only, checked on every redirect, 20-second timeout, first 30,000 characters of text kept); no credentials, telemetry, shell commands, background processes or self-updates; registers no tools, hooks or middleware, only a Desktop page and a dashboard API; stores cases, rounds, ballots and briefings in $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugin-data/ld-workbench/; reads a .docx or .txt case file or a backup file only when the user picks one; writes an export only to a path the user picks in the save dialog, inside their home folder; the optional dictation button uses the speech recognition built into the desktop app's browser engine when that engine provides it, which may send the audio to that engine's speech service; no private ViberVN Bot imports.

name: letsfg
description: Search and book real flights and hotels through the hosted LetsFG MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR), with the letsfg travel-booking workflow skill bundled: fares across airlines and the major travel sites, flexible dates, destinations in a region, bookable hotel rates, then book, follow and stop bookings. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only; the server is added by the sign-in command below). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at letsfg.co/mcp. Booking tools act on real money: a booking holds the price on the card saved on the user's LetsFG account (captured only once the airline or hotel confirms, released if it fails); per LetsFG, a booking, paid extra or hotel cancellation starts only when the user presses Approve in an e-mail from LetsFG, never from the conversation, and ViberVN Bot itself does not prompt before these tools unless you set `trust: untrusted` on the letsfg MCP server. Card details are only ever entered on letsfg.co, never in the conversation. Traveller details given for a booking (name, date of birth, gender, passport, contact, address) are sent to LetsFG and saved on that account. The server and its OAuth sign-in are added with `vibervnbot mcp add letsfg --url https://letsfg.co/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`.

name: lib-docs
description: Look up current library docs from public npm and PyPI (no API keys). Resolve a package, fetch README and metadata, keep recent lookups on Desktop. Disclosure — HTTPS to registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org and cdn.jsdelivr.net (npm READMEs) only; package name and version leave the machine; recent lookups are stored under $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugin-data/lib-docs; the Desktop pane inserts text through ViberVN Bot Desktop's internal vibervnbot:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API).

name: lightkeeper
description: An Obsidian-compatible map of how your codebase works (modules, flows, integrations, platform traps, decisions), kept outside the repo and kept honest by hooks: a primer on the first turn, pointers to the notes that own what you are asking about or editing, and a reminder through the verify gate when code moved but the map did not. Eight lightkeeper:* skills carry the procedures (init, seed, tidy, trace, release, knowledge-vault, vault-sync, vault-tidy); the vault CLI (find, check, sync, status, log, export) works from any shell. Not a memory provider. Disclosure — each hook runs python3 on the plugin's own scripts as a synchronous subprocess with a 10 s timeout (on every user message, after every write_file and patch, at the verify step and at session end), and those scripts run read-only git commands (rev-parse, remote get-url, worktree list, ls-tree, status, log) in the session's checkout and in the vault folder; the session primer and prompt hints put text from the vault's notes into the model's context; the hooks read the vault registry ~/.claude/vaults and the vault folders it lists, and write only inside the vault (_meta/index.json), a small per-session state file in the system temporary directory ($TMPDIR), and the plugin's own data directory; the init, seed, sync, tidy, trace and release procedures run the vault CLI through the terminal and commit to the vault's own git repository, and vault init appends the vault to ~/.claude/vaults and, only when you pass its opt-in flags, copies a vault launcher to ~/.local/bin (--install-cli), installs report-only post-merge and pre-push hooks in your code checkouts (--git-hook), or adds a post-commit hook that pushes every vault commit to the remote you name (--backup-remote); vault export writes an HTML map that loads d3 7.9.0 from cdnjs.cloudflare.com when opened; no other network calls, no telemetry, no credentials, no dependencies beyond Python 3.9 and git. Silent until a vault covers the session's working directory.

name: lightningai
description: Lightning AI as a ViberVN Bot model provider (--provider lightning, lightning-ai, lightningai): OpenAI-compatible gateway at https://lightning.ai/api/v1, models fetched live from /models. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to lightning.ai through ViberVN Bot' own client with LIGHTNING_API_KEY (or LIGHTNING_AI_API_KEY), optional LIGHTNING_BASE_URL overrides the endpoint; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads/writes no files and starts no processes.

name: lightningai-rate-limit
description: Per-process throttle for Lightning AI (https://lightning.ai/api/v1) keeping LLM requests within the ~15 requests/min limit, using an in-memory token bucket. Gates only calls whose provider or base_url points at Lightning AI; no-op otherwise. Disclosure — registers one llm_execution middleware and nothing else; no network calls, files, or processes of its own.

name: limbic
description:
Local long-term memory for ViberVN Bot agents. Everything stays on your machine: an SQLite store plus bundled embedding and NLI models, no telemetry, no LLMs.
Limbic is designed on the physiological brain, opaque and organic. Memories strengthen or atrophy with use, corrections replace what they superseded — all deterministic background mechanisms, zero LLM calls.
Algorithmic forgetting keeps atrophied memories out of the database. Recall is calibrated: when nothing in memory is confident enough, it abstains instead of guessing, so the agent answers honestly rather than surfacing near-misses. First start downloads ~1 GB of pinned models once, then runs fully offline. PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (commercial use requires a separate license). Disclosure — the agent-facing tools are remember, recall and forget (forget lists candidate facts for a query, then deletes the one fact id the user picks, scoped to the current user, and appends a hash-only receipt of the content's sha256, length, user id and fact id to limbic.db.deletions.jsonl beside the database); on first primary session start downloads ~1.0GB of ONNX models (Arctic Embed 2.0 L int8 embedding, ~570MB; MiniLMv2 NLI, ~430MB, on first contradiction check) from huggingface.co at pinned commits with hash checks into ~/.cache/limbic/ (outside VIBERVNBOT_HOME; %USERPROFILE%\.cache\limbic on Windows); at every model load, every file in those cache folders that is not in the pinned manifest is deleted — including unrelated files if you point embedding/nli cache_dir at a shared folder; spaCy NER models are optional: `vibervnbot limbic languages --set <lang>` and `vibervnbot limbic setup` run `python -m spacy download <model>`, which pip-installs each model package (~14.5MB, version picked by spaCy, not hash-pinned) from spaCy's GitHub releases into ViberVN Bot's own Python environment, and `vibervnbot limbic setup` also pre-downloads both ONNX models; memory stays local in limbic.db under VIBERVNBOT_HOME, facts whose trust decays to zero are deleted automatically, and vibervnbot backup adds VACUUM snapshots under VIBERVNBOT_HOME/backups; no telemetry.

name: linkedcamp
description: Plan, build and run LinkedIn and email outreach in LinkedCamp through LinkedCamp's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.linkedcamp.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in with the account's API key, no keys in config): campaigns, audience search URLs, multi-step sequences, leads, unified inbox and AI-drafted replies, sending-account health, analytics, reply agents, and agency sub-accounts. Bundles the linkedcamp-outreach workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to LinkedCamp's hosted server (mcp.linkedcamp.com) and acts on the user's LinkedCamp account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. Some tools reach real people (campaign_launch starts outreach, message_send delivers at once); the package marks the server untrusted, so ViberVN Bot asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and blocks them in unattended runs.

name: linkup
description: Linkup web search: live cited search (fast/standard/deep), URL-to-Markdown fetch with JS rendering, async deep research, and a Linkup backend for the built-in web_search / web_extract tools. Disclosure — sends search queries, fetch URLs and research briefs to api.linkup.so with your LINKUP_API_KEY (Linkup fetches pages server-side); when selected with vibervnbot linkup use-as-web-backend it also handles the built-in web_search and web_extract calls; large fetched pages are cached under $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/cache/linkup for 24 hours.

name: liquid-inference-provider
description: Liquid Inference, an auction exchange for LLM inference, as a ViberVN Bot model provider (provider id `liquid`): the exchange sends each request to the eligible offer with the lowest estimated charge, and each request carries a cap on its charge (1 USD by default; set `model.default_headers.x-liquid-cap-usd` to change it). Submitted by Architect, the operator of Liquid Inference. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Chat requests (full prompts and tool results), auxiliary tasks (model `liquid.auto`) and the model list go through ViberVN Bot's own client to https://router.inference.ai.exchange/v1 (or LIQUID_BASE_URL) with LIQUID_API_KEY. The exchange forwards each request to whichever third-party provider wins its auction. Each request is billed up to its `x-liquid-cap-usd` cap (1 USD by default, set with `model.default_headers.x-liquid-cap-usd`) and carries `X-Title: ViberVN Bot`. A top-level `reasoning_effort` is sent only when you select a level.

name: little-canary
description: Screens user turns and blocks downstream tools on a BLOCK verdict; the original prompt still reaches the model.

name: live-time
description: Inject live current time into every LLM call via the pre_llm_call hook — fixes stale session-start timestamps in long/cross-day conversations.

name: llm-antidote
description: Runtime guardrails, behavioral evaluation, and signed fleet admission for ViberVN Bot: a versioned capability policy that blocks or requires approval for model tool calls, paired synthetic behavioral evaluation with no real side effects, and a signed local promotion gate that refuses a model whose evidence does not satisfy signed fleet policy. Hooks-only (no agent tools). Disclosure — Adds approval prompts to tool calls by default (balanced mode): every MCP, connector or other-plugin tool, memory and skill writes, file reads outside the working and temp directories, and network-capable terminal/code commands go to ViberVN Bot's approval prompt; strict mode blocks them instead, and opt-in enforced fleet mode blocks all tool calls until the served model name matches the admitted one. The user-run `vibervnbot antidote eval run` command sends synthetic prompts (and the API key you name) to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint you pass, as billed model calls (default suite up to ~170 requests); `model inspect hf:` queries huggingface.co; `fleet keygen` writes unencrypted Ed25519 private keys (mode 0600) to paths you choose.

name: llmslim
description: Context engine that compresses older tool output and turns locally with LLMSlim instead of asking a model for a summary: no LLM call, deterministic output, and the start of the prompt is sent unchanged, so prompt caching keeps working. Select it with context.engine: llmslim. Disclosure: installs llmslim==0.11.2 from PyPI (with numpy, scikit-learn and jsonschema); registers no tools, hooks or middleware; makes no network calls, runs no shell commands, needs no credentials, writes no files and sends no telemetry; reads its settings from config.yaml through ViberVN Bot's config loader. Token counts use a character estimate unless tiktoken is already installed in ViberVN Bot's environment, in which case tiktoken may download its encoding file once.

name: loaded-skills-indicator
description: Status-bar chip, popover and dockable pane showing which skills are read into the active ViberVN Bot Desktop conversation's context: full bodies bold with an accent dot, compression-pruned ones ghosted, never-loaded ones not listed. A second pane view lists the whole skill library grouped by category with descriptions and a loaded marker, and clicking a skill drops /<skill> into the composer for you to send (it never submits). A small local backend reads the profile's state.db read-only to tell a live skill body from a [SKILL_PRUNED] marker, and reads SKILL.md frontmatter for the descriptions. No network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no writes. Disclosure — the local backend opens state.db read-only for the requested session in this profile, the default root and, as a fallback, every other profile's state.db, and returns only skill names and load state; it reads SKILL.md frontmatter under the ViberVN Bot skill directories and makes no network calls or writes.

name: local-system-one-vibervnbot
description: Local System One / Laya Typed Decisions control plane for ViberVN Bot. Sends bounded turn data to a configurable sidecar for reversible OFF/Shadow/Canary routing decisions, with explicit Canary acknowledgement and fail-open behavior. Disclosure — executes nothing and does not start the sidecar. In Shadow/Canary mode, Search and Model Tier may POST the current task plus bounded recent conversation context; Notification Shadow may POST the completed turn's final assistant response (up to 6000 chars) plus lifecycle metadata. The default sidecar URL is loopback 127.0.0.1:8787 but is user-configurable to any host and no auth header is added. Notification is observation-only: the plugin never sends a push/message/webhook and persists decision metadata, not raw response text. Its only request mutations, in acknowledged Canary mode on the first provider call of a turn, are removing web_search/web_extract tools for audited deterministic no-Web rules and (off by default) lowering reasoning_effort for gemini-3.8-flash-tiered on audited hard-fast rules. The sidecar (same repo, separate pip install, Apple-Silicon MLX/CoreML) is a text classifier that downloads a pinned Hugging Face model.

name: local_knowledge
description: Native ViberVN Bot tools for a configurable local capability index: search/get/neighbors plus local usage feedback/reporting.

name: long-conversations
