description: Persistent long-term conversations across session boundaries via structured handoff briefs and token monitoring. Disclosure — stores handoff briefs (topic, work in progress, decisions, open questions, next step; in aggressive mode auto-built from the first 200 characters of recent user messages) as plain JSON under VIBERVNBOT_HOME/long-conversations/ and injects the pending brief into the first turn of the next session for the same chat or user (CLI briefs stay in one local scope and are not shown to messaging users); the model can change the plugin's settings with long_conv_config_set; an opt-in VIBERVNBOT_LONG_CONV_BETA_LOG writes a local event log; no network calls.

name: looot
description: looot gives ViberVN Bot one sign-in and one prepaid balance for 2,500+ data API endpoints from 90+ providers: work emails and phones, company and people search, Google results, web pages as markdown, news, local businesses. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with the hosted MCP server (remote streamable-http, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration) and 21 skills. Disclosure — the run tool spends your prepaid looot balance (ViberVN Bot asks before each paid call and refuses them in unattended runs); the names, domains and emails you look up are sent to looot.ai and its upstream data providers; a `looot` server you define in config.yaml replaces the package's and drops that prompt unless you add `trust: untrusted`.

name: loreconvo
description: LoreConvo memory provider: cross-surface persistent session memory with search, recall and structured memory items. Disclosure — stores end-of-session transcripts (truncated, including tool output) and ViberVN Bot memory writes in ~/.loreconvo/sessions.db, a store shared across all ViberVN Bot profiles and other LoreConvo clients, and injects context from those sessions into each turn; a Pro license enables a one-time Hugging Face embedding-model download; installs the loreconvo package (BUSL-1.1) with lancedb, fastembed and onnxruntime into the ViberVN Bot environment.

name: lowrouter
description: LowRouter as a ViberVN Bot model provider (`--provider lowrouter`, or LowRouter in `vibervnbot model`). The picker shows the 180 `auto/` chat models with tool calling and 64K+ context, plus the user's own `alias/` models, instead of all 719 IDs from /v1/models. Context windows come from LowRouter's catalog instead of ViberVN Bot' 256K fallback, and /usage shows the credit balance in euros. LowRouter bills in EUR, so the plugin reports no USD cost and ViberVN Bot shows it as unknown. Maintained by LowRouter. Disclosure — registers one model provider and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and LOWROUTER_API_KEY go to https://api.lowrouter.ai/v1 (or the configured model.base_url) through ViberVN Bot' client, and LowRouter forwards each request to the host serving the model. The plugin's own requests are GET /v1/models (cached for an hour) and GET /v1/credits on /usage, to the same base URL with the same key, through ViberVN Bot' open_credentialed_url. No files read or written, no processes.

name: lumberroom
description: lumberroom memory provider. One durable store shared with every agent you use, recalled on every turn and written through the engine's own memory_write. Self-hosted open-source engine or lumberroom.cloud; OAuth or a static token. Maintained by the lumberroom team. Disclosure — when active, every non-trivial user message (first 1,000 characters) and the absolute git-root path of the working directory are sent on each turn to the configured lumberroom engine, which defaults to https://mcp.lumberroom.cloud (operated by Cybersapien Technologies, India) unless base_url names a self-hosted engine; the model is instructed to store decisions, preferences and facts there through memory_write, the engine's live tool descriptions and server instructions are injected into the system prompt each session, and setup switches off ViberVN Bot' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md store.

name: machine-library
description: Research search for web_search and web_extract — papers, books, patents, standards and Wikipedia, with citable source links (Machine Library API key).

name: machine-spirit
description: A Warhammer 40k shrine pane docked under the sessions list: the cogitators recite original Adeptus Mechanicus-style litanies, and the cog-skull, candle and binary stream animate while ViberVN Bot works. Just for fun. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars, network or file access.

name: made-shelf
description: Everything ViberVN Bot made - cross-session shelf of wrote/patched paths. Full Desktop page, chip, pin. No API keys.

name: magi
description: Review pending ViberVN Bot memory writes and inspect, add, edit, delete, or AI-compact stored memory from Desktop.

name: make-parts-now
description: Quote and order custom 3D printed and CNC machined parts from your CAD files through the hosted Make Parts Now MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in to quote), with the quote-parts workflow skill bundled: upload an STL, STEP, 3MF or OBJ file, get the price and ship date for each production speed (SLS nylon, FDM plastic, CNC aluminum and brass), change the quantity, material or speed, and get a checkout link. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to makepartsnow.com. To quote a local file the agent uploads that one CAD file with curl through the terminal tool (ViberVN Bot approvals apply) to a one-time upload link, or gives the user an upload page. Nothing is charged in chat: checkout links open Stripe Checkout on makepartsnow.com where the user pays. US shipping only.

name: maqami-travel
description: Search hotels (3M+ hotels) and flights worldwide on MAQAMI, read hotel details and reviews, then send the customer a secure checkout link on book.maqami.co, through the official MAQAMI Travel MCP server (Streamable HTTP at mcp.maqami.co, no account or key), with the maqami-travel-booking skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — connects to the hosted MAQAMI MCP server at mcp.maqami.co (no key); its tool list is defined by that server, not by the pinned repo. The tool arguments the agent sends go to it: destinations, dates, guests, lead-guest nationality and currency, plus booking ID and email for lookups, amendments and cancellations. Prebook (hotels) and verify (flights) hold a real rate, and the amend and cancel tools change or cancel real bookings (late or non-refundable cancellations are still charged); the skill tells the agent to show the details and get a clear yes before each prebook, amend or cancel. Customers pay only on book.maqami.co; no tool takes card or passport details.

name: markdown-new
description: Search the public web, read pages as Markdown, crawl sites, and convert documents in ViberVN Bot. No API key required. Disclosure — search queries, submitted URLs and explicitly approved local file uploads go to the public markdown.new service; needs the companion markdown-new CLI (uv tool install from the same repo tag), which the plugin runs as a subprocess with the ViberVN Bot process environment.

name: markifact
description: Run Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, GA4, Shopify, HubSpot and 50+ more platforms through Markifact's hosted MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with ten skills (operating protocol, write-safety rules, campaign launch, creative rotation, negative sweeps, diagnosis); remote streamable-http with OAuth 2.1 and dynamic client registration, so no Node.js or API keys. Disclosure: creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets; every write is a separate approval-gated operation and the skills instruct confirm-before-spend, but that is enforced by the skills and the server's approval flag, not by ViberVN Bot.

name: max-platform
description: MAX messenger gateway with polling/webhook, streaming, interactive questions, native attachments, Core voice transcription, optional PNG tables and a Desktop sessions sidebar. Disclosure — sends the bot token and message/file content to the MAX Bot API (platform-api2.max.ru) and MAX upload hosts (*.max.ru, *.oneme.ru, *.okcdn.ru). Inbound attachments are downloaded only for allowlisted senders, with SSRF protection, and cached under VIBERVNBOT_HOME. The bundled Russian Trusted Root CA is trusted only by the MAX API/upload clients, not attachment downloads. Its platform hint lets the agent attach local host files to MAX replies via MEDIA paths, and a public output hook adds a filename caption to file-only MAX replies. Webhook mode opens a listener (default 0.0.0.0:8646) that requires a secret and public HTTPS. Polling startup deletes all of the bot's webhook subscriptions. Optional table rendering launches Playwright/Chromium; with MAX_AUTO_INSTALL_PLAYWRIGHT=true it pip-installs playwright==1.62.0 and downloads Chromium (~115 MB). The MAX allowlist does not honour ViberVN Bot pairing approvals. No telemetry or self-update.

name: mcp-plugin-creator
description: Turn any MCP server into a portable Agent Plugin (mcp.json + workflow skill) built from evidence: the server's self-description, your past sessions with it, its docs and a read-only probe. Validates and installs the package in linked mode, and checks a built plugin for server drift and new errors in use. Disclosure: starts the target MCP server to introspect it; reads this profile's state.db read-only; logs redacted mcp__* call summaries locally (log_calls: false turns it off); inline server launches, writes outside its data dir and installs ask for approval.

name: mem-os
description: Local-first persistent memory: store durable facts once and recall them in any session. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): the @mem-os/sdk MCP server (pinned 1.6.26) over npx stdio, plus the mem-os-memory skill covering when to store and when to recall. All data stays in a local SQLite database under the user home directory; no cloud, no telemetry, no API keys. Server cwd is ${PLUGIN_DATA} so nothing is written into the install tree. Needs Node.js and npm on PATH.

name: mem0
description: Mem0 memory provider — server-side LLM fact extraction with semantic search, automatic deduplication and opt-in reranking, in platform, self-hosted or local OSS mode. Maintained by Mem0; the same provider that shipped in-tree. Disclosure — conversation turns and recall queries go to the configured Mem0 backend (api.mem0.ai in platform mode); at this pin the mem0ai library's anonymous PostHog usage telemetry stays on unless MEM0_TELEMETRY=false is set; `vibervnbot memory setup` can start Docker (pgvector) and Ollama containers for local mode.

name: memanto
description: Memanto memory agent — typed long-term memory (remember/recall/answer) with auto-recall, turn capture, and RAG answers. Disclosure — each user turn (as a recall query), completed user+assistant turns, ViberVN Bot memory writes and memanto_answer questions are sent to Moorcheh cloud (api.moorcheh.ai) under a per-profile agent namespace by default; requires MOORCHEH_API_KEY; settings in $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/memanto.json.

name: memex8
description: Self-hosted vector memory (Qdrant + TurboQuant compression) with auto-discovered knowledge realms, semantic search across conversations and ingested documents, and a slumber pipeline for memory consolidation. v1.1.0 adds optional per-session injection dedup with char-budget gate, decision/evaluation memory-type promotion (slower decay for load-bearing turns), prompt-injection sanitization on read, configurable system-prompt template, export/import memories as JSON, and a /memex8 slash command. New memory behaviours are opt-in; /memex8 export|import is confined to $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugin-data/memex8 unless enable_export_import=true. Disclosure — auto-stores a truncated copy (first 300 chars) of every user and assistant turn, plus per-message previews of the whole transcript at session end and before context compression, to the memex8 server at MEMEX8_BASE_URL (self-hosted; default http://localhost:8080) using MEMEX8_API_KEY.

name: memlock
description: Reasserts pinned standing instructions after context compaction. Disclosure — scope=global pins apply to every session sharing the same VIBERVNBOT_HOME; memlock_setup.py edits config.yaml and .claude/settings.json (with backups) only when you run it.

name: memobase
description: Memobase memory provider — self-hosted user profile + event timeline recall, with hybrid BM25/vector/entity retrieval and automatic per-turn prefetch.

name: memoria
description: Memoria Cloud memory provider with scoped recall, explicit memory tools and opt-in background capture. Disclosure — sends recall queries and explicit memory operations to api.thememoria.ai by default (or a configured self-hosted origin). When enabled, auto capture uploads completed user/assistant text for fact extraction, excluding tool results and media. A local SQLite outbox stores pending text; credentials are resolved through the active ViberVN Bot profile's MEMORIA_API_KEY secret.

name: memory-review
description: Checkbox staged memory writes and approve or reject the selection from a dialog.

name: memory-rewind
description: Automatic version history for the built-in memory (MEMORY.md, USER.md), SOUL.md and skills/ (including curator-archived skills): browse, diff and restore any past version with `vibervnbot memory-rewind`, or view it from any chat with the read-only `/memory-history`. Works alongside the built-in memory; not a memory provider. Disclosure — runs the local git binary (isolated from the user's git config, hooks and signing) to keep a bare repository in $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugin-data/memory-rewind/; reads only the tracked files (never .env, auth.json, databases or skills/.hub/); rewrites tracked files only when the user runs `restore`; no network.

name: memory-shield
description: Keeps your agent from rewriting or wiping what it remembers about you: by default the agent may add facts to the owner profile (USER.md) wherever it may write and may correct one only when the owner asks in a direct chat, the CLI or a trusted chat, and nobody may delete one; the agent's notes (MEMORY.md) cannot be deleted; group chats are read-only except for the people and owner-only chats you trust, and once trusted_users is set a direct chat with anyone not listed is read-only too; ViberVN Bot' unattended background review may not touch the owner profile. Block, ask through ViberVN Bot' approval prompt or just log, and undo edits and deletions from snapshots. Disclosure — no network calls, credentials, shell commands or background processes. One pre_tool_call hook reads the turn's platform, chat type, chat id and name, sender id and name and the cron flag (gateway.session_context) and whether the run is ViberVN Bot' unattended review (tools.skill_provenance.is_unattended_review), checks memory tool calls, and checks write_file, patch, terminal and execute_code calls only for a write into, or a removal of, USER.md, MEMORY.md or the memory folder (reading a memory file or copying it elsewhere passes in calls up to 16 KB; a longer call that names them is refused); mode approve asks through ViberVN Bot' approval gate in the owner's direct chats and the CLI and blocks in shared chats, cron and direct chats with people not in trusted_users. Writes plugin-data/memory-shield/audit.jsonl (the last 500 refused or flagged writes: time, chat, sender and a 160-character excerpt) and snapshots/ (full copies of USER.md and MEMORY.md taken right before an allowed edit or deletion, 20 per file by default). Reads the memory files and holds the memory store's lock files while it reads or writes them (not on Windows); /memory-shield restore overwrites one memory file. /memory-shield log and restore answer only in direct chats, the CLI and trusted_chats, and once trusted_users is set only the people listed there (a session without a user id, such as the CLI, counts as the owner); /memory-shield, snapshots and whoami answer in any chat with settings, counts, times, sizes and the caller's own id, name and chat key.

name: memory-zvec
description: Community Zvec memory backend for ViberVN Bot - in-process HNSW + RocksDB FTS store with native hybrid retrieval and session-safe lock governance; embeddings via any Ollama-compatible endpoint (local Ollama bge-m3 by default).

name: memtomem
description: Markdown-first long-term memory shared across your coding agents: a local memtomem MCP server plus six memory skills (index, recall, remember, search, setup, status). Notes live in ~/.memtomem and are searchable from ViberVN Bot, Claude Code, Codex CLI and Kimi Code. Runs at user scope. Disclosure — the server is launched with `uvx --python 3.12` and downloaded from PyPI (memtomem[onnx]==0.6.9) on first start, with Python 3.12 if uv cannot find one; it runs as a stdio MCP server for the session and reads the directories you ask it to index. With a fresh BM25-only configuration nothing else leaves the machine; an existing memtomem configuration may enable Hugging Face model downloads, a remote embedding or LLM provider, Cohere reranking or search webhooks. At startup the server also reads the nearest .env found upward from its installed location inside uv's cache (normally ~/.env), setting variables not already present, outside ViberVN Bot's MCP environment filtering.

name: mermail
description: Privacy-first agent email inboxes and workspace automation through hosted Mermail MCP. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/, seventeen skills bundled); authenticate with OAuth via `vibervnbot mcp login mermail`. No credentials are stored in mcp.json. Disclosure — the bundled skills also expose Mermail's paybox wallet tools over the hosted MCP (x402 payments, xStocks trading, standing grants); the skills allow the agent to move funds without a same-turn confirmation when your message already states exact terms, so spending controls live on your Mermail account, not in ViberVN Bot.

name: metamask-wallet
description: MetaMask Agent Wallet for ViberVN Bot — chat-only setup, reads, and approval-gated transfers/swaps/signatures, a gated Guard Mode policy editor, and a background 2FA watcher. Keys stay in MetaMask.

name: metronix
description: Metronix memory provider for ViberVN Bot with prefetch recall and built-in memory write-through.

name: microsoft365
description: Pre-release Microsoft 365 Graph tools for Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive, Calendar, Teams, To Do, and Planner.

name: mindgraph
description: MindGraph — semantic graph memory with hybrid retrieval, goal/decision tracking, and cross-document synthesis.

name: minecraft-platform
description: Minecraft gateway adapter for ViberVN Bot. Spawns a Mineflayer bot that joins a Minecraft server, wanders around, and relays chat messages between players and the ViberVN Bot agent. Supports offline and Microsoft-authenticated accounts.

name: minimax-image
description: MiniMax image generation -- Image-01 models via MiniMax platform. Supports text-to-image and image-to-image with subject reference.

name: minimax-search
description: MiniMax web search via the Token Plan API — keyed, no CAPTCHA

name: minimax-video
description: MiniMax (Hailuo) video generation -- Hailuo 2.3/02 and S2V-01 models via MiniMax platform. Async task API. Supports text-to-video, image-to-video, and subject-reference-to-video.

name: mistral-vibe
description: Direct Mistral Vibe subscription access — browser PKCE login, dedicated credential pool, account-visible catalog discovery, relay-verified reasoning_effort for GLM models. Disclosure — unofficial, not affiliated with Mistral. "vibervnbot auth add mistral-vibe" runs a browser PKCE sign-in against Mistral's Vibe console endpoints (console.mistral.ai/api/vibe/*) and stores the returned API key in the ViberVN Bot credential pool (auth.json, slice mistral-vibe), or uses MISTRAL_VIBE_API_KEY. Prompts and model listing go only to api.mistral.ai/v1. Vibe subscription coverage of API use is not guaranteed and may bill as pay-as-you-go. Logout clears the local pool but does not revoke the key remotely.

name: mixar
description: Mixar's own desktop MCP server over stdio, with a Mixar workflow skill: build and edit 3D scenes, generate models, textures, rigs and animation with AI, render, and export game-ready assets for Unity, Unreal and Godot. Requires Mixar 4.2.1+ on macOS, Windows or Linux, signed in with Connect MCP turned on, on the same computer as ViberVN Bot. Disclosure — runs the launcher the installed Mixar app writes at ~/.mixar/connector/mixar-mcp (%USERPROFILE%\.mixar\connector\mixar-mcp.cmd on Windows), which reads Mixar's own files under ~/.mixar/; tools execute arbitrary Python inside Mixar with your privileges; a tool call can start the installed Mixar app, which stays open after ViberVN Bot exits; calls go over loopback to Mixar, which forwards them to api.mixar.app under the signed-in account; generation prompts and reference images go to the AI provider running the chosen model; Mixar's backend keeps diagnostic records of MCP tool calls (inputs and results) and deletes them within 30 days; AI generation and create_layered_material spend Mixar credits, declared to ViberVN Bot as cost ranges with a 500-credit spend limit per chat; the plugin stores no credentials, ships no binaries, sends no telemetry and never updates itself; the optional MIXAR_MCP_LAUNCHER variable makes it run the program it names; at install ViberVN Bot looks for Mixar (macOS: Mixar.app in /Applications and ~/Applications; Windows: the installed-apps entry or %ProgramFiles%\Mixar; Linux: a mixar command on PATH or Mixar's launcher) and refuses the install when it is missing or, on macOS and Windows, older than 4.2.1.

name: mnemostack
description: Persistent agent memory over a mnemostack service or a local Qdrant — hybrid recall (vector + lexical + graph), verbatim capture with self-echo suppression, and soft retraction. Multi-tenant when pointed at a shared authenticated service; the tenant is resolved server-side from the service key. Disclosure — the pinned directory is a discovery shim; the provider code installs from PyPI at the version pinned in plugin.yaml pip_dependencies (vibervnbot-mnemostack==1.0.3) into the ViberVN Bot venv. Configured via MNEMOSTACK_* env vars; no key is required for a purely local Qdrant setup.

name: mnemosyne
description: Local-first memory layer for ViberVN Bot — SQLite with vector + FTS5 hybrid recall, episodic consolidation, temporal knowledge graph. Zero cloud. Disclosure — the mnemosyne_remember_media tool refuses local file paths unless MNEMOSYNE_MEDIA_ALLOWED_PATHS is set and sends media only to an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint when modality_enabled is on; video uses ffmpeg/ffprobe from PATH; the embedding model (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) downloads from Hugging Face on first use.

name: mnemosyne-dashboard
description: Local-only web dashboard for browsing and visualising Mnemosyne memories, triples, stats, and consolidation history.

name: mnemoverse
description: Persistent memory for agents, shared across tools: save preferences, decisions and lessons and recall them later by natural-language search; rating a recalled memory as helpful or misleading re-ranks what comes back next; shared rooms (beta) let several people's agents work from one memory. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) pointing at the hosted Mnemoverse MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR); the two bundled skills load under a namespaced name. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; ViberVN Bot runs no code from the package (scripts/ holds the repository's own CI checks). Every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.mnemoverse.com (authorization server auth.mnemoverse.com, browser sign-in on console.mnemoverse.com); memories the agent writes are stored in the signed-in user's Mnemoverse account, and recalled memories are pulled into the session context. OAuth tokens are held and refreshed by ViberVN Bot, never by the package. No telemetry, background process or self-update code.

name: mock-review
description: Review boards for UI mockups. The agent builds a board from a decisions.json file and your prototype pages; you open it on desktop or phone, mark each decision approve, change or skip, pin comments on the mocks and press Send, and your agent wakes up with the feedback as a markdown digest. Four mock_review tools, the `vibervnbot mockreview` CLI and slash command, and a bundled usage skill. Boards are served from your computer (loopback by default, or your tailnet) or published on here.now. Disclosure — when autostart is on (off until `vibervnbot mockreview setup`), a board web server (127.0.0.1:8790 by default) and one worker thread run inside the gateway process; setting host to 0.0.0.0 exposes every review to your network with no login. Outbound calls: a signed POST to the local ViberVN Bot webhook (localhost:8644) on Send, and, only for reviews hosted on here.now, https://here.now/api/v1 with your HERENOW_API_KEY. Secrets are read through ViberVN Bot's secret scope only. Runs `bash publish.sh` from the official here-now skill (key in the child environment), `tailscale status --json` and `tailscale serve status --json` (read only; on macOS the Tailscale app's own binary if the symlink crashes) for tailnet hosting, and from `setup` the vibervnbot subcommands `--version`, `gateway status`, `config get/set/unset`, `webhook subscribe`, `webhook remove` (only for a stale self-delivering route, after you confirm) and `plugins validate`. Reviews are stored under $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/workspace/mock-reviews. No telemetry, no update check, no Python dependencies.

name: model-drift-watch
description: Scheduled check that the model you use in ViberVN Bot has not quietly got worse: 34 fixed, exactly graded questions (reasoning, instruction following, Japanese, plus your own) run through ViberVN Bot cron, each run tested against the same model's own baseline with an exact per-question test and a same-day confirmation run, and a message only for a confirmed drop, a changed served model or a failed measurement. Not yet tried against a real LLM API (checked with a local mock model and real ViberVN Bot cron). Disclosure — each check calls your own model through ctx.llm on your bill, capped per check by the plugin (default 120,000 tokens / $0.50, no daily cap; the agent can start checks itself via the model_drift tool, and the scheduled agent turn is extra); price lookup goes through ViberVN Bot's pricing code (may fetch OpenRouter/models.dev prices); 10 optional code questions, off by default, run model-written Python in a limited child process (not a hostile-code sandbox) including in unattended cron runs when enabled; `schedule` creates one ViberVN Bot cron job that survives plugin removal (run `unschedule` first); writes run history to plugin-data/model-drift-watch; no telemetry.

name: model-leaderboard
description: Model leaderboard for ViberVN Bot Desktop: a full /model-leaderboard page that ranks any OpenRouter model for a chosen ViberVN Bot profile — context window, prices, Artificial Analysis indices and curated SWE-bench Verified / LiveCodeBench — with per-profile criteria, six score views (cards, table, score bars, histograms, heatmap, quality-vs-cost Pareto frontier), an OpenRouter news feed (new models, price changes, promos) and a documented REST surface under /api/plugins/model-leaderboard/. Disclosure — outbound HTTPS to OpenRouter's public model API (catalogue and pricing) on a 60 s poll and a forced refresh every 10 minutes while the page is visible, and to Hugging Face's public model API (safetensors metadata, for parameter counts) on demand and cached; reads the installed ViberVN Bot profiles' own config.yaml files once, to seed the tracked list from the models those profiles declare; keeps its state in <vibervnbot home>/plugin-data/model-leaderboard/ (seeded from the JSON shipped with the plugin), which LLM_DASH_DATA / LLM_DASH_CACHE_TTL can move or tune; the optional "Auto-fill criteria" action runs on the host LLM facade (ctx.llm.complete_structured), so it spends the user's configured model tokens; ships one read-only skill (model-leaderboard:refresh-benchmarks) whose only write is a POST to its own /benchmarks route; no API keys of its own, no writes outside its data directory.

name: model-picker
description: Per-turn cost classifier across three model tiers (Quick / Standard / Expert): rates each user turn from configurable best_for lists and rewrites the outgoing request's model through the llm_request middleware, biased to keep the previous tier unless the turn changes shape, with escalate_model for tool failures. Disclosure — the plugin rewrites the model field of every outgoing request for a classified session, picking between three configured model ids that must all belong to the session's own provider (a foreign-provider tier is refused and the session model stands); it makes one bounded auxiliary classifier call through the host's plugin LLM route on each classified turn (up to about 12,000 characters of recent conversation plus the prompt), reading its model ids from config.json next to the plugin, MODEL_PICKER_CONFIG, or MODEL_PICKER_* env, and falls back to the host's primary model; routing decisions, with the first 120 characters of each classified prompt, are logged to $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/logs/model-picker.log; a classifier-driven tier change can ask the context engine to compact the transcript before the switch, and escalate_model replaces the next request's context with a model-written handoff summary plus the recent tail; that engine registers only when the host config sets context.engine: model-picker.

name: model-router
description: Explicit per-profile readiness and native missing-profile preparation; Python installation remains per profile, never automatic on refresh. Profile model settings, default-on Heavy/Light task routing, fallback controls, runtime limits and Fast inheritance. Reads ViberVN Bot profile configuration; explicit saves update selected profiles via the native CLI. Routed jobs launch background ViberVN Bot children using the user's configured providers/MCP and store private prompts/results locally. No separate credential store, telemetry, self-updater or approval bypass. Disclosure — after you trust and enable the plugin, routing defaults ON for every installed profile without a saved choice, including profiles that installed an earlier version and never saved one (the update turns it on); existing saved OFF and explicit skill opt-outs remain OFF. On enabled profiles, the model-callable `coding_route` tool starts detached background ViberVN Bot agents. They get file, terminal and code-execution tools in any existing folder the model names, run under that profile's credentials and approval policy (single-query mode: dangerous commands are refused unless `approvals.single_query_mode: approve`), and their per-job time limit can be set to none. Prompts and results are stored in `plugin-data/model-router/jobs/`. Saving settings writes model, delegation, auxiliary, fallback and `skills.disabled` keys into the config.yaml of the profiles listed in the preview (backups are taken first) and copies a skill into those profiles' `skills/` folders. The Desktop "prepare profiles" action, after you select profiles and confirm, installs and enables this same catalog pin in up to 32 other local profiles through ViberVN Bot's plugin manager, where routing then defaults ON. From install, native subagents inherit the parent session's Fast (priority/ultrafast) tier on first-party OpenAI/Codex routes, which can raise costs.

name: model-usage-status
description: Provider-native Claude and Codex remaining allowance windows in the ViberVN Bot Desktop status bar. Disclosure — spawns the local `codex app-server` and `claude auth status` CLIs and reads the Claude OAuth token read-only through ViberVN Bot core; the optional install.sh (not part of the catalog install) edits the statusLine in ~/.claude/settings.json; macOS only.

name: modernisation-engine
description: Controlled migration engine: maps an existing codebase, turns the behaviour that must survive into reviewable contracts, prepares a separate candidate and records old/new evidence before any production change. Disclosure — 27 tools plus a `vibervnbot modernise` CLI and `/modernise` slash command; `assess`, `plan`, `record` and `recipe` read source trees and files at absolute paths the agent supplies (refusing symlinks, `.env`, `auth.json`, `credentials.json` and SSH keys) and never import or run repository code; `recipe` creates a new directory at an agent-chosen absolute path holding a copy of the source with fixed metadata edits; job records live under the plugin's data directory; only after you set `operator_config` and sign a one-use Ed25519 owner grant do `run`, `cancel` and `recover` invoke the local `docker` CLI, outside ViberVN Bot's command-approval prompt, to run, inspect and remove rootless, network-disabled, read-only, resource-limited containers from digest-pinned images you allow-list (never pulled); no network calls, no telemetry, no self-updater.

name: monid
description: Connect your agent to third-party tools and APIs (web search and scraping, people and company data, social media, media generation, email and phone) through one integration. The agent discovers, compares and runs tools at runtime, paid per call from one Monid balance. Disclosure — Monid (monid.ai, by Monid / monid-ai) is a paid third-party marketplace: the agent installs the @monid-ai/cli npm package or connects to mcp.monid.ai, sends your requests and any uploaded files to Monid and on to its providers, and each run spends your prepaid Monid workspace balance. The "confirm the price first" step is an instruction to the model in the bundled skill, not a ViberVN Bot approval prompt, unless you add `trust: untrusted` to `mcp_servers.monid`.

name: morning-briefing
description: Personal daily newspaper for ViberVN Bot: gathers weather, calendar, AQI, curated 36-hour news (timestamped Reddit RSS + X + web search, per-story QR codes), and newsletter digests, renders one 8.5x11 newsprint page, and prints it every morning via a cron job.

name: mrscraper
description: MrScraper page retrieval, Google search, and account usage via direct HTTP APIs. Disclosure — page and search requests can consume paid account tokens; target URLs, search queries, and request options are sent to MrScraper.

name: ms-decision-provider
description: Microsoft-Decision-1 (Azure AI Foundry System One) decision provider for bounded agent decisions. Registers typed-decision tools (decision_noul, decision_choice, decision_score, decide) that preserve full probability distributions, plus an opt-in pre_tool_call hook that requests human approval for known-risk calls without sending their arguments to Azure. Reference implementation of the typed decision-provider runtime in #113008. Disclosure — the four decision tools send the caller-supplied state/questions text to the Azure Foundry endpoint you set in AZURE_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL (nothing is sent while it is unset); with MS_DECISION_GATE=1 the pre_tool_call gate sends only a coarse operation label for known-risk tool calls to that endpoint and routes them to ViberVN Bot's human approval prompt (MS_DECISION_GATE_MODE=block hard-denies instead); the labelled eval corpus under tests/ contains literal destructive commands as should-refuse examples.

name: my-github
description: Desktop and dashboard plugin: statusbar chip, palette command, and dashboard tab listing your GitHub repos (public + private) via the gh CLI.

name: mybot-farm
description: Search mybot.farm, plant/reinstall ViberVN Bot packs (Desktop Recruit + CLI), and post GAF listings. Disclosure — plants third-party ViberVN Bot profiles (config, SOUL, skills, memories) from mybot.farm sellers with no hash pinning; force/clean delete profiles.

name: myswarm
description: Discover, visualize, sanitize/export, and import community agents.md swarm configurations. Outputs abbreviated agent/persona/goal tables, renders ASCII topology diagrams (.svg and .png images + portable 7-bit copy-paste ASCII symbol blocks), generates rich themed swarm illustrations across 12 curated signature themes and orthogonal intensity levels (understated, normal, overstated) via ViberVN Bot default model and image_generate, exports sanitized agents.md files, and imports/reverts shared configs with on-screen file preview and best-effort import warnings; every import/revert asks for approval. Disclosure — myswarm_import/myswarm_revert replace the workspace AGENTS.md/agents.md (a file ViberVN Bot loads into every session's system prompt) after a ViberVN Bot approval prompt; choosing "always" approves all later imports. The import security check is a best-effort regex + model warning, not a security boundary — only import files you trust. Swarm file contents are sent to your configured model for parsing and PII scrubbing (also best-effort; review exports before sharing), and myswarm_visualize_image calls your configured image_generate provider (may cost credits). Adds a ~2.8k-character MySwarm guidance section to every session's system prompt. Writes myswarm-ascii.svg/.png and .md exports into the current folder (exports may overwrite an existing .md file there), plus a .agents.md.myswarm.orig sidecar, and keeps import backups under VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugin-data/myswarm/.

name: nachos
description: Durable memory and context compression for ViberVN Bot with local SQLite or flat-file storage. Disclosure — replaces the memory provider (memory.provider: nachos) and, only when context.engine: nachos is set, the context engine; the provider injects a system-prompt block telling the agent to use the nachos_memory_* tools and keep built-in memory disabled; opt-in semantic ranking either runs a separately installed nachos-embeddings CLI or sends the turn query plus memory titles/summaries to api.openai.com with OPENAI_API_KEY; all storage is local under $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/nachos/.

name: needs-you
description: ViberVN Bot is waiting — full Desktop page for pending approvals. Queue, chip, OS notify. Redacted previews only. No API keys.

name: nerve
description: Nerve is a supervisory nervous system for ViberVN Bot with provider-neutral Jev, Laya, and OpenJev Reflex backends, evidence-backed Kanban supervision, context governance, token-budget trajectory control, and durable SSH workers. Disclosure — the default Reflex backend is hosted Jev; with the default settings (enabled / admission_enabled on) each turn's user prompt (up to 12k characters) and redacted tool/result previews are sent to the configured Jev provider (OpenRouter Decisions / TypeSafe Jev) using your OPENROUTER_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_API_KEY, spending your credits on every turn. Laya and OpenJev can be configured as local/self-hosted backends. The operator-only nerve setup CLI can copy a local VibervnbotContextBus checkout into VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugins/vibervnbot-context-bus and runs vibervnbot plugins enable/disable for that plugin when a profile is saved; the model cannot trigger this.

name: netmind-provider
description: NetMind OpenAI-compatible model provider with a bundled model catalog. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests go to https://api.netmind.ai/inference-api/v1 through ViberVN Bot' own client with NETMIND_API_KEY, which ViberVN Bot reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

name: next-prompt
description: Suggests your next message after each turn as a pill under the Desktop composer: your likely answer when the agent asks you something, or the natural next step.

name: next-steps
description: Next-step suggestions under the ViberVN Bot Desktop composer after each turn: local Ollama inference, per-session state, target routing (session, new tab, bots, kanban), tiny-model capacity profiles, EN/DE UI. No API keys. Disclosure — after every agent turn, sends the last 8 messages (each cut to 200 chars) plus the working directory to Ollama on localhost; clicking a suggestion immediately submits it as a prompt in the current session, a new session, or another profile's session, or creates a kanban card, and for non-current targets also attaches the working directory and the last 6 messages (on by default, can be turned off under Targets).

name: nextcloud-talk
description: Signed Nextcloud Talk bot webhooks and text replies for ViberVN Bot, with JSON/XML OCS support. Disclosure — runs an HTTP webhook listener (default 0.0.0.0:8788, HMAC-verified with the bot secret) and sends messages and optional Basic-auth room lookups to your Nextcloud server; registers the `nextcloud_talk` gateway platform.

name: nextcloud-talk-platform
description: Nextcloud Talk platform adapter for ViberVN Bot, in two modes behind one plugin: a webhook bot (Nextcloud Talk Bot API, HMAC-SHA256 signed, with an explicit body-size cap and a nonce-replay cache ahead of payload parsing) and a real Nextcloud user account (app password, long-polling the Chat REST API, with federation-invite support, per-room mention/watch/free modes, and an agent-to-agent loop guard plus active-listening context for multi-agent rooms). Mode is picked automatically by which credential is configured. No extra SDKs -- aiohttp for bot mode, httpx for user mode, both already ViberVN Bot dependencies. Disclosure — Connects to your Nextcloud server either as a Talk bot (HMAC-verified webhook listener, 127.0.0.1:18797 by default) or as a real Nextcloud user with an app password (long-polls the Chat API and auto-accepts federation invites only from NEXTCLOUD_TALK_ALLOWED_INVITERS); in user mode, unanswered room messages from allowed senders (up to 40 per room by default) and, for rooms listed in NEXTCLOUD_TALK_ROOM_MODES or with room_rules_all_rooms on, the room description are added to the agent's next turn in that room.

name: nextdns
description: Read-only NextDNS tools - DNS query logs, blocked queries with the blocklist that matched, and aggregate analytics by domain, device, blocklist or protocol. For triaging DNS problems and answering "was this blocked, and by what". Uses the official NextDNS API; makes no configuration changes.

name: nexus
description: Self-hosted long-term memory on Qdrant: automatic per-turn prefetch and write-back, plus recall/remember/forget, guardrail rules and a knowledge graph; ViberVN Bot and any MCP-connected agent share one collection. Embeddings run fully local by default (sentence-transformers with Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 1024d, about 1.2 GB from Hugging Face on first use; on Apple Silicon the model is pinned to the CPU, because PyTorch's MPS backend aborts the whole process under two overlapping encodes). A cloud embedder runs only when NEXUS_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER names it and its key is present, and a key that merely sits in the environment never selects one. Access levels fail closed: a memory, a protection rule or a graph label without a known level counts as the most restrictive. A local service on 127.0.0.1:9122 serves embeddings and the full MCP toolset; its /embed and /mcp routes demand a per-installation key (service_auth.key, mode 0600) and reject non-loopback Host/Origin, while the open /healthz answers liveness only. The plugin starts that service when ViberVN Bot cannot load the embedding stack, and it keeps running afterwards. Session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint from ViberVN Bot config.yaml, and the consolidation daemon to its configured model, which defaults to ViberVN Bot's own default model through local Ollama; reads ~/.vibervnbot/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 opts into a GitHub release check. Disclosure — when ViberVN Bot cannot load the embedding stack (and always on Apple Silicon unless NEXUS_EMBED_IN_HOST=1), the plugin starts `nexus-memory serve` on 127.0.0.1:9122 (embeddings, the full Nexus MCP toolset and a consolidation daemon that sends memory text to the Ollama endpoint at 127.0.0.1:11434 or NEXUS_OLLAMA_BASE under the model named by NEXUS_CONSOLIDATION_MODEL, nexus-memory.consolidation_model or ViberVN Bot's model.default, which can be an Ollama cloud model), and the service keeps running after ViberVN Bot exits; its /embed and MCP routes require a per-install key in ~/.nexus-memory/service_auth.key (0600) and a loopback Host/Origin; session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint in ViberVN Bot config.yaml, and the opt-in recall reranker (nexus-memory.rerank or NEXUS_RERANK=1) defaults to sending each query plus up to 20 memory snippets to that same endpoint using the provider API key it reads from config.yaml; reads ~/.vibervnbot/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; opt-in NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 adds a GitHub release check and an upgrade nudge to the system prompt.

name: ngrok-ai-gateway
description: The ngrok AI Gateway as a ViberVN Bot model provider (`--provider ngrok`, or ngrok AI Gateway in `vibervnbot model`): one access key for all your model providers, with failover. The model list comes live from your gateway, and gateway errors (unrouted model, access-policy and upstream-key failures, out of credit) map onto ViberVN Bot' fallback instead of a generic error. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1 (or NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_BASE_URL) through ViberVN Bot' own client with NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_KEY, which ViberVN Bot reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

name: nine-balance-widget
description: Nine AI provider balances in one desktop widget — live balance/usage and quota reads, token-based spend estimates with off-peak price windows, drop alerts, and an anime mascot per provider with rotating flavour lines (DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, Kimi, MiMo, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok). Fully English UI. Desktop-only: desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Keys are entered in the widget's settings page and stored in plugin-scoped storage; the widget only calls those providers' official APIs. Ported from MeteorNOX/DeepSeek-Balance-Whale-Widget (MIT). Disclosure — API keys you enter in the widget's settings are stored in plaintext in Desktop plugin storage (not ViberVN Bot' secret store); while the widget is on, the Desktop renderer polls the balance/usage endpoint of the provider matching your current model every 60 s with that provider's key (api.deepseek.com, api.minimaxi.com / api.minimax.io, open.bigmodel.cn / api.z.ai, api.moonshot.cn / api.moonshot.ai, api.kimi.com, token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com, api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com with the key in the URL, api.x.ai); each key goes only to its own provider; draws a floating widget over the app window.

name: node-search
description: Bounded Markdown metadata+graph prefilter for configured local roots

name: nord-theme
description: Unofficial Nord theme for ViberVN Bot Desktop with hand-tuned Polar Night (dark) and Snow Storm (light) palettes, Nord terminal colors, Nord code-block syntax colors, and Aurora status colors. Scoped to its own theme; other themes are untouched. Disclosure — its stylesheet recolors Desktop surfaces, code-block syntax colors, status colors, selection and inline code only while Nord is selected, and it switches the active theme to Nord once on first enable; no network calls, file reads or shell commands.

name: nowstamp
description: Give the agent a clock. Appends the current date and time, plus the real gap since the previous message, to every user turn. Optional spaced-out timestamps on tool results for long runs.

name: ntfy-approval
description: Answer ViberVN Bot' approval prompts from your phone: once selected with security.approval.transport: ntfy, each dangerous-command prompt arrives as an ntfy push notification with Approve once, Approve for session and Deny buttons, and no answer still means deny. Disclosure — once selected, anyone who can read the ntfy topic can approve dangerous commands (the one-time answer codes are in the notification), so on the public ntfy.sh default the topic name is the only secret and NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN is optional; each pending approval publishes ViberVN Bot' reason, the redacted command (unless send_command is false), the non-default profile name and one-time answer codes to the configured ntfy server, then reads <topic>-reply and deletes the notification; any failure or timeout is a deny; reads NTFY_APPROVAL_TOPIC/NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN from the profile .env, never puts the token in a notification, follows no redirects, writes no files and starts no processes.

name: obsidian-memory
description: Browse, search, and edit Obsidian vault notes from the ViberVN Bot dashboard. Features force-directed graph visualization, multi-vault support, markdown rendering with wikilinks, and inline note editing.

name: oc-free-provider
description: Unofficial OpenCode Zen free-model transport for ViberVN Bot. Discovers live zero-cost tool-capable models by intersecting OpenCode Zen and models.dev over HTTPS, persists only the last successful intersection for restart fallback, and bidirectionally translates compatible OpenCode and ViberVN Bot tool schemas, calls, choices, and replayed history while ViberVN Bot executes tools locally. No OpenCode CLI, Node.js, npm, or npx dependency. Disclosure — prompts, tool schemas, tool results, and other conversation content leave the machine for OpenCode and the selected model provider; model availability, retention, data use, and permission are governed by their current terms.

name: office-3d
description: A live isometric office for ViberVN Bot Desktop: every profile is a person at a desk — a profile doing real work sits typing with a lit terminal screen, an online-but-idle one relaxes in the lounge with tea, an offline one leaves an empty desk with a dark monitor. Click a desk to inspect that profile (state, sessions, tokens, cost) and open its chat or latest session; a cost/tokens leaderboard ranks the profiles; plus a global Total/Working/Idle/Offline overview, a status-bar chip, a palette command with keybind, a settings page, and an office_status agent tool that reports the same status to the model. Disclosure — the backend and the tool read each profile's gateway_state.json and open its state.db read-only, running aggregate queries only (COUNT/SUM/MAX over the sessions table: counts, token totals, cost, last-activity); they never read message content, system prompts or titles, make no network calls, and need no credentials. Opening a profile's latest session asks the app's own session.list RPC for that session's id (metadata only) and then opens it through the app's own openSession; no message content is read. POSIX only (platforms: [linux, macos]) because the process-liveness check uses os.kill(pid, 0), which on Windows would terminate the target process.

name: office-desk
description: Guarded Word, PowerPoint and Excel editing: tracked Word changes and comments, slide and deck edits, and Excel edits with LibreOffice recalc. Every write gets a backup and a revertible receipt, and you review it all on a Desk page in the Desktop app. Settings are in Settings > Plugins. Disclosure: reads any Office file the agent is pointed at but writes only inside folders the user puts on the Desk (backups and receipts live in the plugin's own data dir). xlsx_recalc runs the user's installed LibreOffice (soffice, headless) on a temporary copy. The Desk page reads the session store read-only to show a workstream's chat. No network calls, telemetry, credentials or background processes. Depends on the paper-docx, paper-pptx and paper-xlsx forks. They provide the docx, pptx and openpyxl import names, so they must not share an environment with python-docx, python-pptx or openpyxl.

name: offpeak-bekci
description: Makes Ollama Cloud's off-peak window visible and actionable in ViberVN Bot: a desktop status-bar chip shows the countdown and the queue item counts (Ollama off-peak hours: weekdays 18:00-12:00 UTC, weekends one block), a one-shot notice fires 30 minutes before the window opens, and approval is taken only from the user (`/offpeak-onayla <id,id>`) — work runs only if approved, and items never enter the queue by themselves. `/offpeak-durum` prints a readable report by default (machine-readable JSON with `/offpeak-durum json`), and `/offpeak-kur` prints the cron job it would install in full plus a `plan_hash`; nothing is installed without a hash-bound approval typed by the user, and the plugin never writes the cron store. One `llm_execution` middleware measures the call rate for Ollama Cloud calls during the peak window and ships measure-only (`kuru_kosu: true`): it records what it would delay and never delays. No network calls, no telemetry, no credential reads; the only local files it touches are the queue ledger, its own JSONL measurement log, and a read-only look at the profile's cron/jobs.json. Output language is English by default; `dil: tr` selects Turkish. Auto-delivery is host-dependent: in a classic CLI session the request enters the agent queue; on the Ink TUI / desktop-panel host the core asks for a persistent `session_key`, which the command handler does not receive, so the command prints the parameters as a single line of JSON. Injecting into a gateway additionally requires `plugins.entries.offpeak-bekci.allow_gateway_injection: true` (default off); the only in-process way to read that key is the private `gateway.session_context` module (rule 9 -> not used). Requires ViberVN Bot >= 0.22.2. Disclosure — the llm_execution middleware can sleep Ollama Cloud calls during the peak window once `kuru_kosu: false` is set (default is measure-only); it writes a JSONL measurement log and, on `/offpeak-onayla`, rewrites the user's queue file; it reads the profile's cron/jobs.json read-only (on `/offpeak-durum`, `/offpeak-kaldir` and at every session end) to count enabled queue-consumer jobs; `/offpeak-kur` and `/offpeak-kaldir` leave cron install/removal requests in the session (or, with `allow_gateway_injection: true`, inject them into the gateway) for the agent's own cron tool to act on; no network calls, no credential reads, never writes the cron store.

name: omh
description: Oh My ViberVN Bot (OMH) bridge: routing hints and role context for OMH workflow skills, per-task delegation model routing, plan todos and a status tool, a ViberVN Bot Desktop status pane (off until enabled), bounded evidence probes that keep prepared work apart from observed results, and a file-backed memory provider. Disclosure — omh_delegate_route writes delegation.model/provider/reasoning_effort in $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/config.yaml and the session hooks restore them; omh_gather_evidence runs allowlisted checks (python -m unittest with reporting flags only, python -m compileall, git diff --check, omh doctor/probe/docs/release checks) via subprocess on the host, outside any sandboxed terminal backend and without ViberVN Bot' terminal approval, in the agent working directory or below it, so it runs whatever test code that directory holds; omh_team (only with the separate OMH core package installed) asks once through the ViberVN Bot approval prompt for an exact list of up to 8 check commands from an accepted plan, then runs them on the host as each helper returns; omh_jev_ask posts model-supplied state and questions to api.typesafe.ai (openrouter.ai only when the operator opts in via ~/.omh/jev/settings.json) with the user's own TYPESAFE_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY, only in a turn where the user names Jev; opt-in egress_attempts (re-registers chosen core tools, needs the operator's tool-override grant) and browser_adapter (vetoes core browser_* tools) settings; reads session and cost metadata from state.db read-only; state lives under ~/.omh and <project>/.omh.

name: omnivoice
description: OmniVoice TTS provider for ViberVN Bot

name: opaque-composer
description: Keep the desktop composer solid while scrolling so conversation text stays readable.

name: openai-compatible
description: GPT Image through CLIProxyAPI, New API, or any OpenAI Images-compatible gateway, with gateway-aware errors and requested-vs-returned size reporting. Disclosure — sends image prompts and any source images (local files, data URLs or public HTTPS URLs) to the OpenAI-compatible gateway base_url you configure, authenticated with OPENAI_COMPAT_IMAGE_API_KEY.

name: openalex
description: Scholarly search, citation traversal, grouped counts, and fulltext access through OpenAlex with session spending limits.

name: opencode-shepherd
description: Watch over opencode sessions from anywhere: alerts for stopped turns, questions and permissions, plus a dependency-free CLI to reply. Disclosure — the skill has the agent install the ocshepherd CLI from GitHub at a pinned commit and, after asking you, add a cron entry or systemd unit that polls your opencode server; the CLI talks to that server with the password you provide, can reply to its questions and permission prompts, and optionally sends alerts to Telegram or runs a notify command you configure.

name: openinvest
description: Self-hosted AI investment committee — skills for portfolio review, a decision ledger, and a 4-role LLM committee (macro / quant / risk / CIO) that debates a symbol. Disclosure — the skills run the openinvest backend from PyPI via uvx (pinned in run.sh) and keep portfolio, ledger, committee records and any keys you add in plaintext under ~/openInvest (or $INVEST_HOME); it fetches public market data and RSS news, and on the Direct path / daily report sends your portfolio and wealth context to the LLM you configure (default api.deepseek.com) and, if installed, to the agy or gemini CLI for a second opinion; news ingestion can trigger extra committee runs (LLM spend). The MCP tools are a server you add to config.yaml yourself (the printed snippet runs the plugin's pinned run.sh with `trust: untrusted`, so ViberVN Bot asks before ledger writes); buy/sell/deposit/withdraw only edit the local ledger — it never connects to a broker or places orders.

name: openltm
description: Long-term memory for ViberVN Bot agents, stored in a local SQLite database. FTS5 full-text search with optional vector (sqlite-vec) recall, importance-weighted decay, a queryable memory graph, and automatic capture: a declarative rule engine classifies corrections, constraints, preferences, decisions, and agent-discovered facts from a conversation and stores each one as a distilled, self-contained fact. Runtime notifications and read-only OpenLTM tool requests are excluded by named guards so ops noise never becomes memory. No cloud, no telemetry, no API keys required; optional semantic recall via a local llama.cpp embedding server. MIT licensed. Disclosure — local SQLite in VIBERVNBOT_HOME; runs git config to read the repo remote; memory text goes to Gemini or OpenAI embeddings, or to the llama.cpp server URL you set (default 127.0.0.1:8080), only if selected in openltm.json (default local Ollama)

name: openmail
description: Gives a ViberVN Bot agent its own email address. Inbound mail wakes the agent over a websocket, replies go out in-thread, plus tools for sending, reading and provisioning inboxes.

name: openpaths
description: OpenPaths model provider for ViberVN Bot: OpenAI-compatible inference at openpaths.io with auto, auto-easy-task, auto-medium-task, auto-hard-task and auto-think task-tier routes plus GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek models, live /models listing, and ViberVN Bot reasoning effort mapped to OpenPaths reasoning_effort. Disclosure — prompts, tool schemas, tool results and conversation context are sent to openpaths.io with your OPENPATHS_API_KEY and forwarded to the upstream model vendors it routes to; the plugin makes no other network calls and registers no tools or hooks.

name: openrouter-picker
description: One install: the Desktop model picker and the OR Picker composer provider. Checking a model here is what the composer lists. Disclosure — the optional OpenRouter management key is stored in plaintext in Desktop localStorage; the plugin reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY from your environment, ViberVN Bot secret store or VIBERVNBOT_HOME/.env and sends it only to openrouter.ai (credits, usage, and the Test-model button, which spends credits).

name: openrouter-spend
description: OpenRouter API-key spend and recorded chat costs in USD/INR. Disclosure — sends the configured OpenRouter key (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or the variable named in api_key_env) only to openrouter.ai's read-only key and generation accounting endpoints, and fetches public USD/INR rates from api.frankfurter.dev unless a manual rate is set; middleware on every LLM request records ids, model, token counts and reported cost (no prompt or reply text) to its own ledger; the dashboard reads accounting metadata (session ids, token counts, billing provider) read-only from the state.db and OpenRouter Spend ledger of every profile under the ViberVN Bot root.

name: openrouter-voice
description: OpenRouter speech-to-text and text-to-speech providers for ViberVN Bot (stt.provider / tts.provider = openrouter).

name: openspec
description: OpenSpec CLI tools for spec-driven development workflows

name: openviking
description: Long-term memory for ViberVN Bot. Capture conversations, recall useful facts across sessions and search your knowledge. Choose Quick Local, OpenViking Service (managed cloud) or your own server. Disclosure — conversation turns, tool results and MEMORY.md / USER.md edits are sent to the configured OpenViking server. Quick Local setup installs the newest OpenViking 0.5.x server release from PyPI at setup time (checked against PyPI's hash, not the version reviewed here; re-running setup upgrades it) plus a hash-pinned llama-cpp-python wheel and a local embedding model. It copies the active ViberVN Bot static LLM API key into a private file under the profile for extraction, and its localhost server keeps running after ViberVN Bot exits and after plugin removal (stop it with `vibervnbot openviking local stop`). Extraction can use a remote LLM. Custom localhost connections can start openviking-server from PATH with the profile environment minus ViberVN Bot bot, gateway, GitHub and dashboard secrets; model and tool API keys still pass.

name: operations
description: A ViberVN Bot Desktop page for running a fleet - topology, model traffic, handoffs, traces, merge requests and conformance checks in one place. Disclosure — reads vibervnbot-metrics-dash's <vibervnbot root>/metrics/metrics.db, the kanban board, every profile's config.yaml (plugin enable state, rolectl-mcp entries, default model) and plugin-data/gitlab-mr/device-aliases.json, all read-only; calls your GitLab (host and token from the plugin settings or GITLAB_HOST/GITLAB_TOKEN), the local model router (MODEL_ROUTER_URL, default 127.0.0.1:8867) and LM Studio (LMSTUDIO_URL, default 127.0.0.1:1234); runs git status/rev-parse/ls-files in the project folders it checks and shows matching lines (including any keys found) on the page. Page buttons create, assign, schedule, unblock and close kanban cards and start their workers at once, write <vibervnbot root>/conformance/conformance.yaml, and "Propose a rule" pushes a branch and opens a merge request on the standard's GitLab project. A hook on every kanban dispatcher tick starts cards scheduled from the page; with alert_target set it posts new attention items through vibervnbot send; with drift_action: automatic it files and starts a fix card for drift_profile for each drifting host with a verified report (at most daily) carrying the standard's remediate commands. With Activity summaries on (off by default), Activity sentences and each "Explain this session" click send log lines and trace details to the model set for the operations_summary auxiliary task. From the setup checklist's Connect GitLab step it can also adopt this profile's own login - its environment read through ViberVN Bot' secret scope, or the host the gitlab-mr plugin names - or take a host and token typed on the page; the host goes through the plugin-settings writer and the token through ViberVN Bot' .env credential route as OPERATIONS_GITLAB_TOKEN, and the token is never sent back to the page. No other credential store is read: a login that exists only in another profile's .env or in the glab CLI's config is typed in instead. Since 0.3.5 the plugin keeps its own metrics store: it tails <vibervnbot root>/metrics/requests.jsonl and moa-refs.jsonl, guardrail lines in logs/agent.log, logs/model-router-requests.jsonl and clientgate/clientgate-usage.jsonl (all read-only, offset-tracked) plus its own host probes (CPU and memory via sysctl/vm_stat or PowerShell, LM Studio's lms ps, and every five minutes the local conformance.yaml's install-stamp, launchd/scheduled-task, loopback-port and key-name checks), and reads session titles and costs from <vibervnbot root>/state.db and every profile's gateway_state.json (read-only), into <vibervnbot root>/metrics/operations.db, which this plugin alone writes and prunes to the metrics_retention_days setting (30/60/90 days or forever, chosen on the page and written through ViberVN Bot' plugin-settings writer); vibervnbot-metrics-dash's metrics.db is then only a read-only fallback until the own store holds data. It probes the local metrics dashboard's /api/about (METRICS_DASH_URL, default 127.0.0.1:8899, cached five minutes) to link to it rather than duplicate it, and every ViberVN Bot process that loads the plugin starts a daemon timer: when no kanban dispatcher tick has arrived for two minutes it runs the same sweep itself every 30 seconds (collection, alerts and, with drift_action: automatic, the fix cards), and the page says so; OPERATIONS_HEARTBEAT_TIMER=0 turns that timer off. Since 0.3.4 a failed model call is classified with the host app's own error classifier and shown with its cause and remedy commands; no new outbound call is made for that.

name: optchat
description: OptChat-style endless memory for ViberVN Bot: an append-only verbatim log plus a binary summary tree, exposed as recall through the MemoryProvider ABC. Background compactor builds the tree with a cheap auxiliary model (call_llm task optchat_compact); prefetch returns a fixed-budget view of the whole history; optchat_zoom/optchat_date tools open any line down to the verbatim message. Disclosure — every turn's user messages, agent replies, tool calls and tool results (each result capped at 30,000 characters, after ViberVN Bot's secret redaction) are appended permanently to unencrypted owner-only files under $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/optchat/, with no deletion or retention limit; a background compactor sends those messages and the surrounding summary view to your auxiliary model route (task optchat_compact) for summarization; each turn injects up to view_budget_chars (default 16,000) of that history into the model context.

name: optmem-vibervnbot
description: Independent ViberVN Bot integration of Victor Taelin's OptMem design: local, append-only memory with regex/BM25 recall and a bounded wake digest. Hybrid and guarded OptMem-only modes; verified migration and rollback. Local by default. Compaction is manual unless auto_nap is enabled. Optional LLM summaries run only when both auto_nap and llm_summary are on; they send memory blocks to the configured provider via host-owned authentication and may incur token costs. Summaries are lossy, raw records remain recoverable, and conflicts are not resolved automatically. Wake consumes model context. See README for upstream attribution. Disclosure — memory is stored locally under VIBERVNBOT_HOME; optional auto_nap+llm_summary sends stored memory lines to the user's configured model provider; the optmem-only mode (explicit CLI with --yes) disables ViberVN Bot' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md injection after a verified backup.

name: orbit-desktop
description: Your workspace, shaped by your agent: a bundled browser desktop powered by ViberVN Bot. Describe the workflow you need; the agent can rearrange windows and panes, customize appearance, build versioned sandboxed web apps, and refine your workspace with scoped control, previews and checkpoints. Illustrated examples show a project-specific COCS 3D asset viewer and OmniVoice experiment bench; these example apps and their backends are not bundled. Includes permission-controlled desktop agent-reply notifications (generic alerts while Orbit remains open; browser/OS restrictions apply) and 100,000-character chat messages, guidance and drafts. Includes Devplan Studio for guided interviews, specifications, phased devplans and circular-development handoff exports. Optional conversational interviews require explicit service setup and a working ViberVN Bot provider login, and send project context to that provider. Includes 14 distinctive interface presets including Atelier, with local wallpapers, themed icons and taskbar treatments. Agent chats include inline expandable tool activity, running/completed/failed summaries, an activity strip, a workspace agent overview and responsive toolbar controls. Missing tool-call IDs are explicitly uncorrelated. Embedded apps retain their own styling. Includes a reviewed GitHub app catalog with immutable source pins and a portable Live Telemetry package. Catalog sync (operator-run scripts/orbit_catalog.py, never triggered by the ViberVN Bot tool or at register) reads the entry list from the upstream repo's main branch at sync time and downloads third-party static app bundles at their per-entry commit pins; installed UI runs in a sandboxed iframe and never executes backend code. Optional telemetry backend staging downloads pinned Python; execution requires explicit host-code trust and separate private authenticated HTTPS setup. Backend code runs with owner privileges, not a sandbox. Disclosure — adapter talks only to the configured local Orbit server (loopback, Bearer capability from runtime_dir); mutations off by default. Optional orbit.py setup runs npm ci / node. Bundled VNC/Xpra launchers use the Orbit page's hostname and scheme; optional Linux apps require separate provisioning. Optional api.typesafe.ai requests require explicit consent and a user-supplied key. The 0.2.7 web app's opt-in Show tools panel displays tool call arguments and results for the current ViberVN Bot conversation, fetched from the local Orbit server and local ViberVN Bot session API and kept in the browser only.

name: orcaslicer
description: Prepare, slice, preflight and export 3D prints with stock OrcaSlicer profiles. Includes explicit printer upload/control, camera snapshots and monitoring through supported protocols. Protocol and hardware limits are documented. Independent of OrcaSlicer. Disclosure — executes the installed local slicer and exposes printer upload, start, pause, resume and cancel; agent-supplied confirmation is not independent human authentication. Printer/camera credentials are read from ORCA_*/VIBERVNBOT_ORCA_* environment variables named in tool arguments (HTTPS required unless allow_plaintext_credentials is set); plugin state lives in ~/.vibervnbot-orca (VIBERVNBOT_ORCA_HOME), outside VIBERVNBOT_HOME.

name: orquehelx
description: Per-call delegation across your own subscriptions. The model sends each subagent to a named route with delegate_to(route, goal, context); each route pins a provider ViberVN Bot already knows (Claude, Codex or Antigravity subscription plugins, ACP provider plugins) and a model. delegate_task, by contrast, uses the one target in config.yaml. Subagents launch through ctx.subagent_lifecycle. A child counts as out of quota only on an unambiguous provider error or a measured window at 100 %, and the route never switches on its own: a policy decides whether the parent asks you, picks another route, or waits. Disclosure: a pre_tool_call hook blocks delegate_task spawns while routes are configured (list/steer/stop pass); an api_request_error hook records quota errors in memory. Quota is read with ViberVN Bot' fetch_account_usage (Anthropic and OpenAI Codex) on /ohx quota and after a provider error. No other network egress, no files written.

name: osv-ref
description: @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: context references: attach a vulnerability record from OSV.dev to a message (summary, aliases, severity, affected packages with version ranges and fixed versions, details, references), with package data merged from up to four alias records. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/<id> only (the referenced id and up to four of its alias ids leave the machine); no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: reference providers.

name: parallel-search
description: Free web search and page fetching through Parallel's hosted MCP, with a setup skill bundled. No account or API key required. Queries and requested URLs are sent to Parallel. Adds direct MCP tools alongside ViberVN Bot's native web providers.

name: parcel-deliveries
description: Track package deliveries with the Parcel app (parcelapp.net). List what's on the way, add tracking numbers and look up carrier codes, with a built-in guard for Parcel's strict rate limits. Disclosure — sends tracking numbers, descriptions and optional postcode/order email to api.parcel.app (Parcel Premium API key); the model can add deliveries to the user's Parcel account (add-only, capped at 20/day); caches delivery lists in plugin-data.

name: parlor
description: Rooms where AI agents of any vendor talk to each other. A room is a URL; agents join, read and post over plain HTTP, with no accounts and no sign-in. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: the parlor skill plus the hosted parlor MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no authentication, 8 tools). Disclosure — hosted unauthenticated MCP connector at parlor.sh/mcp (tool set is server-controlled, not pinned) plus a curl fallback; messages the agent writes go to parlor.sh or the server in a given room URL and rooms are public to anyone with the link; room tokens are stored under ~/.local/state/parlor; the skill may keep background wait loops running.

name: parrotnotes
description: Find, search, summarize and save insights for your ParrotNotes in-person meeting notes through the hosted ParrotNotes MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0 + DCR), with the parrotnotes workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.parrotnotes.app (OAuth via a Supabase auth backend); note titles, transcripts and insights from the user's ParrotNotes account are pulled into the session context, and text the model passes to save_note_insight is written to that account. OAuth must be enabled with `vibervnbot mcp add parrotnotes --url https://mcp.parrotnotes.app/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

name: pass-secrets
description: pass (password-store) secret source: resolves secrets from a local, GPG-encrypted, git-tracked password store into environment variables at startup, as a first-class SecretSource beside the built-in Bitwarden and 1Password sources. Stdlib-only (subprocess + pathlib), no Python deps, no network — ever. Config: secrets.pass.{enabled,store_path,subdirs,override_existing,timeout_seconds}. Disclosure — when enabled, shells out to the local pass binary (10 s per entry) for every .gpg entry under the configured store subdirs and injects each as an env var that by default overrides .env and shell values; when enabled, also adds a ~900-char system-prompt note about secret resolution; no network.

name: pastdotdev
description: past.dev memory provider: recall before each turn from source-traced memory of past conversations, with sessions sent to past.dev when they end. Maintained by past.dev. Disclosure — the user's message (as the recall query) and each session's user and assistant text, with common secret shapes redacted, are sent to the past.dev API (api.past.dev by default, or the address you configure) under your past project key, with a past-vibervnbot/<version> User-Agent; the key and identity are read from PAST_API_KEY or ~/.past/config.json, which past.dev's other connectors share; off by default on messaging-gateway sessions.

name: pay
description: Discover priced APIs and pay per request (HTTP 402, x402, MPP) in stablecoins through the official hosted Pay MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://connect.pay.sh/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys or local wallet), with the pay workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — payments plugin for pay.sh: the curl tool spends the hosted Pay account's stablecoin balance; hosted Pay enforces the account's spending limits (none move until the user sets them) and confirms each payment through MCP elicitation, declined when nobody can answer; the plugin marks its server untrusted, but the documented OAuth setup (`vibervnbot mcp add pay`) replaces that entry with a native one that runs at `trust: full` unless the user sets `mcp_servers.pay.trust: untrusted`; chats sharing a ViberVN Bot profile share its Pay account; the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

name: pay-cli
description: Discover priced APIs and pay per request (HTTP 402, x402, MPP) in stablecoins from a wallet on this machine, through the local `pay mcp` stdio server of the official Pay CLI, with the pay workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables; the user installs the `pay` CLI (brew or npm) and runs `pay setup` first, and the server is offered only while `pay` is on PATH. Disclosure — payments plugin for pay.sh: ViberVN Bot starts `pay mcp` as a long-running local process; the curl tool spends the local wallet's stablecoin balance; each payment is confirmed by the user through MCP elicitation (PAY_FORCE_ELICITATION=1, declined when nobody can answer) and the server is marked untrusted; every profile using the plugin shares the same local wallet.

name: pcs-security-tls-posture
description: Read-only audit of local TLS posture — certificate validity, key strength, deprecated protocols, weak cipher suites, and the certificate each server's configuration points at. Disclosure — reads a fixed list of system certificate and nginx/Apache config paths under / (or a caller-supplied prefix); makes no network connections and runs no subprocesses. If the sibling plugin pcs-security-core is installed, its copy of the shared contract is loaded in preference to the bundled one.

name: pdf-surgeon
description: Model-driven editor of PDF text whose result keeps the original typesetting, by rewriting the page content stream in place — the string operand inside the existing BT/ET block is replaced and the Tm origin of everything after it on the line is retargeted, so font, size, colour, baseline, char/word spacing, horizontal scale and kerning survive untouched because they are never rewritten.
