Keeps secrets out of chat/prompt context and redacts verbatim output of credential-shaped values; it is not a boundary against a model that deliberately reads it. Adds a static system-prompt section and a /secret command. Imports private core helpers read-only (_config_profile_scope, _is_vibervnbot_provider_credential, _CONFIG_LOCK).

name: secret-handoff
description: Ephemeral credential paste: request_secret asks through clarify and injects the reply over CDP, never storing it. Disclosure — the reply is typed into the focused field of the page whose origin matches the requested service, over the endpoint from BROWSER_CDP_URL or SECRET_HANDOFF_CDP_URL; the answer is visible in the CLI scrollback or the chat history of the surface that asked, and the value is never written to disk, the tool result, or the session transcript.

name: secure-env-ingress
description: One-use HTTPS forms for missing environment secrets, native encrypted Browser Vault logins/TOTP setup keys and payment cards, protected hosted payment-field filling, nested HTTPS verification codes/passcodes, and approved secret operations outside chat and LLM input. Disclosure — /senv setup supplies a skill using sudo for host packages and TLS setup after approval; the TLS listener binds all interfaces by default; pre_gateway_dispatch observes gateway messages to bind commands to their sender. In interactive Telegram sessions, secure_env_vault saves logins or fills a code field through the captured browser supervisor without explicitly submitting the site form. Explicit parent payment/nested-code targeting requires compatible host task/profile ownership and browser-generation evidence and fails closed without it; this is not a general fix for native Vault named-tab selection. Payment filling requires separate native consent and exact document/control guards; explicit resume requires existing nonempty values to match Vault. Site input callbacks, especially 3-D Secure, may authorize or auto-submit an operation. Unknown outcomes require external verification before retry. secure_operation executes administrator-allowlisted, SHA-256-pinned external Python consumers with gateway privileges; consumers are trusted, not sandboxed, and none are enabled by default. Secret input is not persisted by this mode; consumers must enforce their own handling policy. Links are bearer authorization, not submitter identity; cancellation cannot stop an already-running consumer.

name: sem-weave
description: CLI-backed skills for local code discovery and entity-diff review with Sem, plus optional Weave branch-merge previews. Requires user-installed CLIs; does not apply edits or merges, install binaries, or change Git configuration.

name: sendblue
description: Sendblue iMessage / SMS integration. Provides typing indicators, async daemon routing, and Active LLM Tools for SMS dispatch.

name: senler-io-user
description: Get task-specific guidance for Senler agents, automations and knowledge, connect your account through MCP OAuth, and automate selected webhook events with an outbound Relay connection. Disclosure — ViberVN Bot installs the declared `python-socks[asyncio]` dependency for native SOCKS proxy support. First activation of the enabled plugin adds a `senler-io-user` MCP server (mcp-senler-io-user.senler.io; OAuth handled by ViberVN Bot) to the profile's config.yaml and records completion through plugin settings, which native uninstall clears. Reinstalling and enabling the plugin prepares a missing MCP again. The old durable marker from 0.5.2–0.5.3 is ignored, so upgrading restores a missing entry once, including an entry manually removed before this upgrade. Existing compatible and disabled connections are preserved; later loads in the same installation respect manual removal. Explicit chat setup can restore a removed connection. Relay setup enables a `senler-io` gateway platform in the same profile. Once you enable automation, the gateway keeps an outbound WSS connection to a Senler-supplied Relay address and runs unattended agent turns on incoming Senler events (customer messages, leads, etc.); the platform is `trusted_inbound`, so these events bypass ViberVN Bot allowlists and pairing, and customer text reaches the model as untrusted data. During those runs a hook allows the Senler MCP and native tool discovery and pins customer replies to the event's dialog, but other Senler MCP writes run without a ViberVN Bot approval prompt, limited only by your saved instructions and your Senler account permissions. Relay credentials, instructions, event payloads and reports are stored unencrypted in `<VIBERVNBOT_HOME>/senler-io-relay.sqlite3`; result reports (up to 16,000 characters) and this machine's hostname (as the Relay client name) are sent to Senler. Configured monitoring also stores notification recipients, queued texts and delivery receipts in that database; the selected native ViberVN Bot messaging adapter sends summaries and delivery-test messages to the saved recipient.

name: serpapi
description: SerpApi web, Maps, News, Shopping, Hotels, Flights, and Travel Explore for ViberVN Bot.

name: serverless-inference-for-vibervnbot
description: CoreWeave Serverless Inference model provider. Disclosure — ViberVN Bot sends model discovery and chat requests, including prompts and tool results, to https://api.inference.wandb.ai/v1 (CoreWeave / W&B Inference) using COREWEAVE_API_KEY; the installed provider registers a profile only and reads no credential files, starts no processes and adds no telemetry.

name: session-dashboard
description: Session Analyzer — per-session analytics for the ViberVN Bot desktop app: full page at /session-dashboard with token/cache/cost aggregates, tool-call breakdown, file changes, failure groups, and Ask AI (copies a ready-to-run analysis prompt into a fresh draft chat). Read-only over state.db.

name: session-find
description: A search window over your ViberVN Bot session history, opened with Cmd+Option+F, from the command palette, or from the glyph in the bottom bar whose hover shows the chord. Finds a session by an exact word, identifier or phrase through the gateway's own full text index, and by meaning as well when a session-find service answers on loopback; typed filters (in:, -in:, after:, before:, me:, repo: and quoted phrases) are mirrored as chips under the box. The empty box lists pinned then recent sessions, the preview pane shows the matching message with its neighbours, and the footer carries the round trip in whole milliseconds. It reads the session database read only, registers no agent tools, hooks or middleware, needs no credentials or environment variables; its only network calls are the loopback checks named below. The window half ships off by default and is switched on in the app's plugin inventory. Disclosure — while the search window is in use, the plugin's dashboard backend checks every 30 seconds for a separate session-find service at http://127.0.0.1:8474 (or the URL in SESSION_FIND_URL) and, when one answers, sends it your search text, preview requests and the ids of sessions you open, and shows the results it returns; otherwise it reads your ViberVN Bot session database read-only.

name: session-flow
description: Session pane for ViberVN Bot Desktop: Firefox-style session groups with project grouping, list/grid views, Ctrl+Scroll session cycling with a HUD, session-row styling and a built-in settings page. All timers are ctx-owned intervals disposed on unload (live-session poll ~30 s, session refresh ~45 s, project cache 60 s, activity expiry 30 s). The standalone full build in this repo (full/plugin.js, install.sh) is not part of this catalog entry. Contact: info@agantila.com. Disclosure — SDK-only Desktop plugin: reads the local ViberVN Bot gateway through public RPCs (projects.tree, projects.list, session.list, session.active_list, session.context_breakdown) and, on your actions, writes through public RPCs (projects.create/update/add_folder/remove_folder/set_primary/set_active/delete, session.create, session.cwd.set, session.title, session.branch_stored, session.archive, session.close, session.delete); captures Ctrl+mouse-wheel across the app (browser zoom suppressed except over canvases, editors and zoomable images) to cycle sessions; settings and groups stay in the app's local plugin storage; no outbound network, no shell commands, no credentials, no self-update.

name: session-lens
description: Read-only observability for ViberVN Bot Desktop: what each session cost and why, its full trace, recurring tool failures, every profile at a glance, provider quotas and service balances, model comparison with cheaper-route evidence, and instruction-rule grading. Disclosure — reads every profile's state.db read-only plus agent logs, cron/gateway state, config.yaml and .env (key names, and the values of keys an adapter uses); with the credentials ViberVN Bot' own resolvers return, calls only each configured vendor's usage or balance endpoint (hosts listed in the README), sending Grok CLI client headers to cli-chat-proxy.grok.com and a Claude Code user-agent to api.anthropic.com; ViberVN Bot' resolvers may renew ViberVN Bot' Codex and xAI logins and, when ViberVN Bot holds no other Anthropic credential, Claude Code's login; runs the local monid CLI when installed; an Anthropic one-token Claude Haiku probe is off by default; writes no ViberVN Bot state itself and sends no session content anywhere.

name: session-mirror
description: Mirrors ViberVN Bot Desktop, CLI, TUI and ACP conversations into Discord: one public thread per session in a channel you choose, one post per turn (your message and the reply), so work started on a desktop can be followed from the phone. Posting runs on a background thread and never delays or breaks a turn. Disclosure — register() adds one post_llm_call hook; every turn's text (your message and the final reply, not tool calls or outputs) is sent to the Discord REST API (discord.com) using the bot token you configure, after ViberVN Bot's redact_for_egress plus a local token-pattern filter (fail-closed: nothing is sent if the redactor is unavailable); mentions are disabled. The bot token is read only via agent.secret_scope.get_secret (an UnscopedSecretError under multiplexing skips the turn); no external command is ever run. Each turn reads the session's title and source from $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/state.db read-only; session-to-thread ids are stored (mode 0600) in $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/state/session-mirror.json. The optional `vibervnbot session-mirror backfill` CLI command reads $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/state.db read-only and replays past sessions through the same redaction. No other files, telemetry or long-running processes beyond one daemon sender thread.

name: session-ref
description: Reference another ViberVN Bot session in the Desktop composer with @session — type @ and pick from live session suggestions. Inserts a compact @session:"<title>" reference; nothing is injected into context, the agent resolves it with its own session-search. No more copying session IDs.

name: session-token-counter
description: Accumulated input/output token totals and context-window occupancy for the focused session, in the ViberVN Bot Desktop status bar.

name: severian
description: Local-first long-term memory for ViberVN Bot agents: a canonical append-only store (SQLite or PostgreSQL+pgvector) with five-dimensional tenant/profile/collection/agent/session scope, hybrid BM25+vector retrieval with a re-ranker, memories that cite the observations they came from, per-turn user facts, real dates next to relative times, truth resolution when a newer fact replaces an older one, and a conflict note when two returned memories disagree. Fully offline by default; Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B semantic embeddings opt-in, locally or in a user-owned sidecar. On OmniMemEval's public long-term-memory leaderboard (its own models, prompts and full public sets) it scores 90.6 LongMemEval (1st), 87.3 LoCoMo (2nd) and 71.6 BEAM 100K (2nd, within noise of the lead); it re-ran LCM-X to check the board's records, and per-question results, a strict second marker and scripts are published in the repo. Disclosure — stores every conversation turn in one SQLite database under the ViberVN Bot root (`<vibervnbot root>/severian`) shared by all profiles with rows scoped per profile, or in the PostgreSQL database named by `SEVERIAN_DSN`; the opt-in Qwen/Granite embeddings download a model from Hugging Face on first use, and the opt-in embedding sidecar sends memory text to the URL you configure.

name: sgme
description: SGME (拾光记忆) self-hosted long-term memory engine — tagged memories with provenance, per-turn recall, automatic session refinement, a skills library, wiki knowledge base, care signals, communication roles and a three-pool task system (ideas/demands/projects), all behind one HTTP service you own. The plugin is a thin bridge: no LLM, no database, everything heavy runs in your SGME server (local or remote). Disclosure — the plugin talks only to the SGME server you configure (default http://127.0.0.1:9910, SGME_BASE_URL for a remote server), sending SGME_AGENT_KEY / SGME_ADMIN_KEY read through ViberVN Bot's secret scope; each session's user, assistant and tool messages are appended to that server and refined into memories at session end by an LLM you configure on the SGME side; its sgme_* tools let the model read and change memories, skills, wiki pages and tasks on that server and write skill packages under $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugin-data/sgme/skills/ on the SGME host; credential names in the SGME vault can be listed, and reading a credential value into the conversation is off by default (credential_get_enabled / SGME_ENABLE_CREDENTIAL_GET); no third-party services, no telemetry.

name: shodan
description: Shodan tools with complete capability declarations.

name: showly
description: Preview, publish, and manage websites hosted on Showly from ViberVN Bot, through the hosted Showly MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — tool calls go to Showly's hosted MCP server at mcp.showly.ai. The bundled showly-hosting skill makes Showly the default for any deploy, preview or share request that names no provider, and new links default to public (anyone with the link). The showly-reports skill runs a bundled local Node.js renderer (vendored answer-me-with-html 0.4.14, upstream self-update check removed) through the shell and uploads the report directory to Showly when sharing is requested. Sign-in is out of band: `npx @showly/mcp-server login --to vibervnbot` (unpinned) writes MCP_SHOWLY_API_KEY into ~/.vibervnbot/config.yaml.

name: sidebar-cycle
description: Step through ViberVN Bot Desktop sidebar sessions in on-screen order with Ctrl+Cmd+] / Ctrl+Cmd+[ (rebindable), wrapping at both ends. SDK-only: session-row slot markers for order, host.state for the focused session, host.openSession for navigation.

name: sidebar-manager
description: Hide and reorder core sidebar navigation rows from a statusbar dialog.

name: sigrex
description: Build, run and manage sigrex.io trading automation (code and AI strategies, trading bots, webhooks and signals across crypto exchanges, DEXs and prediction markets) through the official Sigrex MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.sigrex.io, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config), with the sigrex workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables; needs a free Sigrex account. The connection has full account access, including actions that can place live trades. Disclosure — the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; the bundled skill instructs the agent to confirm before any action that moves money or changes data.

name: sketch-pad
description: Draw a shape on a Desktop pad and attach the PNG to the next ViberVN Bot chat message. For "what is this shape" when you have no photo.

name: skill-integrity
description: Rug-pull detection for installed agent skills — fingerprints every file in every skill directory (SHA-256), keeps a profile-local snapshot, and reports exactly which skill files changed, appeared, or vanished since; a skill that mutates after install without the user touching it is the rug-pull signal. A skill directory made unreadable is reported as a finding, never treated as clean. Read-only observer, stdlib-only, zero network calls; blind spots (oversize files, symlinks, permission-denied) are counted and printed, never silent. The wrapper registers an hourly pre_llm_call hook that injects findings into the agent context, plus a /skill-integrity slash command (snapshot | check | show) that creates the baseline snapshot and shows the file-level diff. The CLI supports --state-dir to target the plugin's manifest directly. Skill dirs and state derive from get_vibervnbot_home(), covering non-default profiles. Disclosure — reads (hash-only, read-only) every file under the active profile's skills directory and ~/.claude/skills, stores a mode-0600 snapshot in VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugin-data/skill-integrity, and at most hourly injects the names of changed skills into the agent's context.

name: skill-lineage
description: Records where each skill version's content came from, so a skill that rewrites itself can be audited afterwards. For every skill write — a foreground skill_manage call, a background-review edit, or a curator consolidation — it stores the skill content fingerprint before and after, the sources present earlier in the same session (the text the user typed, tool results such as a fetched page or a file, and skills that were read), how each source is linked to the added lines — strong (at least three shared 8-word shingles), anchor (a shared operative token: a URL or host, a shell command with its first argument, a package install, a file path, an environment variable, an IP or e-mail address, that is not common across sources), or context (seen in the session, nothing measurable shared; recorded, not followed by default) — and a seq -> prev_hash -> hash chain over the entries. Text is never stored: hashes are keyed per install and the key stays in plugin-data/skill-lineage. `vibervnbot skill-lineage trace <skill>` shows where the newest version came from, `descendants <url|skill>` lists every skill a source produced, `report` lists versions carrying operative lines of no traceable origin, `verify` re-walks the chain, and `head` prints a value to record elsewhere so a later `verify --head` can tell truncation from an intact chain; a key reset is recorded in the chain and shown in `status` rather than happening silently. The plugin does not stop a write and does not judge a skill: it records and it verifies, and it does not claim a source caused an edit. Prior work on memory lineage (MemLineage, arXiv:2605.14421) is acknowledged in the README. Measured on 2026-10-22 against ViberVN Bot 3166d61: Python 3.14 62 passed; Python 3.11 54 passed, 1 skipped; `vibervnbot plugins validate` reports no warning other than one known false positive (a test template that quotes a "curl | sh" instruction as data and never runs it). Evaluation (generated scenarios and 120 real-model runs) in the README; raw output in eval/. A manual end-to-end run in an isolated VIBERVNBOT_HOME (one real session creating a skill through skill_manage, then status/trace/descendants/report/verify/head) passed, raw output in tests/smoke-2026-10-21.txt. Disclosure — four read-only hooks (on_session_start, pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call); reads tool results, user messages and skill files (in this profile, every other profile's skills folder, the project's .vibervnbot/skills and the skills.external_dirs it reads from config.yaml) to compute keyed hashes; keeps hashes (no text) for 7 days per session and the lineage chain (hashes and skill names) under plugin-data/skill-lineage; no network, no credentials, never blocks or changes a tool call.

name: skill-retrieval
description: BM25-based skill retrieval for large skill libraries. An llm_request middleware rewrites the outgoing request's <available_skills> block to names only (the same bytes every turn, so prompt caching is unaffected), and a pre_llm_call hook appends the top-K matching skill descriptions to the current user message. Uses public plugin surfaces only (register_middleware, register_hook); reads SKILL.md frontmatter from the profile's skill roots and imports a few agent.prompt_builder / agent.skill_utils helpers read-only. pyyaml is the only dependency. Disclosure — optional Jev rerank, off by default: with SKILL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK=jev and TYPESAFE_API_KEY set (read from the environment only), each turn POSTs the user message (injection patterns stripped, capped at 2000 chars) and up to 12 shortlisted skill descriptions (400 chars each) to api.typesafe.ai (3 s timeout, no retries, BM25 order kept on error), and appends a local JSONL log (timestamp, session id, 200-char query excerpt, both orders) under $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/data/jev-trial/, rotated past 5 MB. With the rerank off it makes no network calls and writes no files.

name: skill-router
description: Evidence-based, session-safe skill routing with auditable decisions and opt-in learning

name: snag-shelf
description: Everything that snagged - cross-session shelf of failed tool calls. Full Desktop page, chip, pin, fix-prompt insert. No API keys. Disclosure — stores failed tool-call metadata (tool, truncated args with key-name redaction, error snippet) locally in plugin-data; no network.

name: source-tray
description: Session source tray — URLs the ViberVN Bot agent opened via web_search, web_extract, or browser_navigate. Desktop pane and /sources. No search backend of its own and no API keys.

name: specstream
description: SpecStream gives ViberVN Bot finished lists from the live web: describe the list in plain words and get every matching row with the page it was read from, priced per match with a maximum you approve before anything runs. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with the hosted MCP server (remote streamable-http, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration) and four skills (compile, review-work, approve-work, continue-work); no Python, no executables, no stored credentials. Disclosure — your request text and your answers to the price are sent to api.specstream.ai; approving a price spends your SpecStream balance (new accounts get $10 free) and the plugin marks its server `untrusted`, so ViberVN Bot asks before every call that is not read-only and refuses those calls in unattended runs; a `specstream` server you define in config.yaml replaces the package's and drops that prompt unless you add `trust: untrusted`.

name: spectator
description: Harness-neutral live session sharing, summaries, and branch queries. Disclosure — reads state.db read-only and exposes masked transcripts to invite-token guests on the dashboard; host-approved guest suggestions are injected via ctx.inject_message.

name: speechify
description: The official Speechify text-to-speech provider (tts.provider: speechify), maintained by Speechify. Simba 3.5 voices in 48 languages with low-latency streaming in voice mode, Opus voice notes for messaging platforms, and a vibervnbot speechify command to list voices and hear a test line. Disclosure — sends the text being spoken, the chosen voice and model, the plugin's name and version (Speechify-Caller attribution headers), and your SPEECHIFY_API_KEY to api.speechify.ai (or the base_url / SPEECHIFY_BASE_URL you configure); synthesis is billed to your Speechify workspace; generated audio is written to ViberVN Bot's audio cache; no tools, hooks or middleware; no telemetry.

name: spotify-desktop
description: Spotify Connect remote for ViberVN Bot Desktop — status-bar mini player (now playing, transport, volume, devices, search, playlists, queue) reusing the ViberVN Bot Spotify login (Spotify Premium required for playback control). Unified agent+desktop package: Electron status-bar player plus a dashboard-API backend (desktop-focused, no web UI). No agent tools; config via plugins.entries.spotify-desktop.settings (poll intervals).

name: stack
description: Git-backed Markdown memory with background curation and model-based recall. Disclosure — runs a background curation agent with terminal, file-read and patch tools on your configured auxiliary model, fed raw conversation turns; it commits and pushes the memory store to whatever git remotes you configure, and pulls shared submodules at session start; the engine runs via uv run, which fetches pyyaml==6.0.2 from PyPI; an optional dataset file (memory.stack.dataset_enabled, off by default) stores full transcripts locally with no rotation.

name: stacktree
description: Publish what ViberVN Bot builds (reports, dashboards, briefs, proposals) to a private link that opens in any browser with no account for the viewer, set a passcode or limit it to a company's email addresses, update it in place, and see who opened it and what they commented. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Stacktree's remote MCP server at api.stacktr.ee (OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, token kept by ViberVN Bot); the HTML the model passes to publish_html or update_site is stored in the user's Stacktree account and served at the returned link (unlisted by default, public when a public_slug is set); page titles, open counts and third-party reader comments from that account are read into the session; the remote tools that publish, update, gate, delete pages or email approval requests run without a ViberVN Bot approval prompt; the required sign-in step `vibervnbot mcp add stacktree --url https://api.stacktr.ee/mcp --auth oauth` writes a config.yaml server entry that replaces the package's own.

name: stalkchain
description: Crypto research in plain English through the official StalkChain Data MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://data.stalkchain.com/mcp/directory, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): check a coin before you buy, vet a trader before you copy them, see what smart money is buying, review a wallet and set price alerts, across Solana, Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Monad, Hyperliquid and Robinhood Chain, plus the StonkFun launchpad. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + 18 skills), no Python or executables; needs a StalkChain account with credits. Read-only: never trades, moves funds or signs anything; the only write is the user's own price alerts, after they confirm. Disclosure — the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; each tool call sends the tool name and its inputs to data.stalkchain.com and spends the account's credits; price alerts are stored by StalkChain with their destination (account email or a user-given Discord, Slack or Telegram webhook URL, which can embed a bot token) until deleted or fired.

name: sticky-notes
description: In-window sticky notes for ViberVN Bot Desktop.

name: stop-ledger
description: Local ledger of the turns you stopped while ViberVN Bot was still working (/stop, or /new and /reset during a running turn, on messaging platforms, the TUI and the desktop app): /stop-log shows how many running turns were stopped, how many by /stop and by /new, in how many sessions and how long ago the last one was, per platform or per day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /stop-log recent lists the newest stops (ten, or up to 100 with /stop-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes stop metadata (platform, /stop or /new, ViberVN Bot's label for the stop, a 12-digit hash of the session key; no session key or chat content) to plugin-data/stop-ledger/stops.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot delay or undo a stop; no network

name: storm-fusion-research
description: Human-gated perspective-panel research. One question, several seats, one judge, one human. Solo, native subagent panel, or per-seat MoA/Fusion fanout via the storm_run_panel tool. Disclosure — every seat/judge call runs through ViberVN Bot's plugin LLM lane on your own credentials; with llm.allow_provider_override / allow_model_override enabled the agent picks provider and model per seat and spend follows that choice. The human gates are skill instructions to the agent, not enforced by the tool.

name: stream-speed
description: How fast each model starts answering and how fast it writes: /speed shows the median and p90 time to first text and the median characters per second per model, provider or day, or lists the newest streams (ten, or up to 100 with /speed recent 50), for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded, from the streaming hooks. Disclosure — writes per-response stream timings (ids, model, timings, character count, no text) to plugin-data/stream-speed/streams.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; atexit waits up to 1 s; no network

name: stt-vocab
description: Puts the names a speech-to-text model mis-hears into the transcription prompt ViberVN Bot sends with each voice message: terms you list (globally or per surface) and names found in this profile's memories/USER.md and MEMORY.md, most important last, within the 896 characters ViberVN Bot keeps for Whisper-family backends; your stt.prompt stays in front. Notes written in German, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese or Turkish can be named in the languages setting. Disclosure — register() adds one pre_transcription hook that returns a new prompt string; memory-derived names go only to local backends (faster-whisper, local_command) unless allow_remote is set, and the memory files are not read otherwise; reads at most 256 KB per memory file; no tools, network access, subprocesses or writes; ViberVN Bot uploads the prompt with the audio to the configured STT provider.

name: sugar
description: Local-first persistent memory for coding agents. SQLite on your disk - decisions, preferences, error patterns, and guidelines with project and global scopes and guideline-aware search. No cloud, no API key, nothing leaves the machine.

name: sunshine-moonlight
description: Set up and diagnose Moonlight game streaming (Sunshine host <-> Moonlight client) between machines that run ViberVN Bot. One tool, action-based: discover hosts on the tailnet/LAN, preflight ports, install+start Sunshine, pair clients, verify encoders, and launch a stream. Writes to remote machines only over SSH and only when the action says so. Disclosure — runs shell commands as your user on this machine and, over SSH, on hosts you name (BatchMode, your existing keys); `install` runs `sudo` with your package manager to install `sunshine` or `moonlight-qt` without a ViberVN Bot approval prompt; `configure`/`start` rewrite Sunshine's config (with a backup) and restart its user service; `discover` reads `tailscale status` and port-probes your tailnet peers; `launch` starts a Moonlight process. No credentials stored, no telemetry.

name: superlocalmemory
description: Local-first long-term memory for ViberVN Bot, kept on your own computer: recall before each turn, tool-outcome logging, opt-in turn capture, 16 skills and /slm commands. Disclosure — talks only to the `superlocalmemory` MCP server you configure and grant in `plugins.entries.superlocalmemory.mcp_allowlist` (on this computer, or on another one with `connection: remote`): each turn's user message (redacted) is sent for recall and every tool call's arguments and result (redacted, up to 2,000 characters each) are logged to it, and with `capture_turns` on every turn is saved; `/slm` commands run the local `slm` CLI, including ones that change SLM and host settings (`/slm upgrade-hosts --apply` writes the plugin's grant into ViberVN Bot config.yaml); `slm_agent` starts a child agent that inherits the parent session's tools.

name: supermemory
description: Supermemory semantic long-term memory provider — profile recall, semantic search, explicit memory tools, and per-turn conversation capture. Maintained by Supermemory; the same provider that shipped in-tree.

name: surp-vibervnbot-x402-llm
description: Marketplace-aware LLM routing for Surp — live prices for all models, provider TPS and trusted flags, mid-chat seller switching, secret masking, and approval-gated paid chat. Disclosure — the messages passed to surp_chat and SURP_API_KEY go to the surp.ivc.lol gateway, run by the individual developer ivcained (operator page https://surp.ivc.lol/operator, terms https://surp.ivc.lol/terms; not affiliated with Surplus Intelligence), which forwards them to third-party sellers on the Surplus Intelligence marketplace, including sellers not flagged trusted unless trusted_only is set; paid surp_chat calls spend from the user's prepaid Surp balance (USDC on Base, 5 % gateway markup), each behind a per-model ViberVN Bot approval prompt (denied in cron and other unattended runs by default) plus a per-request ceiling (max_spend_usd, default $0.05); the price, provider, quote, combo and cache tools call the same gateway without a key; routing preferences are stored under VIBERVNBOT_HOME/cache/surp-vibervnbot-x402-llm/.

name: switchbot-control
description: SwitchBot OpenAPI v1.1, personal use. No Plug Mini on/off. Locks off unless enabled. setPosition only Curtain/Curtain3 (0=open). Disclosure — Controls real devices through the SwitchBot cloud API (api.switch-bot.com) using your SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET. Each call reads SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET for the active profile, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. Every command asks for ViberVN Bot approval and is refused under cron, yolo, approvals off and unattended sessions. Lock and door devices stay refused unless you turn on safety_devices. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your ViberVN Bot gateway can request a command and approve it. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml each time. The optional watch is a cron job (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. Not tested on real devices. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off.

name: t3-code-theme
description: Unofficial port of the standard T3 Code dark theme for ViberVN Bot Desktop. Palette, T3 composer, sidebar thread cards with project and branch, model labels and confirm dialogs. Scoped to its own theme; other themes are untouched. Disclosure — unofficial T3 Code lookalike theme; its stylesheet restyles and hides some native Desktop controls, it reads local session metadata (branch, repo, provider) for sidebar cards, and it switches the active theme once on first enable.

name: tabella
description: Document lifecycle for agents in one package: create .docx/.xlsx/.pptx/.pdf/.odt/.ods/.odp from structured JSON or raw HTML/CSS, convert between formats via pandoc + LaTeX, and read any document — anydoc (Rust, office formats and text PDFs to Markdown, in-process) with LiteParse + Tesseract OCR fallback for scanned PDFs and images, plus PDF text editing with output-directory guards. Ships as an Agent Plugins v1 package (auto-discovered plugin.json + mcp.json declaring a stdio MCP server — the client spawns it per the v1 lifecycle, PLUGIN_ROOT/PLUGIN_DATA injected — plus an optional self-host streamable-HTTP server; first run of either bootstraps the dependency venv). The HTTP lane binds to 127.0.0.1 only and requires Bearer auth out of the box: a random token is generated into PLUGIN_DATA on first run (TABELLA_TOKEN overrides); requests with an Origin header or a non-JSON body are rejected, and model-supplied HTML cannot fetch network or local-file resources (data: URIs only — the same fetcher now also guards CSS input, not just HTML). Pandoc invocations are argument-safe: extra_args is allowlisted (--toc, --number-sections, -V key=value) and from_format/to_format are validated against the built-in format-name grammar (^[a-z0-9_]+([+-][a-z0-9_]+)*$), closing pandoc's *.lua reader/writer code-exec path; both servers re-exec into the dependency venv after bootstrap. Disclosure — Python deps (python-docx, openpyxl, python-pptx, weasyprint, odfpy, Pillow, lxml, PyMuPDF, firecrawl-anydoc, liteparse — 10 direct packages, transitives included in a 25-package closure) are pinned to exact versions with sha256 hashes in requirements-pinned.txt and installed with --require-hashes into a venv under PLUGIN_DATA or ~/.venvs/docs (scripts/setup.sh on Linux/macOS; on Windows the venv is built with the standard library's venv module — no bash or MSYS2 needed); system pandoc is required for conversion, a TeX engine (e.g. texlive-xetex) only when the output format is PDF (weasyprint for HTML->PDF); OCR needs the tesseract binary (UB-Mannheim build on Windows); all conversion, reading, OCR and PDF editing run locally with no network or telemetry; nothing is uploaded; read, convert, and PDF-edit tools access exactly the filesystem paths you pass; doc_create_document additionally containment-checks its output paths against the configured output directory (escape warns). Linux and Windows are CI-tested platforms (five-lane smoke battery on windows-latest: stdio lifecycle through a natively bootstrapped venv, create, read, pdf-from-html via the GTK runtime, pandoc convert).

name: tailgate
description: Per-job progress updates in chat for jobs ViberVN Bot hands off to other machines (coding agents, CI, scripts), with per-job mute and follow and no model calls.

name: talaria-webui
description: Extends ViberVN Bot API capabilities to deliver a richer chat interface with Talaria WebUI. Disclosure — adds API_SERVER_KEY-authenticated /talaria/v1 routes to the ViberVN Bot API server (cross-session history search, rewind/branch/compress of API sessions, runs with the profile's instructions and prefill); stores response metadata (no message bodies) in $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/talaria/observations.db; relies on private api_server/AIAgent internals behind feature detection.

name: tam
description: Local-first long-term memory backed by total-agent-memory (TAM) over MCP — saves each completed turn (with a noise filter; TAM's quality gate applies), recalls relevant memories before each turn within a token budget, and adds tam_recall / tam_save tools; optional TAM team server for shared company memory. Disclosure — local mode starts the separately installed tam binary as a child process per session with an allowlisted environment that carries no credentials: ViberVN Bot provider keys (including HF_TOKEN and OLLAMA_API_KEY), TAM_API_TOKEN and any *_TOKEN / *_API_KEY / *_SECRET / *_PASSWORD variable are withheld, and of HF_* / OLLAMA_* only non-secret settings pass (OLLAMA_URL, OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL, HF_HOME, HF_HUB_OFFLINE); it stores user/assistant turn text plus built-in memory additions (not tool output) in TAM's store, by default outside VIBERVNBOT_HOME and shared with other agents using TAM; remote mode sends the same text to the user-configured URL with an optional TAM_API_TOKEN bearer token; vibervnbot memory setup tam writes tam.json, TAM_API_TOKEN to .env and memory.provider in config.yaml.

name: tamavibervnbot
description: Grow a local TamaVibervnbot pet from real ViberVN Bot agent activity. Disclosure — hooks write a pet ledger and sprite atlas under $VIBERVNBOT_HOME only; the optional python -m tamavibervnbot CLI additionally reads/writes ~/.codex, ~/.petdex and ~/.evopet, runs an unauthenticated loopback preview server (127.0.0.1:8765) and on macOS compiles a Swift overlay and installs a RunAtLoad+KeepAlive LaunchAgent with no uninstall command. No network egress, no credential reads.

name: tameru
description: Big tool outputs, kept small, nothing lost: old tool results shrink to the lines that matter and every distinct error, and the tameru_expand tool brings back the exact original. Deterministic and local, with no LLM calls. Disclosure — Subclasses ViberVN Bot's built-in ContextCompressor and overrides its private prune/demote methods (checks their shape at startup and falls back to stock compaction when they change). Unless you set compression.proactive_prune_tokens yourself, turns on proactive tool-result pruning with a trigger scaled to the model's context window, and after each prune shortens ViberVN Bot's re-prune runway. Adds a model-callable tameru_expand tool that returns pruned tool output from memory or from this session's archive (web, browser and MCP output stays wrapped as untrusted data); complex regex greps run in a short-lived local Python child process. No network calls; the render log is off by default.

name: tavily-plugin
description: Search, extract, map, crawl, and research through Tavily hosted MCP, with Tavily skills. The default connection requires TAVILY_API_KEY; supports ViberVN Bot-managed OAuth through a native MCP override. Disclosure — Connects to Tavily's hosted MCP server at `mcp.tavily.com` and sends it the search queries, URLs and research prompts the agent issues, authenticated with `TAVILY_API_KEY` or a ViberVN Bot-managed Tavily OAuth sign-in.

name: teamorouter
description: TeamoRouter as ViberVN Bot model providers on one key: `teamorouter` serves Claude models over TeamoRouter's native Anthropic Messages API (so ViberVN Bot' Anthropic prompt caching and thinking apply), and `teamorouter-openai` serves GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM and Grok models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's tool-capable chat models from TeamoRouter's public catalog, leaving out image, service-tier and free-tier variants, and context windows come from the same catalog. Maintained by TeamoRouter. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and TEAMOROUTER_API_KEY go to https://api.teamorouter.com (/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions) through ViberVN Bot' own clients, and TeamoRouter forwards each request to the upstream vendor serving the model. The plugin's own request is GET https://api.teamorouter.com/v1/models/pricing, a public endpoint, sent without the key and cached for an hour. `teamorouter-openai` requests carry a fixed `X-Client-Source: vibervnbot-teamorouter-plugin` header (via the profile's default_headers), used only to count traffic from this plugin; Claude requests carry no header from the plugin. No telemetry, no files read or written, no stored credentials, no processes.

name: telegram-client
description: Telegram client pane for ViberVN Bot Desktop: dialogs, message history with image previews and per-post image reload, forum topics, and reviewed send/reply/save/delete/mark-as-read actions via a dedicated Telethon user session (separate from the core gateway bot token). All history is sanitized before rendering. Disclosure — the profile dashboard backend reads dialogs and message history and downloads media for in-page previews (page byte-budgeted and cached in memory); TELEGRAM_API_ID/TELEGRAM_API_HASH come from the profile's ViberVN Bot secrets; login challenges stay in process memory; the dedicated Telethon session lives in VIBERVNBOT_HOME/telegram-plugin-auth/ (directory 0700, .session and its -wal/-shm sidecars 0600), and anyone holding that session file controls the Telegram account; delete removes the selected message for everyone; mutations go prepare -> exact preview -> confirm -> commit -> readback, and the pane's "Confirm actions" switch (on by default) can turn the preview step off; message links open in the system browser (http and https only).

name: telegram-notify
description: Remote Telegram lifecycle notifications for the main ViberVN Bot agent: turn start, completion with a bounded final answer, interruption/failure, and user-facing approval requests. Suppresses subagent, Telegram-origin lifecycle, and automatic/smart-approval noise. Outbound-only, no input channel. Disclosure — enabled by default once installed and reuses the core Telegram gateway's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL when present, so each main-agent turn's final answer (up to 3,200 chars) and approval-request command text (up to 700 chars) from CLI, Desktop and eligible gateway platforms are sent to api.telegram.org for delivery to that one chat; Telegram-origin lifecycle and approval-prompt copies (and, when notify_on_approval_response is enabled, Telegram-origin approval-response copies) are suppressed because the core Telegram gateway already delivers them in that chat; token and state are stored 0600 under VIBERVNBOT_HOME/telegram-notify.

name: telegram-stickers
description: Lets your agent answer in Telegram with a sticker, the way a person reacts to a joke or good news: four default packs made by Telegram out of the box, then packs you list or send the bot in a direct chat; picked by emoji or by meaning, sent as a reply in the current chat and forum topic, paced per chat, with a per-chat off switch the agent cannot undo. Pace and packs can be set in words in your direct chat. Disclosure: calls only the Telegram Bot API (api.telegram.org or the configured api_base) with the gateway's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, read through ViberVN Bot' secret scope: getStickerSet for the packs in use (during the first-run setup also from a short background thread, only for a sender ViberVN Bot answers, at most 32 at once), sendSticker, and getFile plus one download per sticker for /stickers describe, which the owner starts and which sends each sticker image to the vision model configured in ViberVN Bot. A native Telegram handler sees stickers sent to the bot in direct chats (not in groups), skips forwarded ones and keeps pack name, sticker kind and sender id in memory for up to an hour; everyone the bot answers in a direct chat can add packs, up to max_learned_packs in all (default 100, 0 for no limit; learn_packs: false turns learning off). A pre_llm_call hook appends fixed text to the user message of Telegram turns: a sticker hint of about 540 characters, a settings note of about 310 characters when the message mentions stickers, or a setup paragraph during the first-run setup. Writes catalog.json, descriptions.json and state.json under plugin-data/telegram-stickers/ and reads ViberVN Bot' sticker_cache.json. No middleware: the sticker tools run through ViberVN Bot like any tool. Uses ViberVN Bot functions outside the plugin API (tools.vision_tools.vision_analyze_tool, gateway.session_context.get_session_env) and reads the call stack to tell the local CLI or TUI from other callers of /stickers. No shell commands, telemetry or self-update. Anyone the bot answers in a direct chat counts as the owner: they can change pacing, packs, banned stickers and per-chat on/off; the off switch the agent cannot undo holds in groups only.

name: telegram_dashboard_probe
description: One pinned Telegram message with the state of your ViberVN Bot on one phone screen: gateway, backup, config drift, the cron ticker and its jobs, whether the Telegram channel is deaf, whether the agent sees its rules and whether its memory writes stand unapproved, account limits and version. Read-only, no LLM calls, nothing to press. Disclosure — Claude and Codex limits come from ViberVN Bot' own account-usage fetcher, called every tick (which, like /usage, may refresh OAuth tokens through ViberVN Bot' own auth code); at most once per limits_refresh_seconds (default 900 s) the Grok weekly pool is read from https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing and /v1/settings with the xai-oauth token ViberVN Bot resolves (which, like any ViberVN Bot request to xAI, may refresh that OAuth token and save it to auth.json, or clear a dead one, through ViberVN Bot' own auth code), sending the header x-xai-token-auth xai-grok-cli that identifies the request as the Grok CLI (an undocumented xAI host ViberVN Bot itself does not use), and Kimi Code windows from the kimi-coding base URL /v1/usages with the kimi-coding key ViberVN Bot resolves (which, like any ViberVN Bot key lookup without a usable key in .env or the environment, may save ViberVN Bot' credential pool back to auth.json once when loading it changes something, e.g. a placeholder key in .env) and a User-Agent of claude-code/0.1.0 (undocumented provider surfaces), and up to four operator-configured limits_sources, if set, each with one GET to http on loopback only (127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1), with no proxy and no redirect, optionally sending Authorization: Bearer with the value of an environment variable the operator names (never a *_BOT_TOKEN one); every tick the tail of VIBERVNBOT_HOME/logs/errors.log (the last 256 KB; the whole file, up to 4 MB, until the first successful read) is read for Gemini HTTP 429 lines, of which only the time, limit, retry and model are kept, and for the engine's own 'Failed to send Telegram message' lines, of which only the time is kept, never the message text; with a memory provider configured, the last 256 KB of the same log are also read for the engine's warnings about that provider, of which only the time and whether one says unavailable are kept; every tick VIBERVNBOT_HOME/cron/jobs.json is read for each job's id, name, enabled flag, state, times, status and failure streak (never prompt, script, deliver, skills or the model) and the ticker's marker files for their epoch, and VIBERVNBOT_HOME/cron/executions.db is opened read-only (sqlite3 mode=ro with PRAGMA query_only, in a worker under the tick's deadline) for the job_id, status, delivery_outcome and time columns of failed or undelivered runs, never the error column; the engine's error texts are reduced to the kind of the error in a word and never reach the screen or the record; the connected Telegram adapter's public property send_path_degraded is read every tick, and, as a capability and not a contract, four private attributes of the live adapter object (_updates_received_total, _polling_generation, _polling_last_progress_monotonic, _polling_generation_started_monotonic) are read as attributes, nothing is called on it, and an adapter without them shows no data for that line; every tick VIBERVNBOT_HOME/state.db is opened read-only the same way for the newest saved system prompt of each platform the running gateway lists in VIBERVNBOT_HOME/gateway_state.json, and the project context files the engine would load (.vibervnbot.md or VIBERVNBOT.md in that directory and each parent up to the git root, the AGENTS.override.md / AGENTS.md / agents.md chain from the git root down, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules and .cursor/rules/*.mdc; up to 4 MB each, links followed as the engine follows them) are read from the directory that prompt names (else the engine's TERMINAL_CWD or the gateway's working directory), and .vibervnbot.md, VIBERVNBOT.md and the AGENTS names also from the gateway's working directory and VIBERVNBOT_HOME, which may be outside VIBERVNBOT_HOME; to tell whether the prompt carries them as they are on disk; only a verdict, the file names, sizes and times are kept, never the prompt's or a file's text; every tick VIBERVNBOT_HOME/memories/MEMORY.md and USER.md (up to 4 MB each) are read to count their characters against the limits, the waiting writes in VIBERVNBOT_HOME/pending/memory and pending/skills (up to 2,000 files) for their names and times and, of the memory ones (up to 256 KB each), each add's target and length, and the time of VIBERVNBOT_HOME/skills/.curator_ledger.jsonl; never a notebook's, an entry's or a waiting write's text, and nothing there is written; the private vibervnbot_cli.version_info._cached_version_info and the signature of agent.prompt_builder._read_text_with_timeout are read from modules the gateway already imported, and nothing is called or changed on them; the release check keeps only each release's version and publication time and downloads, installs or replaces nothing; config.yaml is read through ViberVN Bot' own YAML parser for the memory limits, switches, approval gate and provider name, skills.write_approval and each platform's skip_context_files; the plugin's own code never reads the Telegram bot token and never writes vendor credential files (ViberVN Bot' auth code it calls for Grok and Kimi may, as said above), and no request the plugin's own code sends with a token in a header follows a redirect; the latest ViberVN Bot release is read from api.github.com without a token at most once per 15 minutes (releases/latest with the last answer's ETag; the release list releases?per_page=100 only when Latest names another version); an operator-configured drift_command, if set, runs as a subprocess; the delivery record is written under VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugin-data/.

name: telesec
description: Telegram Business secretary: transcribes voice notes, round videos, and speech attachments right in the chat, with Settings and per-chat controls in Telegram's Manage Bot panel, plus opt-in text history (with import from a Telegram export), correspondence stats, and contact dossiers. Disclosure — audio goes to the STT backend ViberVN Bot is configured with (local or external); transcript cleanup sends chat text through the host ctx.llm; opt-in dossiers send chat text through the ViberVN Bot model task telesec_dossier (default Vercel AI Gateway to Google with zero data retention; an optional message check on the same gateway and optional Cloudflare fact extraction are off by default); an owner-sent /dossier posts that contact's stored dossier (without the owner note, but written with it) into the Business chat for the contact to read; runs local ffprobe/ffmpeg (argument lists, no shell) on attached audio; opt-in dossiers run a gateway background thread; modes, opt-in history, and dossiers are stored 0600 under VIBERVNBOT_HOME/data/telesec; reads only the numeric bot id prefix of TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN; no telemetry.

name: telnyx-provider
description: Vendor-maintained Telnyx inference provider with an authenticated live model catalog, hosted open models, frontier routes, and catalog-derived pricing.

name: terraform-drift
description: Compare pinned Terraform provider and module versions with the public registry. Disclosure — tools are on for every ViberVN Bot surface, including the gateway. Stop a surface with vibervnbot tools disable --platform <name> terraform-drift, or the plugin with vibervnbot plugins disable terraform-drift. Nothing is written under plugin-data/terraform-drift, and there is no key. Only the directory you name is read, and only .tf, .tf.json, and .terraform.lock.hcl. Symlinks and .. are refused, and .env, tfvars, .terraform, backend values, and hashes are not returned. The provider pin is the lock version, not the required_providers constraint. A module pin is an exact version only. GET calls only registry.terraform.io and, for a github.com source, raw.githubusercontent.com CHANGELOG.md. Redirects and proxy variables are ignored. A timeout or failed read leaves latest empty and is not called current. Semver orders versions, so 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.0. The digest text is not sent and no cron job is created. known keeps newer versions, and omitting it does not call rows new today. There is no approval card. Before the call, name the directory and say there is no init, plan, apply, or state write. Cron, yolo, and approvals off can still run this read. MIT, no daily cap, requires ViberVN Bot >=0.21.4.

name: thomas
description: Fine-tune a small calibrated encoder classifier on Modal and rate it with gonogo. Every GPU launch goes through the human approval gate with the exact config shown; data checks and evaluation run locally for free. Disclosure — thomas_encoder_train spends the user's Modal GPU credits and uploads the chosen training JSONL rows to Modal after the human approval gate; the base model is downloaded from Hugging Face on the Modal side. Training and inference run in a separate Python interpreter the user configures via THOMAS_PYTHON (with the author's thomas package, torch and modal installed); the ViberVN Bot venv only gets gonogo-eval. Runs and artifacts are written under VIBERVNBOT_HOME/thomas/runs; the eval tool writes report files to the path the model supplies.

name: tidal
description: TIDAL for ViberVN Bot: five tools (playback through local mpv, search, playlists, library, mixes) over the unofficial TIDAL API via tidalapi. Login is TIDAL's own PKCE login flow (vibervnbot tidal login) — no developer app needed. Playback runs on the ViberVN Bot machine (mpv); TIDAL has no remote-device API like Spotify Connect. Needs a TIDAL subscription (any tier). Disclosure — unofficial TIDAL integration (community tidalapi library using TIDAL's own app client); stores your TIDAL access and refresh token in plaintext (owner-only, 0600) under $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugin-data/tidal/ and refreshes it itself; playback spawns a detached local mpv process with an IPC socket and plays audio on the ViberVN Bot machine.

name: time-gap
description: Inject an implicit time-gap sense only when a gap or a date rollover crosses.

name: timestamp-ref
description: @ts: context references that turn timestamps into readable times for the model: @ts:1729468800123 attaches the moment in UTC, in the local time zone and as ISO 8601, with its weekday, how long ago or ahead it is, the same moment in Unix seconds, milliseconds and microseconds, and its ISO week; bare numbers are read as seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds by their length (or an s/ms/us/ns suffix) and the block says which; ISO 8601 and RFC 2822 dates and now work too, and up to 10 values in one reference also get the gaps between them; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a value as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's datetime; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials; register() only adds the @ts: reference provider

name: tinyfish
description: TinyFish: the web, built into ViberVN Bot. Free Search and Fetch power ViberVN Bot's own web_search and web_extract, and when a site needs clicks, forms or a login, a remote browser and the tinyfish_agent web agent handle it. Disclosure — sends search queries, URLs to fetch and tinyfish_agent goals with your TINYFISH_API_KEY to the TinyFish API (*.tinyfish.ai). Browser sessions and tinyfish_agent runs spend TinyFish credits. Under the default `request` policy each one goes through ViberVN Bot's approval prompt first (a session/always answer covers every later call; cron and unattended runs are denied unless you allow them). Setting `tinyfish.credit_policy.<feature>: allow` or YOLO skips the prompt. `vibervnbot tinyfish setup` / `browser enable` (run by you) save the key to ViberVN Bot .env, set web.search_backend/extract_backend and browser.cloud_provider in config.yaml, enable the web/browser toolsets, and can install the agent-browser CLI after asking.

name: titanos-mcp
description: Connect ViberVN Bot to Titanos marketplace, Amazon, listings, Ads, and product research tools through the pinned Titanos OAuth MCP client. This portable Agent Plugin v1 package bundles seven operating skills, requires Node.js 20.18.1 or newer, and uses browser authorization with a Titanos account. Disclosure — starts the npm package @titanos/mcp-agents@1.47.2 via npx (fetched from npm on first run); its tools read and WRITE live marketplace/Ads accounts under your Titanos OAuth session.

name: together
description: Together AI model-provider plugin — OpenAI-compatible API, 270+ serverless open-weight models, live catalog discovery.

name: token-cost-meter
description: Live token usage, model-aware USD cost and prompt-cache savings in the ViberVN Bot Desktop status bar, with a persistent per-day ledger that survives restarts. Disclosure — Desktop only; no network calls of its own (prices come from the gateway's model.options and a bundled models.dev rate table); stores per-day token totals, per-session counters and last-known rates in its own Desktop plugin storage; costs are list-price estimates, not billing data.

name: token-lens
description: Token consumption analytics for ViberVN Bot: records exact per-call usage from pre/post_api_request hooks, decomposes every request into categories (system prompt, built-in and per-MCP-server tool schemas, skills, memory, history, tool results, output, reasoning) calibrated to billed totals, and adds a Token Lens dashboard tab plus a Sessions-page card with deterministic and AI-evaluated token-reduction suggestions; `vibervnbot token-lens refresh` runs a suggestion refresh from the CLI. Disclosure — records per-API-call token counts (no message text) from pre/post_api_request hooks into token_lens.db at the ViberVN Bot home root (per-call rows kept 90 days, rollups kept), and reads ViberVN Bot's state.db read-only for session token totals and, during the optional dashboard history import, message text for estimation only; after 10 recorded sessions it automatically calls your configured main model through ViberVN Bot's plugin LLM facade every 5 sessions (up to two calls per refresh, capped at 50,000 tokens by meta_budget_tokens), sending aggregated token statistics plus the names of your enabled MCP servers and plugins, and auto-applies the model's proposed category regex rules and rubric changes (logged to token_lens.EVOLUTION.md; evolve_rules: false turns this off); the dashboard's refresh button spawns a detached `vibervnbot token-lens refresh` process that logs to logs/token-lens-refresh.log; its data paths follow the VIBERVNBOT_HOME environment variable rather than the active profile, so in a multi-profile gateway every profile records into the launch profile's database; no third-party network calls, no telemetry.

name: tokenwatch
description: Monitor ViberVN Bot token usage, notify at thresholds, and freeze tool/gateway activity at configured limits.

name: tokstat
description: Live token usage in the ViberVN Bot Desktop status bar: cumulative total, a real-time this-turn counter, last-turn delta, context occupancy, and prompt-cache hit rate. Event-driven (no polling, no RPC); English and Chinese, follows the app locale.

name: tool-slimmer
description: Reduce ViberVN Bot tool-schema overhead and show selector savings in the dashboard. Disclosure — optional mode jev (off by default; needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY) sends each turn's request text and up to 32 candidate tool names and descriptions to TypeSafe (api.typesafe.ai); all other modes run locally. Optional user-run scripts can patch ViberVN Bot core on older ViberVN Bot and install a systemd user self-heal unit; the dashboard advisor edits the tool_slimmer section of config.yaml with a backup.

name: toolaria
description: Rescues oversized MCP and web tool results before they flood context.

name: tracekit
description: Tracekit's signer decides every tool call before it runs (deny blocks, ask waits for a person) and signs each call and its outcome into a run you can verify offline. Disclosure — every tool call's name and arguments, plus its result (in full for tools Tracekit's policy marks untrusted, otherwise a SHA-256 digest), go to a Tracekit signer: by default a same-user dev signer (`python -m tracekit signer serve --dev`) that the plugin starts on first use as a detached background process, which keeps running after ViberVN Bot exits until 15 minutes idle and stores signed runs plus each call's redacted arguments and results (encrypted, kept 7 days) under your user's data directory (~/.local/share/tracekit on Linux), or a remote signer when you set TRACEKIT_SIGNER to an https:// URL. The plugin fails closed: when tracekit-ai can't load or the signer refuses or can't be reached, tool calls are blocked (including every tool an execute_code script calls), and an `ask` decision holds the call until someone approves it in Tracekit or ViberVN Bot's hook timeout runs out.

name: traceverse_vibervnbot_otel
description: ViberVN Bot OpenTelemetry traces and dashboard logs, with local-model cost estimates and optional in-process evaluation, GPU, energy, and CO2 metrics via genai-otel-instrument. Disclosure — Sends OpenTelemetry traces and log records for every turn, LLM call and tool call (session ids, models, token counts, costs, tool names, errors) to an OTLP endpoint, `http://localhost:4318` unless `VIBERVNBOT_OTEL_ENDPOINT` points elsewhere; prompt, response and tool argument/result text is included only when `VIBERVNBOT_OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true`; if `genai-otel-instrument` is installed it is activated in-process and instruments the LLM client libraries ViberVN Bot uses.

name: true402-swap-guard
description: Blocks token buys when true402 finds a honeypot or a rug in progress — one pre_tool_call hook in front of every trading tool, MCP server and terminal command (Base, Ethereum, BSC, Solana). Free edition: it never pays, holds no wallet key and has no payment code. Disclosure — the pre_tool_call hook reads the command string of every tool call and the parameters of trading-named tools; when a call looks like a buy, each candidate token address and its chain (every 0x address in a trading shell command except well-known majors and an unambiguous sold token, which can include a recipient or wallet address) is sent to true402.dev's free check endpoint, with no prompts, amounts or other tool data. Uses true402's small daily free allowance; when it is used up, a token counts as unchecked and passes by default (configurable to ask or block). Blocks only on a definite danger verdict for a token being bought; a possible sale or a configured caution goes to the ViberVN Bot approval gate, and one "always" answer there silences all later guard prompts. No stored data, no shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

name: tsubasa
description: Tsubasa OpenAI-compatible model provider (tool calling not supported yet). Disclosure — sends prompts and your TSUBASA_API_KEY to api.tsubasa.sh, operated by PalmAndWand; the API currently serves Canada only and answers HTTP 451 to requests from elsewhere.

name: ttsbuddy
description: Native TTS Buddy speech provider using the existing TTS Buddy CLI, with offline voice selection, MP3 generation, ViberVN Bot voice-message conversion and exact-job recovery, plus terminal-only account deletion through CLI 0.16.0+. Disclosure — runs the user-installed `ttsbuddy` CLI (argument array, speech text on stdin), which sends the text and voice settings to TTS Buddy, downloads the hosted audio and uses the account's quota. Credentials come from the profile's `TTSBUDDY_API_KEY` secret or, when the user selects `cli_config_dir`, from that CLI profile's own saved login, which the CLI may read and update. The model-callable `ttsbuddy_recover` tool downloads an existing job to a new MP3 path the model chooses (never overwrites). The terminal command `vibervnbot ttsbuddy account delete` can permanently delete the TTS Buddy account, its hosted files and identity, and cancel subscriptions, after `--yes` and a fresh email code entered at a hidden prompt or protected stdin.

name: turn-bell
description: A bell in the ViberVN Bot desktop composer that pings the ntfy topic ViberVN Bot already uses when a turn finishes. Click to cycle off, current turn, or all turns. Disclosure — when enabled, posts the first line of each finished reply plus model, duration, token and cost figures to the ntfy server/topic ViberVN Bot is configured with (default ntfy.sh); reads NTFY_* from the profile .env and falls back to the ntfy CLI's ~/.config/ntfy/client.yml login (read-only).

name: turn-usage
description: Usage and cost footer appended to every reply — tokens, cache hit rate, cost and context occupancy, plus a per-tool time breakdown showing which tool actually consumed the wall clock. Waiting time (a blocking user prompt) is reported separately and excluded from the active-time denominator. Pure computation, never calls a model; any failure leaves the reply untouched. Disclosure — the usage footer is appended to the stored assistant reply, so it is replayed to the model on later turns and adds tokens to every turn.

name: twenty-crm
description: Twenty CRM for ViberVN Bot with managed self-hosting, external-instance connectivity, REST, GraphQL, and live schema introspection.

name: typesafe-skill-router
description: TypeSafe (Jev) skill routing: the request is routed before the model call and the one skill from the live roster that fits it is named in a single <skill_relevance> line on the user message — nothing is injected when nothing fits.

name: umt
description: Connect 28 production-ready MCP servers to any coding agent. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): three zero-config stdio servers out of the box (Hacker News, arXiv, npm registry, each pinned to an exact npm version), plus the umt-mcp skill that drives the umt CLI to wire any of the 28 servers into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Zed and more. Needs Node.js and npm on PATH.

name: unbrowse
description: Unbrowse: websites as APIs. Read any page as clean markdown, run tasks on sites through learned first-party APIs (no browser), and drive a cloud browser with saved logins when nothing matches. Also a web_extract backend and a guard that routes public-web browser_* calls to Unbrowse. Disclosure — hosted service: page URLs, task text and tool arguments are sent to unbrowse.ai with your API key, pages are fetched and site logins are stored on Unbrowse's side, and verified calls bill the Unbrowse account; once UNBROWSE_API_KEY is set the plugin blocks the built-in browser_* tools and web_extract on public URLs by default (settings blockBrowser/blockWebExtract, or UNBROWSE_ALLOW_BUILTIN_BROWSER=1).

name: unibaseio-membase
description: Long-term memory for you and your AI from Membase (membase.com, by Unibase): one memory every connected AI shares. Searches the user's Membase memory before each turn (8 s, fail-open) and adds membase_search, membase_save and membase_profile. Disclosure — user prompts are sent as search queries to the Membase API (api.app.membase.com); with the opt-in capture_turns setting the user's messages are saved there too, and what ViberVN Bot' built-in memory records about the user is saved to their Membase profile. MEMBASE_API_KEY comes from the ViberVN Bot secret scope; the only local file is $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/unibaseio-membase.json. No background processes, shell commands or telemetry.

name: unicode-ref
description: @unicode: context references that spell text out character by character for the model: @unicode:"text" attaches a table of every character of the quoted text (code point, Unicode name, category) with notes on what does not show on screen: invisible characters and their positions, text-direction controls, spaces other than the ordinary one, Unicode tag characters (decoded), words that mix Latin letters with lookalike Cyrillic, Greek or fullwidth ones, and private-use or unassigned code points; @unicode:U+200B describes up to 20 code points (name, category, UTF-8 bytes, decomposition); the TUI and Desktop composer suggest characters by name. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, using Python's unicodedata; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials; register() only adds the @unicode: reference provider

name: unitares
description: Records each ViberVN Bot session on a UNITARES server you run: one identity per session and one check-in per completed turn, so the agent's working record carries across sessions. Fail-open; never blocks the agent. Disclosure — sends only to the server named in UNITARES_MCP_URL, which you host; there is no default server. Per session it sends your model name and platform; per completed turn a fixed check-in marker (never user, assistant or tool text). Hooks run synchronously, so an unresponsive server can delay a call by roughly 40 seconds (connection plus call timeout). After 3 consecutive failures the plugin stops reporting for that session only, until the session is finalized or reset; it stays fail-open and never blocks the agent. If UNITARES_BEARER is set, it is sent as a request header to that same server only.

name: unraid
description: Read-only Unraid monitoring for ViberVN Bot Desktop: server metadata, array capacity, Docker containers, virtual machines, and grouped alerts. Disclosure — sends fixed GraphQL queries to the user-configured Unraid host and stores a VIEWER key through ViberVN Bot secret scope; no telemetry, background process, shell, SSH, MCP, or mutations.

name: usage-flame
description: Pinned glowing chip + fire-themed panel with live subscription-quota windows (remaining %, reset countdown, burn-rate pace and run-out forecast with sparkline history) for every provider ViberVN Bot reports usage for. 12 color themes and fonts, RU/EN, zero dependencies, works on Windows. Disclosure — runs vibervnbot usage --json through the Desktop gateway (cli.exec) every 1–15 minutes and sweeps up to 8 providers every 15 minutes; each run queries that provider's usage endpoint with the credential ViberVN Bot already holds. Reads the composer's selected provider from Desktop localStorage. No network calls of its own.

name: usage-guard
description: Keeps an agent inside its subscription allowance: refuses a provider dispatch once a subscription usage window is exhausted, so an account that allows paid extra usage stops at the wall instead of spending overage. Reads the usage ViberVN Bot already displays, holds no credentials, and never touches account or billing settings. Disclosure — refuses main-loop provider calls (including MoA turns) for the providers in `provider_keys` (Anthropic and OpenAI Codex by default) when a subscription usage window reaches `threshold_percent`, and by default (`fail_open: false`) also refuses when usage data is missing, stale, unreadable, or the guard's own config is malformed; usage is read through ViberVN Bot's own account-usage fetcher (no credentials held, at most one read per source every 180 seconds by default) and cached in $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugin-data/usage-guard/usage.json; a `pre_llm_call` hook adds a short usage note to the next turn's context at 80% and 90% used by default, and an opt-in (off by default) `llm_request` middleware lowers an existing output-token budget near the usage limit; both read only the cache, never the network; auxiliary calls (compression, vision, titles, MoA advisors) are not gated.

name: usage-ledger
description: Local-only content-free usage tally and native Desktop statusline (Windows and macOS beta).

name: usage-stats
description: Multi-provider usage/balance for the ViberVN Bot Desktop status bar — shows live usage for OpenCode, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Kimi, NovitaAI, ZAI, Alibaba, Arcee, plus gateway-native Claude/Codex/Cursor.

name: ux3-product-design-harness
description: MIT-licensed product judgment across User, Evidence and Business flows, with one portable Agent Plugins v1 skill and all 91 original skill files. Disclosure: skill instructions run bundled local Python/jsonschema validators and read/write user-controlled local briefs, context packs and review outputs, which can contain personal data. Optional evidence gathering uses explicitly user/host-authorized tools, including external search and connectors; selected claims, queries or evidence go to the chosen services under their policies. There is no publisher-operated receiving endpoint, retention service, telemetry or background process. The bundled jev_gate.py runs offline; connecting a remote decision service needs separate configuration and consent. No MCP server, native plugin entrypoint, registered tools, hooks or middleware.

name: vault-view
description: Local Markdown vault workspace for ViberVN Bot Desktop: visual editing, progressive reading, cached image previews, optional per-conversation workspaces, pinned tabs, explicit selection quoting, tag search, links, backlinks and a graph. Compatible with Obsidian vaults. File transport requires a Linux/macOS gateway; Windows Desktop requires a WSL-hosted Unix backend, not a native Windows gateway; ffmpeg thumbnails are optional. Remote images and agent guidance are independent opt-ins and disabled by default; automatic note-content sharing is disabled; direct Obsidian opening is temporarily hidden. Disclosure — reads and writes notes in the vault folder you choose through Desktop shell commands on the gateway host; remote Markdown images and agent navigation guidance stay off until you opt in.

name: vaultknox
description: Secret-leak protection for ViberVN Bot chats. Scans inbound messages and outbound replies for API keys, tokens, and passwords with a 28-pattern detector registry, redacts them before they reach session storage or the user, and injects safe secret-handling rules so the agent never asks for secrets in chat. Zero dependencies, fully offline detection; pairs with the optional vibervnbot-vault CLI for encrypted storage. Disclosure — rewrites inbound user messages (regex secret redaction, may false-positive on password-like strings), injects a secret-handling prompt each conversation and rewrites assistant replies that ask for secrets; outbound replies are value-redacted with the same registry (regex-based, so a shape no detector covers passes through), with findings logged as detector name plus SHA-256 fingerprint and never the raw value. The vaultknox tool is inert unless the separate vaultknox pip package is installed, its write gate is a tool argument the model sets, and a vault policy that authorises raw consume_token returns the plaintext to the model.

name: vaultwarden
description: Vaultwarden / Bitwarden Password Manager (bw CLI) secret source

name: vector-platform
description: Vector (vectorapp.io) messaging platform plugin: ViberVN Bot becomes a first-class Nostr-based Vector bot (its own nsec/npub identity), relaying DMs through a local Rust sidecar that wraps vector-sdk. First run needs `vibervnbot gateway setup`, which provisions the bot identity (create or import). Disclosure — `vibervnbot gateway setup` downloads a prebuilt vector-bridge binary from github.com/BonesGit/vibervnbot-vector-platform/releases (tag v<version>, sha256 checked against that release's SHA256SUMS; set vector.prebuilt.download: false to build from the bundled Rust source), merges `vector:` settings into ~/.vibervnbot/config.yaml, writes VECTOR_* to ~/.vibervnbot/.env, and publishes a public bot profile (kind-0, bot: true) to Nostr discovery relays.

name: vet402
description: Look a paid x402 or MPP URL up in vet402's public record of real purchases before the agent pays it. BLOCK stops the tool call. ALLOW, and a WARN that only says vet402 has not bought there yet, let it run. Any other WARN, a URL with no record for the paying HTTP method, and a vet402 outage ask for approval, and the call is refused when nobody can answer (yolo, approvals off, cron). vet402 only knows endpoints in public x402 and MPP discovery, so an unlisted URL asks. By default only mpp_fetch is checked, and a payment made inside ViberVN Bot HTTPX traffic is not seen. Disclosure — sends each guarded or model-queried URL (scheme, host, port and path; userinfo, query and fragment stripped) and its HTTP method to vet402.com in up to two HTTPS GETs; a missing record or a vet402 outage asks for approval and is refused when nobody can answer, unless VET402_UNKNOWN=allow lets it pay; while enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session.

name: viajante
description: Flight and hotel search from your own machine through a local MCP server and one skill that tells the agent how to read the results.
