Disclosure — independent fan project bundling CHUNSOFT Pokémon sprites and SpriteCollab contributions that are excluded from the MIT code license; reads session busy state and message-complete/tool-start/tool-complete events read-only (other chats contribute only "a turn finished"), focuses the composer (caret only, no text) or reveals its own pane only on a user click or command, saves a PNG snapshot to your downloads only when you click Save a snapshot, and keeps companion state in plugin storage; no network or model calls.

name: vibervnbot-project-stewardship
description: Durable project ownership and bounded initiative management for ViberVN Bot fleets. Disclosure — a `pre_llm_call` hook adds a project's saved rules, decisions and facts to turns of bots assigned to that project; objective checks run allowlisted local programs only at autonomy level 3+ and GitHub objectives shell out to your own `gh api`; it creates and edits ViberVN Bot Kanban tasks through ViberVN Bot' internal kanban modules (title/body/tenant written directly to kanban.db), keeps its own SQLite DB under `<ViberVN Bot home>/plugin-data/vibervnbot-dockyard/`, and its optional HTTP API (`/stewardship/v1`, 127.0.0.1) stays closed until you set a bearer token.

name: vibervnbot-proton
description: Proton Mail, Calendar, Contacts and Drive for a ViberVN Bot, through an MIT-licensed client built from Proton's own open-source Go libraries (go-srp, go-proton-api) — no Proton Bridge and no paid plan. Reads, searches and sends mail (attachments, scheduled send, labels, folders), manages calendar events and RSVPs, contacts (signed/encrypted vCards), and Drive (upload, download, move, rename, trash, public share links). Sign-in runs in a terminal via `vibervnbot proton login` and the account password is never taken through chat; sending is refused until a recipient allowlist is set and every send is gated by ViberVN Bot's pre_tool_call approval. Disclosure — talks to Proton's private, undocumented web API over the network; stores a per-account session file (0600) holding OAuth-style tokens and the derived key passphrase (never the password) under the profile's plugin-data folder, and on first load copies any sessions from the standalone client's `~/.config/protonlite` into it; reads local files you approve for attachments and Drive uploads and writes downloaded attachments and Drive files under that plugin-data folder; shells out to gpg for calendar/Drive key provisioning; `proton_schedule_followup` creates one-shot ViberVN Bot cron jobs (read-only Proton toolset) that run unattended and deliver to your home channel; no self-update, no downloaded binaries, no telemetry.

name: vibervnbot-pubky
description: Setup helper for managed Pubky agents. The launcher syncs agent state, including conversation database snapshots and portable configuration, to your remote Pubky homeserver.

name: vibervnbot-quest
description: Read-only pixel-art RPG view of real ViberVN Bot Kanban and worker activity, with a live web dashboard tab and an optional native Desktop page. The Desktop page currently supports explicit local connections only; registry and SSH remote connections fail closed until a public SDK connection-lifecycle hook is available. Standalone demo data is synthetic. Disclosure — reads local ViberVN Bot data outside its own directory (kanban.db, every profile's state.db, profile.yaml, config.yaml model/effort, logs/agent.log, bot-status.json) on each dashboard poll: every /replay or /events request (about every 10 s while the tab is open) runs the bundled Python extractor as a subprocess (argument list, no shell, 30 s timeout); a background thread samples bot-status.json every 30 s (VIBERVNBOT_QUEST_SAMPLER=off disables it) and writes bot-status history, checkpoint state, a lock and a random 0600 HMAC key under <vibervnbot_home>/vibervnbot-quest/ (not yet plugin-data); profile names and task titles are hidden unless enabled and only shown to host-authenticated dashboard sessions; the Desktop page works only on an explicit local connection; no network calls beyond the local ViberVN Bot backend.

name: vibervnbot-resetwatch
description: Track subscription quotas and reset times in ViberVN Bot Desktop. Disclosure — probe.py re-executes itself under the ViberVN Bot Python interpreter located via VIBERVNBOT_PYTHON / VIRTUAL_ENV / the parent process or the ViberVN Bot installer's managed venv (VIBERVNBOT_HOME/installs). Every credential read is read-only and nothing is refreshed or stored: it reads provider API keys from the process environment, the ViberVN Bot .env, the Vaultwarden plugin's local secret cache (cache/vaultwarden_cache.json, only when Vaultwarden is the sole enabled secret source, keyed by a hash of BW_SESSION, which is never sent) and Docker s6 container env files; ViberVN Bot's saved OAuth logins (auth.json credential pool and VIBERVNBOT_HOME/.anthropic_oauth.json); and other coding-assistant CLIs' local logins: Claude Code (credentials file, macOS keychain or Windows Credential Manager), Codex, Cursor (macOS keychain and the IDE's state.vscdb, opened read-only), Kimi, Grok, ZCode and Command Code. For GitHub Copilot (on by default) it tries COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN (through ViberVN Bot get_secret, else the process environment), then the Copilot editor's apps.json / hosts.json, then runs gh auth token (prompts disabled, 3-second limit), trying each token in turn until GitHub accepts one. It sends each key only to its own vendor's usage endpoint, presenting the vendor client's identity headers where a private endpoint expects them (Claude Code and Codex CLI user agents, the Grok CLI client headers, and for Copilot the VS Code / Copilot Chat editor headers on api.github.com/copilot_internal/user, which GitHub does not document); environment variables such as GROK_CLI_CHAT_PROXY_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME and GROK_HOME change which host or file it uses. Usage results are cached under VIBERVNBOT_HOME/cache/resetwatch, never tokens. It exposes nothing to the model: it is a Desktop page only.

name: vibervnbot-rich-ui
description: Rich, evidence-backed answer cards — tables, charts, metrics, timelines, sources — rendered inline in the desktop transcript Disclosure — Image and ImageGallery cards load agent-supplied https image URLs (up to 8 per gallery) from any host when the card renders in Desktop

name: vibervnbot-routines
description: A minimal Routines page in ViberVN Bot Desktop that turns crontab's five cron.manage actions into a plain-language interface for non-developers - name a routine, pick a schedule, write the prompt, and pause or resume it. No cron syntax, no service, no database; routine data stays in the host.

name: vibervnbot-rss
description: Read RSS and Atom feeds and discuss articles in ViberVN Bot Desktop. Disclosure — feeds and full articles are fetched with curl through the gateway's shell.exec on the connected ViberVN Bot host (public-IPv4 SSRF guard); opt-in AI grading sends article excerpts to your configured model and creates VIBERVNBOT_HOME/skills/rss-importance-grading/SKILL.md if missing; opt-in image loading fetches publisher images directly from Desktop.

name: vibervnbot-rustpush-imessage
description: Local-only iMessage platform plugin backed by a launchd-supervised OpenBubbles RustPush sidecar over a same-user Unix socket.

name: vibervnbot-security-audit
description: Approval-gated local security audit for ViberVN Bot using Gitleaks, OSV-Scanner, and Semgrep CE.

name: vibervnbot-self-healing-context
description:
Intercepts runtime errors and dynamically patches the context window 
using local SQLite FTS5 memory for zero-downtime recovery.

name: vibervnbot-seo
description: Native ViberVN Bot port of Claude SEO 2.4.2: 45 SEO workflow and specialist skills, a credential-scoped vibervnbot_seo_run tool, an isolated Python runtime, and advisory JSON-LD feedback. Derived from Claude SEO 2.4.2 (MIT; FLOW prompt materials CC BY 4.0). Disclosure — derived from Claude SEO 2.4.2 (MIT; FLOW prompt materials CC BY 4.0); the vibervnbot_seo_run tool starts local subprocesses in the ViberVN Bot host process, not a Docker terminal sandbox, and model-supplied script arguments may name host paths, so it can read host files (the Gemini image-edit utility uploads the named file to Google, the IndexNow utility reads a URL-list file); `vibervnbot seo setup` downloads Python packages from PyPI within version ranges into a private environment and optionally Chromium through Playwright; audits fetch user-selected websites; separately configured providers (Moz, Bing Webmaster, Keywords Everywhere, Google APIs, Matomo, DataForSEO, IndexNow, Google Gemini) receive the data sent to them and may incur charges; skills ask before paid or mutating calls but the tool does not enforce approvals; Gemini images are saved to ~/Documents/nanobanana_generated, and other runtime state stays in ViberVN Bot plugin data storage; provider keys are read from the active ViberVN Bot profile and passed only to the script that needs them; Google OAuth workflows are disabled; no telemetry, bundled credentials, background process or self-updater.

name: vibervnbot-session-diff
description: Persistent session file diffs, run comparisons, and individual edit history in ViberVN Bot Desktop.

name: vibervnbot-session-reset-policy
description: Opt-in idle/daily gateway conversation resets. Reads the existing session_reset block (mode idle | daily | both, idle_minutes, at_hour) and starts a fresh session on the first inbound message past the boundary. No timers, no background writes.

name: vibervnbot-session-warmer
description: Opt-in bounded idle prompt warming for explicitly allowlisted OpenAI-compatible text-chat endpoints. Sends potentially billable requests; no tool execution or conversation writes. Does not support Codex/Responses or native Anthropic. Authenticated endpoints use optional VIBERVNBOT_SESSION_WARMER_API_KEY.

name: vibervnbot-sidepulse
description: SidePulse lifecycle status backend; Desktop focus tracking requires the separate companion in the linked setup guide. Disclosure — forwards event names, a hashed agent id, the raw session_id and tool names to a local AF_UNIX socket and a 0600 jsonl log; no network egress.

name: vibervnbot-slash-router
description: Jev-powered routing for misspelled, shortened, and meaning-based slash commands in the ViberVN Bot Desktop composer. Preserves drafts when unsure. Requires a TypeSafe API key; every non-exact lookup uses paid TypeSafe API usage. Disclosure — every non-exact slash token is sent through the plugin's local backend to api.typesafe.ai (paid, your TYPESAFE_API_KEY) together with the Desktop command catalog (names and descriptions), any prior route, up to 8 saved correction explanations and any clarification you type into its panel; message arguments and conversation content are not sent; the backend reads VIBERVNBOT_HOME/.env only to check whether TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set.

name: vibervnbot-snapcompact
description: Snapcompact context engine: archives conversation history as dense bitmap PNG frames that vision models read back at ~1/3 the token cost.

name: vibervnbot-soniox
description: Native BYOK Soniox text-to-speech and asynchronous speech-to-text providers with configurable languages and voices, automatic STT language detection, and ViberVN Bot voice-bubble support. Disclosure — TTS sends reply text and synthesis settings to tts-rt.soniox.com; STT uploads audio, optional language hints, and optional prompt context to api.soniox.com, then best-effort deletes the remote transcription and uploaded file. SONIOX_API_KEY is resolved through ViberVN Bot' active-profile secret scope. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, or stored credentials.

name: vibervnbot-speech
description: Give your agent the voice it deserves. Guided TTS and STT setup for ViberVN Bot, with voice search and previews, model switching, testing, and native spoken replies across supported providers. Access 80+ speech models through a single API key with the AllModels router.

name: vibervnbot-ssh
description: Manage SSH connections and remote workspaces in ViberVN Bot Desktop.

name: vibervnbot-structured-aux-models
description: Routes selected ViberVN Bot auxiliary tasks (approval, MCP sampling, compression) through bounded Jev decision calls on OpenRouter instead of free-form chat prompts, failing open to the operator's own auxiliary provider for anything it cannot express as a decision. Disclosure — sends redacted approval prompts, MCP tool names and compression transcript blocks to openrouter.ai using your OpenRouter key (read-only); on any error approvals escalate to you, never auto-approve; the default decision_model is a moving alias, pin it.

name: vibervnbot-stt-enhance
description: Local speech-to-text (provider stt_enhance) with faster-whisper or opt-in sherpa-onnx Parakeet V3 and long-audio chunking, plus an optional bounded LLM pass that enhances the transcript using a custom skill, an inline prompt or the default, and keeps the raw transcript on failure. Disclosure — audio is decoded locally. Post-processing is on by default and sends the transcript text to the LLM ViberVN Bot routes the stt_enhance auxiliary task to (your main, usually remote, provider unless you point it at a local endpoint or set post_processing.enabled: false). It reads the body of the SKILL.md you configure (never executed) and runs ffmpeg/ffprobe. The opt-in Parakeet backend reads a local model export and, on first use and only when your config.yaml explicitly sets security.allow_lazy_installs: true, installs pinned sherpa-onnx and numpy from PyPI into ~/.vibervnbot/plugin-runtimes/vibervnbot-stt-enhance/ (shared by all profiles). No tools, hooks, background processes, telemetry or stored credentials.

name: vibervnbot-subscription-meter
description: Provider-neutral subscription quota matrix panel — each provider's subscription window as a single time x quota row (elapsed vs remaining at a glance), with UI-side show/hide per provider row. Disclosure — reads provider keys from the current profile's .env and token presence from its auth.json, and calls each provider's own usage/balance API with that key (Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, Command Code, DeepSeek, xAI management, OpenRouter, Alibaba Cloud BSS, Grok, Codex via ViberVN Bot); an optional shared_sources setting reads another profile's .env/auth.json the same way; the token-activity heatmap reads per-day token totals, providers and model names from the state.db of this profile and of every other profile on the install (read-only, no message content, nothing leaves the machine); nothing is written outside this plugin's settings.

name: vibervnbot-switchyard
description: Jev-powered ViberVN Bot plugin for skill/model routing, typed assess, DOM/Cua computer use, adaptive reasoning effort with a per-turn receipt line, and FTS rerank. Disclosure: the default-on adaptive llm_request sends up to 1,200 characters of the current user message to TypeSafe/OpenRouter after ViberVN Bot redact_for_egress (no history or tool output); greetings and thanks are decided locally with no call; without the ViberVN Bot redactor it sends metadata only (disable via adaptive_reasoning_effort false). Separate default-on hosted skill routing sends up to 4,000 characters of the current user turn after ViberVN Bot redact_for_egress, plus skill names, to the same provider; without the redactor it stays local (opt down to local_only); light turns (greetings, closed acknowledgements, and read-only listings) skip that hosted call by default. Model routing remains advisory. Disclosure — By default, adaptive effort sends up to 1,200 characters of the current user message, and hosted skill routing sends up to 4,000 characters plus skill names, to TypeSafe/OpenRouter Jev after ViberVN Bot redact_for_egress (greetings and light turns stay local). The jev_session_search_rerank and jev_computer_use DOM tools send query/card and public-page text using the plugin's own masking. Off unless enabled: evidence prefetch sends source files the user names under evidence_finder_root (up to 80 KB), cross-tool stuck advice sends redacted error excerpts, and the switchyard-approvals provider, once selected for auxiliary.approval, sends flagged shell commands and your approval policy to OpenRouter Jev, whose confident verdict can auto-approve them (any failure falls back to a human prompt). /switchyard effort receipt saves the plugin's own setting to config.yaml.

name: vibervnbot-t3-control
description: Bounded tools to list, read, create, and control local T3 coding threads on Linux and WSL2.

name: vibervnbot-tabular
description: Tabular AI that grows with your tables — ViberVN Bot skills for honest tabular ML, one entry point. Disclosure — Installing pulls numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, pyarrow, joblib and pyyaml into ViberVN Bot's environment. The skills have the agent run Python on your data files, may ask it to pip install catboost, tabicl/torch, mapie or matplotlib, and the TabICL skill downloads a pretrained checkpoint of a few hundred MB on first use. Saved checkpoints are pickles: load only ones you made.

name: vibervnbot-tailscale
description: Browse Tailscale devices and connect to remote ViberVN Bot instances in ViberVN Bot Desktop.

name: vibervnbot-talk
description: Realtime voice for ViberVN Bot through terminal, Discord, dashboard and Desktop. Live voice mode (TALK_VOICE_MODE=live, TALK_LIVE_AUTH=subscription) connects with your own Codex OAuth session to the undocumented chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/realtime/calls endpoint, which is outside the vendor's published API terms and may change or stop working without notice.

name: vibervnbot-taskbar-badge
description: Windows taskbar badge on the ViberVN Bot window when a turn finishes. Calls navigator.setAppBadge on the message.complete event while the window is in the background, and clears it when the window regains focus or another session is opened. Disclosure — no network calls and no data leaves the machine; the badge is drawn by the app's own Electron process, which maps the Chromium Badging API onto the Windows taskbar overlay.

name: vibervnbot-teammates
description: Give your agent a team: named subagents with their own instructions, tools and model, which it assigns work to, checks on and steers mid-task. The operator defines the roster; the agent follows up with a digest of earlier results and can work a Kanban teammates lane with a review handoff. Launches subagents only through the public ctx.subagent_lifecycle API. Stock ViberVN Bot; no patched core. Disclosure — adds six tools (teammates_roster, teammate_assign, teammate_check, teammate_wait, teammate_message, teammate_stop) and a /teammates command; the model picks only a teammate name, and the operator's config decides what it means. Teammates run as in-process ViberVN Bot subagents using credentials selected by ViberVN Bot from the parent, delegation settings or an operator-configured teammate route where supported. Toolsets narrow the parent's tools at toolset granularity only (the file toolset includes write_file and patch); ViberVN Bot can add inherited MCP toolsets back unless delegation.inherit_mcp_toolsets is false. A teammate with invalid settings refuses to launch. A delegated child cannot start teammates. Steering uses the lifecycle steer where ViberVN Bot provides it, otherwise delegate_task's steer action with the turn-bound parent. Under plugins.isolation: host every tool except the roster refuses. Optionally the roster is read from an operator-named YAML file (roster_file, relative to the profile home or absolute, so several profiles can share one); the plugin never writes it. It keeps a per-profile SQLite run ledger in its plugin-data folder (goals, statuses, clipped summaries, role hashes and available token receipts; no full transcripts). It does not read credential stores. Where supported in-process, subagent_start and post_api_request hooks collect token receipts for mapped child sessions. For a card assigned to its non-profile lane, it claims the card through the Kanban DB, heartbeats the claim and its worker, then moves the card to review without a reviewer, or blocks it on failure, a stop or an unavailable result; it never completes a card. It runs one in-process monitor thread per run to retain finished results and, for lane runs, keep the claim alive; no network calls, child processes or self-updates of its own. Completion-notice code exists but never injects on current ViberVN Bot because the host cannot bind notices to the receiving session; use teammate_wait instead. Includes a report-a-problem skill: the agent drafts a bug report and files it to this repository with gh only after the user approves the draft.

name: vibervnbot-telemetry
description: Observability + budget guardrails for ViberVN Bot — tokens, cost, latency, tool calls per session and cron job. Persists to local SQLite. Exposes /stats and /budget slash commands. Disclosure — records per-session tokens, cost, latency, tool names and sender/profile ids (no message text) in ~/.vibervnbot/telemetry/telemetry.db; fetches public model pricing from openrouter.ai/api/v1/models on first load and at most once a day; in the default enforce mode first load writes a $5/day, $100/month global budget to telemetry/budget.yaml, and a hard breach blocks every tool call and pauses the over-budget cron job until the window resets (set plugins.entries.vibervnbot-telemetry.settings.mode: observe to record without enforcing); the optional standalone dashboard server binds 127.0.0.1 with no auth.

name: vibervnbot-telemetry-dashboard
description: Dashboard-only read plugin: visualize the shared-metrics telemetry ViberVN Bot collects locally — metric families, drilldowns, milestone timeline, install snapshot, and the exact next package payload. Send stays off.

name: vibervnbot-tenuo
description:
Security guardrails for ViberVN Bot tool calls: per-call authorization, so a prompt injection cannot make the agent do more than you allowed. Each call is checked against a signed, expiring permission slip (a warrant) before the handler runs, down to the arguments (file paths, search queries, spending limits), and every decision lands in a local audit log. Give cron jobs, delegate_task subagents and gateway users their own policy.
Disclosure — vibervnbot-tenuo is a no-op until a warrant is configured and blocks every tool call in a kanban worker that has no per-task warrant; it appends every tool call's name and full arguments to $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/tenuo/audit.jsonl (disable with audit_log: false); when TENUO_CONNECT_TOKEN or TENUO_CONTROL_PLANE_URL are set, the bundled tenuo SDK (compiled Rust core) streams those decisions, including arguments, to that control plane.

name: vibervnbot-terminal
description: Run the ViberVN Bot terminal interface in a ViberVN Bot Desktop workspace tab.

name: vibervnbot-token-speed
description: Live decode tokens-per-second chip for the ViberVN Bot Desktop status bar: 1-second sliding window while the model is still streaming, tool execution time excluded from decode seconds, UI spinner frames never counted, TTFT tracked separately, cumulative totals calibrated against authoritative provider usage at turn end. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

name: vibervnbot-toolsmith
description: Local developer tools, transformation recipes, and reviewed chat handoff inside ViberVN Bot Desktop.

name: vibervnbot-town
description: Local pixel-art town where every ViberVN Bot session is a resident and every tool call walks to a building. Passive lifecycle bridge to a loopback-only server; prompts, arguments, and output never leave the process. Disclosure — version 0.3.0 bundles the Town Node server and a prebuilt browser app inside the plugin directory and adds a vibervnbot town setup/start/status/stop/open command tree. Nothing is downloaded and no npm install runs at any point; node (^20.19 or >=22.12) must already be installed and is launched only by the explicit vibervnbot town start command, bound to 127.0.0.1 only. Runtime state, a 0600 bridge token, a bounded event journal and rotated server logs are written under VIBERVNBOT_HOME/vibervnbot-town/runtime/. On start the server also reads VIBERVNBOT_HOME/cron/jobs.json (job id and enabled flag only) to place one resident per enabled scheduled job.

name: vibervnbot-tripo
description: Tripo 3D tools on Tripo's v3 API (openapi.tripo3d.ai). Text, photo or multiview to 3D, image edits, retexturing, splitting into parts, Smart UV, auto-rigging, preset animations, retopology, format conversion (FBX, USDZ, STL, 3MF, OBJ, GLTF) and downloads, with an inline 3D viewer in ViberVN Bot Desktop that shows whether a model is really rigged, a library pane that shows where each model came from (the steps behind it, its prompt, a jump back to the chat that made it, and one-click next steps), a local model inspector, and a status-bar chip with the Tripo balance and this chat's spend. Every credit-spending call goes through ViberVN Bot's approval prompt with its estimated cost, and a per-chat limit (a setting under Settings → Plugins, default 100 credits) makes it ask again past it. Needs TRIPO_API_KEY. Unofficial; not affiliated with Tripo or VAST. Disclosure — sends prompts and the local images or 3D model files you or the agent name (up to 50 MB; every local-file upload, free calls included, goes through ViberVN Bot's approval prompt) to Tripo's API at openapi.tripo3d.ai with TRIPO_API_KEY; saves downloaded models to $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/tripo/ or a folder the agent picks (never overwriting: a clash gets a " (2)" suffix), and the Desktop viewer's save button copies models into your Downloads/Tripo folder (or the folder set in its settings); keeps a local task history in $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/tripo/history.json (chat id, tool, prompt, parent task, estimated cost, saved file paths; at most 2,000 tasks, never sent anywhere); the Desktop library opens local .glb/.fbx/.obj/.stl files only from inside your home folder, $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/tripo/ or the viewer's download folder, and uploads nothing; the status-bar chip reads your Tripo balance every two minutes and after each Tripo tool call; no shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

name: vibervnbot-trove
description: DAG-based context engine that never loses a message — full-text search, semantic recall, assertion-backed evidence compilation, and pre-answer sufficiency gating Disclosure — replaces the context engine and stores every turn's full raw transcript in VIBERVNBOT_HOME/trove.db with secret redaction OFF by default; with TROVE_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=voyage, transcript text is sent to Voyage AI for embeddings; as a fallback it reads private AIAgent attributes read-only via frame inspection. No other network egress.

name: vibervnbot-vcc
description: Algorithmic (no-LLM) context compaction engine: builds summaries by deterministic regex extraction instead of a summarizer-model call — zero-token, byte-reproducible, inside the built-in ContextCompressor; compacted turns stay searchable via session_search. Disclosure — no network calls, no env vars, no secrets, no telemetry; registers no tools/hooks/middleware and reads only the turns the host passes for compaction; debug: true (default false) writes one metadata-only file $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/vcc-debug.json. Derived from pi-vcc (MIT, sting8k)

name: vibervnbot-vcc-engine
description: Instant context compaction for ViberVN Bot: builds the compaction summary in milliseconds with no LLM call, keeping the exact commands, exit codes, errors and files, each linked back to its original message for recall via session_search. Disclosure — no network calls, shell commands or credentials; reads ViberVN Bot's config.yaml through ViberVN Bot's own loader; subclasses ContextCompressor and relies on its private methods, falling back to the stock compressor if they are missing.

name: vibervnbot-verifier
description: Attach an independent verifier (advisor) model to your ViberVN Bot session: it reviews each primary-agent turn delta, raises findings (note / caution / blocker), and can steer a blocker back into the session before the primary agent goes wrong. Read-only tool access (read_file, search_files) is available but off by default and best treated as opt-in plumbing -- measured across 216 reviews the reviewer made ~4 tool calls. Supports a VERIFIER.yml roster of named specialists, each with its own model and tool grant, plus VERIFIER.md review priorities. Ships disabled and off by default. Disclosure — off by default. When enabled, each primary turn's regex-redacted transcript delta goes to the verifier model's provider on that provider's terms and billing (one or more calls per turn per roster entry). So do any VERIFIER.md / VERIFIER.yml briefs found in VIBERVNBOT_HOME and from the working directory up to the repo root (confined to that root, 256 KiB per file). A project VERIFIER.yml can add named verifiers and instructions whose findings are injected into your session, and a blocker finding can keep a coding turn going. With advisor_tools on, an advisor can read any file the session can read through read_file/search_files, and those reads also go to the provider. The optional engagement gate sends a ≤1,500-char redacted digest per turn. The optional phase gate sends the redacted arguments of an impending destructive or publishing tool call and can block that call (it fails open). Findings, reasoning, short redacted excerpts and gate decisions are logged under VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugin-data/vibervnbot-verifier (rotated at 8 MB). Adds a /verify command, a dashboard API and a Desktop Verifier page. Development scripts (evals/, sidecar/, autoresearch/) run only when launched by hand: provider experiments use DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from the process environment or the host `vibervnbot` CLI, and offline analysis reads the active profile's session database and decision logs. No telemetry, no runtime shell execution, no access to ViberVN Bot's stored credentials.

name: vibervnbot-video-editor
description: Local video editor for your own footage: 45 FFmpeg tools for the agent (cut, silence removal, 9:16 reframe, captions, music with ducking, loudness, platform export and checks) plus a visual editor in ViberVN Bot Desktop with canvas, any number of tracks for text, shapes, video overlays and music, scenes and an English/German help. 100% local, no API key. Licence: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Disclosure — the Desktop page starts a local web server on 127.0.0.1 (random port, per-run token) that can read and write media and image files anywhere under your home folder (and any VE_EDITOR_ROOTS); preview caches go to the system temp folder. The agent tools run ffmpeg/ffprobe on the input paths the model passes and write media, image or .srt files at the output paths it passes (replacing an existing file only with overwrite: true).

name: vibervnbot-vision-inline
description: Attach an image inline to the session model when it can see one, instead of letting an explicit auxiliary.vision backend describe it. Core already attaches images natively by default; what this plugin changes is an explicit auxiliary.vision setting, which it overrides so the model reads the pixels directly. The image stays in context, so follow-ups do not reprocess it. The model's modality comes from the local models.dev cache; no network calls and nothing to configure. Disclosure — replaces the vision_analyze handler through tool_execution middleware: when the local models.dev cache says the main model takes images and its provider carries images in tool results, it attaches the image itself even if you configured an auxiliary.vision backend (agent.image_input_mode: text still turns this off); the image stays in the conversation and is resent on later turns; relies on ViberVN Bot private vision helpers, so after a ViberVN Bot update it may silently fall back to the normal path.

name: vibervnbot-vpn
description: Named network exits for the agent's browser: ask it to browse from another country and it switches, then verifies by reading back the address the far end actually saw, never trusting a label. Any VPN, WireGuard config or proxy works as a local exit; gluetun containers are discovered automatically and one can be brought up on demand. VPN credentials never reach the agent, the chat or the model. Disclosure -- a root-owned helper, installed out of band by the user through a narrow exact-path sudoers rule, is the only thing that reads the credentials and writes them to a root-only file (the agent names a country, never the key), and it pulls the gluetun image pinned by digest; the helper manages gluetun Docker containers, bringing exits up and down; the plugin registers a tool_execution middleware that holds browser_* calls when no verified exit is up (the kill switch, and optional cross-provider failover); it verifies exits by calling public IP-geolocation services (ipinfo, ifconfig.co, ip2location, cloudflare); credential entry is CLI-only, with no model tool for it -- `vibervnbot vpn provider <name> --set` (interactive) or `--from-ref`, which resolves a WireGuard config from pass/gopass or a host file host-side and never returns it to the model; opening a .onion needs `vibervnbot vpn allow-onion`, a terminal command a person runs (no model tool) that turns off ViberVN Bot's own internal-address check so onion names resolve and restarts ViberVN Bot, and the plugin never writes that setting itself; the active profile comes from the plugin context (ctx.profile_name), not a private core import.

name: vibervnbot-whatsapp-voice
description: Live voice calls with ViberVN Bot over WhatsApp, on the linked-device (personal number) setup most ViberVN Bot users already have, with no WhatsApp Business account. Call your bot's number and talk to your ViberVN Bot: the voice uses ViberVN Bot's own persona (a short briefing fetched from ViberVN Bot) and hands real work to ViberVN Bot mid-call. Or let ViberVN Bot call you for things that matter: whatsapp_call_owner rings only the configured owner number (it has no destination parameter) and reports answered, no answer or declined, so the agent can fall back to another channel, including from cron. A short summary of each call arrives in WhatsApp. Speech runs on Gemini Live (gemini-3.8-live by default), reusing the Gemini key ViberVN Bot already has; any Live setup field is configurable, plus a language lock. Setup is a dashboard tab (pairing QR, settings, test call) or an agent runbook skill. Disclosure — runs a separate sidecar process (Rust, built on whatsapp-rust) that the user starts or installs as a systemd/launchd user service; the binary is downloaded from this repo's GitHub release, built and attested by its release workflow, and checked against checksums pinned in the repo (plus the build attestation when the gh CLI is present). The sidecar becomes an extra linked device of the bot's WhatsApp number through an unofficial protocol, stores that session in the plugin's data directory, and answers only the owner's number. During calls it streams audio to generativelanguage.googleapis.com with GOOGLE_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY (read via get_secret), along with the persona briefing, the outgoing call's reason and ask_vibervnbot results as text. It calls the local api_server with API_SERVER_KEY for ask_vibervnbot (a full ViberVN Bot turn with the owner's tools), the persona briefing (at startup and after each call) and the post-call summary, a run that may write to ViberVN Bot memory and whose result is sent to the owner on WhatsApp. The dashboard tab's backend saves only this plugin's settings (through vibervnbot config set), starts and stops pairing, places test calls to the owner, and restarts the sidecar service (systemctl --user or launchctl). No telemetry.

name: vibervnbot-wincred
description: Resolve ViberVN Bot environment variables from the current user's Windows Credential Manager at startup, instead of keeping provider keys in plaintext in .env or auth.json. Config is secrets.wincred.map, an ENV_VAR -> generic-credential-target mapping (bare names or wincred:// names); each value is read with CredReadW in the current user's vault and handed to the secret-source orchestrator, which applies it with the usual precedence, provenance and conflict rules. Values may be UTF-8 or UTF-16LE (cmdkey and the Credential UI write UTF-16); anything that does not decode to text, or that contains interior NULs, is skipped with a warning instead of being injected as a mangled key. Disclosure - this source reads your Windows Credential Manager: only the generic credentials named in the map, with no enumeration of the vault. Resolved values become environment variables of the ViberVN Bot process and its children, exactly like .env entries, so anything that can read that environment can see them. The package is read-only and stdlib-only (ctypes): it never creates, updates or deletes credentials, writes no files, starts no subprocesses, makes no network calls and does not self-update. Windows only. Credential Manager is user-scoped, so this raises the at-rest bar for backups, cloud sync and dotfiles; it is not a boundary against code already running as the same user. Applying fetched values stays the orchestrator's job; the plugin never writes os.environ itself. Disclosure — when enabled, reads only the Windows Credential Manager generic credentials named in secrets.wincred.map (no vault enumeration) and injects them as environment variables of the ViberVN Bot process and its children, exactly like .env entries; read-only, stdlib ctypes, no subprocesses, no network, no file writes; user-scoped at-rest protection, not a boundary against code already running as the same user.

name: vibervnbot-windows-computer-use
description: THEIA — The Human Environment Intelligence Aperture: virtual-desktop capture, fused stage observation, guarded caches, bounded dynamic workflows, and persistent raw-RGB LocateAnything C++/Q5 CUDA grounding.

name: vibervnbot-windows-eventlog
description: Answer "why did this process die" on Windows: three read-only tools over the Windows Event Log. win_crash_events reads Application Error / Application Hang / Windows Error Reporting / .NET Runtime records for a time window, decodes the exception code (0xC0000005 -> ACCESS_VIOLATION and the other codes a debugger would name), reports the faulting module, its path and the fault offset, and groups repeated crashes by app and signature. Records are classified by provider as well as by event id, so unrelated providers that reuse ids 1000 and 1001 for informational events are not reported as crashes. win_shutdown_events reads the System log for Kernel-Power 41 unexpected restarts, bugchecks decoded to names (0x9F -> DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE, accepting the decimal form some providers emit), EventLog 6008 dirty shutdowns, 1074 operator-initiated restarts with the process and comment, and the 6005/6006/12/13 start and stop markers. win_eventlog_query is the general case: any channel, filtered by event ids, levels, an exact provider name or a payload substring, returning structured records instead of raw XML. Queries read newest-first and stop at the window start or at a 5000-record scan cap; a call returns at most 200 records and marks truncated payload text. Channel names, provider names and numeric filters are validated before anything is interpolated into the query. Disclosure - this plugin reads the local Windows event logs and hands what it finds to the model: application and faulting-module paths, exception codes and offsets, report ids, service names and provider message text, which routinely includes user and machine paths (C:\Users\<name>\...). Treat tool output like any other local diagnostic dump when sharing it. It reads only the channels the current account may read - Security and some operational logs answer with an access-denied error rather than any attempt to obtain elevation - and it never writes to a log, clears one or configures a channel. Stdlib-only (ctypes wevtapi plus xml.etree): no Python dependencies, no child processes, no network calls, no file writes, no self-update. Windows only. Disclosure — reads the local Windows event logs and hands what it finds to the model: application and faulting-module paths, exception codes and offsets, report ids, service names and provider message text, which routinely include user and machine paths (C:\Users\<name>\...); win_eventlog_query reads any channel the account running ViberVN Bot may read, so an unelevated account gets access-denied on Security and some operational logs while an elevated ViberVN Bot can return Security-log records (logon events with account names and source addresses). It never requests elevation, never writes to, clears or configures a log, and has no Python dependencies, child processes, network calls, file writes or self-update. Windows only.

name: vibervnbot-windows-ops
description: Windows and WSL triage skills for ViberVN Bot: processes that survive a quit (orphaned stdio MCP trees, lingering python/uv/node children), WSL-to-Windows interop where an argument reaches cmd.exe as shell syntax, config and encoding traps (UTF-8 BOM, legacy console code pages), and long-path or reserved-name errors. One skill plus a copy-paste command reference; the process, argv and job-object failure modes are pinned to reports #131561, #132069 and #61059 and re-verified against current main. Disclosure — instructions only: no tools, hooks, middleware, network calls or credentials, and the destructive diagnostics are marked and gated on asking the user first.

name: vibervnbot-windows-ports
description: Answer "who holds this port" on Windows. win_port_owners reads the TCP and UDP owner tables through iphlpapi (the same rows netstat -ano prints, with the owning PID attached) and resolves each PID to its image name and path, returning one structured record per endpoint. Filters cover one port, several ports, a process substring, the protocol (tcp, udp or both), the TCP state (listen, established, any state name, or all; UDP rows report bound) and IPv6 inclusion, with a record cap and a per-process summary of the rows returned. Built for the failure mode that stalls agents on Windows: a gateway, backend or bridge that cannot bind, where the error names a port but not the process holding it. netstat -ano prints columns, not fields, and its PID still needs a second command (tasklist, or a PowerShell round-trip) to become an image name; this tool is one in-process call instead of a shell parse plus a join, with no child process and no dependency on PowerShell being installed or allowed by execution policy. A protected process whose image cannot be queried keeps its PID and reports a null process name instead of failing the call. Disclosure - the tool reports the local and remote addresses, ports, PIDs and process image paths that netstat -ano and Task Manager already show, and those values reach the model; treat the output like any other local diagnostic listing. Read-only: no socket is opened, bound or connected, the only process access is QueryFullProcessImageName with PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION to read an image name, and there is no memory reading, no handle inheritance and no injection. Stdlib-only (ctypes): no Python dependencies, no child processes, no network calls, no file writes, no self-update. Windows only.

name: vibervnbot-windows-process
description: Answer "what is still running, and who started it" on Windows: win_process_table reads the process table (PID, parent PID, image name) and adds each process's image path and creation time, then marks every row with whether its recorded parent is still the process that spawned it. Windows stores a parent PID rather than a handle, so a child that outlived its parent points at a PID that is either unused or reused by a newer process; a parent that started after its child cannot have spawned it, so both cases are reported as gone or reused instead of a plausible but wrong parent name. Filters cover one PID, several PIDs, a name or path substring, a parent PID, and an orphans-only view of what outlived its parent, with a result cap and an option to leave out Windows session processes. Use it for leftover gateway/backend/server children after a quit, for telling thirty python.exe rows apart by start time, and for checking whether a process started before or after the thing being debugged. Read-only: processes are opened with PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION for QueryFullProcessImageName and GetProcessTimes only - no memory reads (command lines are deliberately out of scope), no handle duplication, no writes, no child processes. Stdlib-only (ctypes): no Python dependencies, no network calls, no file writes, no self-update. Windows only. Disclosure - the tool reports image names, image paths and start times to the model, and those routinely include the user and machine name (C:\Users\<name>\...) and reveal which editor, shell or agent started which process; treat the output like a Task Manager screenshot.

name: vibervnbot-workbench
description: The ViberVN Bot desktop app in your browser. `vibervnbot workbench` serves the desktop interface through the ViberVN Bot dashboard, for headless servers, VPSes and tablets. Disclosure — community plugin. On the first `vibervnbot workbench` run and again after each ViberVN Bot update it runs `npm install --ignore-scripts` (guided by ViberVN Bot's lockfile) and Vite against your ViberVN Bot checkout's desktop sources, writing only under ~/.vibervnbot/vibervnbot-workbench and its own plugin dir (the checkout is only read), and starts `vibervnbot dashboard` on loopback when none is running.

name: vibervnbot-worker-monitor
description: Kanban board groups and worker health in the ViberVN Bot Desktop footer: blocked cards first and red, live running state as a coloured dot, hover for the breakdown, one click to open the board. Worker-only fork of vibervnbot-monitor. No credentials are read and there is no network egress; it opens kanban.db and each profile's state.db read-only and returns counts only. Zero model tokens.

name: vibervnbot-workflows
description: Agent-owned workflow graphs for ViberVN Bot — a background runner executes a JSON DAG of agent nodes, fan-outs (quorum) and human/machine gates with fingerprint replay-skip resume, cooperative steer, typed failure events and compact status payloads; ships a desktop DAG view, an inline transcript card and the authoring skill with measured budget recipes. Stock ViberVN Bot; no patched core required. Disclosure — every workflow run spawns a detached background runner (wf.py run <id>) that survives session end, gateway restart and plugin disable until the graph reaches a boundary or workflow stop; each agent node is a child vibervnbot chat --query-file … --oneshot -Q … inheriting the runner's environment, and a node with profile set runs as that named profile (with its own credentials) only if the target's workflow_team.json lists the launcher; a gate's wait.until_argv runs an agent-authored argv directly from the runner, outside ViberVN Bot' tool-approval gate (the engine uses no shell, but the shipped machine-watch and incident-response templates use it to run a shell line read from a fixed-name handoff file under $VIBERVNBOT_HOME, and release-lifecycle one read from a per-run handoff file in the run dir); the runner makes itself the subreaper of its children and SIGTERM/SIGKILLs any process a node leaves running (its own descendants plus pids registered in the run's .proctree_sidecar.jsonl) when the node finishes, retries or the run stops; run and amend send a one-token ping through ViberVN Bot' configured providers to check pinned model routes; at gate.held/run.done/run.failed the runner reads the API server key from config.yaml and POSTs a wake turn to the local ViberVN Bot API server — the gate.held wake only relays the gate to the human, but the run.done wake tells the woken session to turn the run's findings into tracked work and dispatch follow-up work (as PRs) before the turn ends, and the run.failed wake to apply one corrective amend/repair/resume; a transform_llm_output hook appends a ::workflow{id} card line to replies for runs the session launched in the last 30 minutes; the runner reads WORKFLOW_MAX_SEATS (that key only) from $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/.env and the active profile's .env; state.db is read read-only, including every profile's session ids and profile names, and status/wait can read runs in sibling profiles' workflows dirs; state lives under $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/workflows/ (or a configured runs_root). No other network of its own.

name: vibervnbot-wsl-terminal
description: Run ViberVN Bot' terminal tools inside an existing WSL distro on Windows: one bash -c per command as the distro's default user, over the same files Windows sees at /mnt/<drive>, with no Docker Desktop, no image and no container to start or tear down. A host cwd is translated (C:\Users\me\proj becomes /mnt/c/Users/me/proj, \\wsl.localhost paths become the distro's own paths) and the mount root is asked once with wslpath, so a distro that moved its automount point still gets correct paths. cwd persists across commands, stdin and exit codes ride through wsl.exe, and vibervnbot doctor / setup and the dashboard picker get real rows (wsl.exe path, WSL version, distros present, selected distro). VIBERVNBOT_WSL_DISTRO and VIBERVNBOT_WSL_USER select the distro and the user. Disclosure — this is a full-access backend, not a sandbox: when it is the selected backend, everything the terminal tool runs executes as your user inside your distro, with that distro's files, permissions and network access, so dangerous-command approval stays on and ViberVN Bot never stops the distro. The plugin itself reads no credentials, stores nothing and makes no network calls; it spawns wsl.exe per command and wslpath once per distro. It rewrites one core-produced string, the trailing cwd marker, because under WSL a command substitution is handed the directory wsl.exe started in rather than the shell's current one (measurements in the repo's VALIDATION.md); nothing in ViberVN Bot is patched or rebound at runtime.

name: vibervnbot-wslc-sandbox
description: Run ViberVN Bot' terminal, file and execute_code tools in a Linux container on Microsoft's WSL Containers (wslc) runtime, so Windows users who run WSL Containers get a sandbox without Docker Desktop. Disclosure — the plugin spawns the wslc CLI (one short-lived process per command, plus one long-lived container per environment) and every call runs inside that container; containers have outbound network access unless docker_network is false; persistent sandboxes are left stopped on disk until removed; host environment variables enter the container only when named in docker_forward_env, and only paths listed in docker_volumes are bind-mounted. wslc rejects --cap-drop, --security-opt, --pids-limit, --init and --storage-opt, so this sandbox is not capability-dropped the way the Docker backend's is, container_disk is reported but not enforced, and dangerous-command approval deliberately stays enabled for this backend. The plugin reads no credentials, stores none, and makes no network calls of its own.

name: vibervnbot-xai
description: The xAI API surfaces core does not cover, nothing it already ships (provider, x_search, web search, TTS, STT and Imagine stay in core). Voice module: full-duplex Grok Voice (grok-voice-latest) in the Desktop composer, built like core's GPT-Live mode; the voice model hands real work to ViberVN Bot as a normal turn on the open chat (surface voice-live) and reads the result aloud; the backend mints a 300 s xAI client secret so XAI_API_KEY never reaches the renderer. Collections module: one read-only tool, xai_collections_search, over documents the user already indexed in xAI Collections (GET /v1/collections, POST /v1/documents/search). Disclosure — the voice button captures microphone audio and streams it to api.x.ai over a WebSocket; the backend calls api.x.ai once per call with XAI_API_KEY (read through agent.secret_scope) to mint the secret; delegated requests run as normal ViberVN Bot turns with the profile's full toolset and approvals, and their final text (up to 3000 characters) plus the last spoken turns are sent back to xAI. Each xai_collections_search call sends the query to api.x.ai with XAI_API_KEY and returns passages into the conversation. Nothing is uploaded, stored or deleted and no telemetry is emitted; xAI bills on the user's key.

name: vibervnbot-zh
description: Simplified Chinese (简体中文) language pack. Declarative locales/zh.yaml overlay for part of approval.* and gateway.*; placeholders match en.yaml.

name: vibervnbot_otel
description: OpenTelemetry for ViberVN Bot: sessions, LLM and API calls, tool calls, sub-agents and approvals as OTLP traces, metrics and logs to any OTLP backend. Disclosure — sends span data including prompts, tool arguments and tool output only to backends you configure (a backends: list, an OTEL_* variable, or LANGSMITH_TRACING=true); by default content_capture is full and unclipped (preview clips to 1200 chars, off sends none); vendor SDK keys already in the environment are used only after that opt-in; with nothing configured it keeps a local owner-only SQLite store under $VIBERVNBOT_HOME and sends nothing; installs opentelemetry-api, -sdk, -exporter-otlp-proto-http (>=1.35,<2) and PyYAML.

name: vidiq
description: Grow on YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok with vidIQ. Disclosure — skills only; you add vidIQ's hosted MCP server yourself with vibervnbot mcp add vidiq --url https://mcp.vidiq.com/mcp --auth oauth; tool calls send your prompts and authorized channel data to vidIQ and spend vidIQ account credits.

name: vk-platform
description: VK Messenger gateway with community Long Poll, media attachments, allowlists, and project-lane routing.

name: voice-ledger
description: Local ledger of the voice messages and recordings ViberVN Bot transcribes (voice messages from messaging platforms, CLI voice mode): /voice-log shows how many recordings there were, how much audio in total and typically, and how long ago the last one was, per speech-to-text provider, model, source, language or day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days or everything recorded; /voice-log recent lists the newest recordings (ten, or up to 100 with /voice-log recent 50). Disclosure — writes recording metadata (source, provider, model, language, file size read from the file system; no audio, file path, prompt or transcript) to plugin-data/voice-ledger/voice.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, always returns None so the transcription request is unchanged; no network

name: voicestudio
description: Client for the local VoiceStudio text-to-speech app (debpalash/VoiceStudio): speak short text, design or clone voices, browse voices, render chaptered long-form audio, dub videos, and check server status. Six tools with mirrored slash commands plus a bundled skill. Disclosure — sends the text, script files, videos and voice samples you point it at to the VoiceStudio server you configure (default http://127.0.0.1:3900, plain HTTP) and saves the returned audio under VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugin-data/voicestudio; no credentials, no telemetry, no self-update.

name: vornik-companion
description: Vornik as ViberVN Bot's hardened broker and long-term memory: ViberVN Bot holds no credentials; privileged work runs in operator-approved workflows on your own Vornik daemon. Disclosure — talks only to the self-hosted Vornik daemon at VORNIK_URL with VORNIK_BROKER_TOKEN (and VORNIK_MEMORY_TOKEN for memory); broker tools let the agent start operator-approved workflows on that daemon (writes are approved by a person in Vornik); when selected as memory provider it sends each turn's user query for recall, mirrors MEMORY.md and USER.md writes to the daemon, and asks the daemon to stop recalling (not delete) a mirrored entry that ViberVN Bot removes or replaces (/vornik-memory lists and /vornik-forget forgets what Vornik keeps); artifact tools expose only named outputs allowed by the approved workflow from completed runs and read bounded text or return short-lived binary download links from the daemon; task diagnosis tools (offered only when the daemon advertises companion-progress) return a broker task's execution events and closed error classes as the daemon serves them to a broker key; vibervnbot vornik approvals on writes security.approval.transport (and vornik_companion.approval_namespace) to ViberVN Bot config, after which ViberVN Bot's own dangerous-command prompts (the redacted command text) are sent through the local vornikctl agent host-approval to the daemon and answered on the paired phone, any failure or a Vornik outage denying the command unless transport_fallback: builtin is set, and the plugin never decides itself; vibervnbot vornik connect runs the local vornikctl, which adds an MCP entry to ViberVN Bot config.

name: wait-ledger
description: Local ledger of the times ViberVN Bot stopped to wait for you (approval prompts, clarify questions, password prompts): /waits shows how many waits there were, how many were answered or left unanswered, and how long ViberVN Bot stood still in total, typically and at most, per kind of prompt, per platform or per day, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, the latest session or everything recorded; /waits recent lists the newest waits (ten, or up to 100 with /waits recent 50). Disclosure — writes wait metadata (session id, platform, kind of prompt, how it ended, wait time; no prompt text, answer or session key) to plugin-data/wait-ledger/waits.jsonl, trimmed to 5,000 rows past 2 MB; observer only, cannot answer, delay or change a prompt; no network

name: walkie-talkie
description: Let one session message another existing session (Telegram topic, group thread or DM), waking it like a user turn so the reply lands in that chat Disclosure — starts agent turns in other existing gateway sessions (any routed chat, including groups, and from cron jobs) via ctx.inject_message, only after plugins.entries.walkie-talkie.allow_gateway_injection: true; after an accepted handoff it posts a visible copy into the target chat through ViberVN Bot's send_message helper using your existing gateway bot credentials; reads state.db, config.yaml and cron/jobs.json read-only; no network calls of its own, no shell, no telemetry.

name: wallaby-provider
description: Wallaby Token — curated open-weight inference (Kimi K3); adds Wallaby to the vibervnbot model provider list.

name: wallpaper-theme
description: A ViberVN Bot Desktop theme that follows your wallpaper. Reads Pywal's ~/.cache/wal/colors.json by default, or any palette JSON you point it at (settings page or ~/.config/vibervnbot-wallpaper-theme/config.json), derives a palette with checked contrast floors and repaints live when the file changes. Optional glass mode paints a translucent background for native window materials or compositor blur. Disclosure — the desktop half uses only @vibervnbot/plugin-sdk; the palette file is read by the package's own backend route (dashboard/plugin_api.py, GET /api/plugins/wallpaper-theme/palette, mounted once the plugin is in plugins.enabled), polled every 3 seconds with a change stamp. That route reads only JSON files inside the user's home directory (or XDG_*_HOME) under 256 KiB and returns colour fields only, never raw file text. No network calls, no shell commands, no credentials, no telemetry.

name: watchline
description: Watchline delivery adapter for ViberVN Bot. Polls a Watchline pull channel and forwards matched events into the ViberVN Bot gateway as inbound messages.

name: waypoint
description: Session status for ViberVN Bot Desktop: a thin bar next to every sidebar session with four states — Working (remembers your next step), Waiting on someone (who/what plus a follow-up reminder), Done (outcome plus a fresh-start handoff) and untracked. Suggests 3 next steps per session (instant quick ideas from the chat, opt-in AI ideas from the auxiliary model, priority colours) with one-click Ask, a Power up button that asks a strong model for sharper ideas on demand, and Mark complete to stop suggestions. Adds a Status Board page (columns, follow-ups due, stale sessions, archive all done), triage of untracked sessions, a resume banner above the composer, a status-bar counter, a daily summary, palette commands and English/Arabic (RTL). SDK-only: session-row slots, a route, sidebar nav, status bar, composer banner, palette. Disclosure — no network calls of its own (all model calls go through ViberVN Bot llm.oneshot); AI next-step suggestions are OFF by default; when enabled, after new replies (at most every 90 s) the plugin sends the focused session's last ~12 user/assistant messages (≤ ~7,000 chars) plus its title and the user's notes to the auxiliary task title_generation (ViberVN Bot default "auto" = your main model); Power up runs only when pressed — also with AI suggestions off — and sends a longer excerpt (last ~20 messages, ≤ ~12,000 chars) to the plugin's own auxiliary tasks waypoint_ideas / waypoint_ideas_2 (registered by __init__.py; unset they resolve to "auto" = your main model) or, for "My chat model", to the open session's model; an optional automatic big idea (off by default) uses the same choice at most every 10 minutes; Power up call log (2.5.0): the Python half also registers two observe-only hooks (pre_auxiliary_call, post_auxiliary_call) that ignore every auxiliary task except waypoint_ideas / waypoint_ideas_2 and, for those, write one line per call to the user's own ViberVN Bot log (logs/agent.log) and append a record to <VIBERVNBOT_HOME>/plugin-data/waypoint/power-calls.jsonl (rolls over at ~1 MB): model, provider, reasoning effort, response time, token counts (logged as 'unknown' with a reason when ViberVN Bot reports none), finish reason and status — never prompt, message or reply text, nothing leaves the machine, and the hooks never modify a call; reads session history (session.history) and titles (session.list); statuses, notes and cached suggestion text are kept in desktop plugin storage; archives sessions only when you press Archive (undo offered) or confirm "Archive N done" on the board (no undo; sessions stay under Archived); posts in-app and native OS notifications for due reminders and a once-a-day local summary; writes composer drafts only on Ask / Insert / Start fresh session and never sends them.

name: weather
description: Weather data, radar/model imagery, and verified meteorological calculations. Built on metrust, rusbie, wrf-rust, rustdar, and ecape-rs.

name: web-crawler-spider
description: A small spider that lives on the ViberVN Bot Desktop window: a web that grows with tool calls, helper spiders for subagents, an amber mood while ViberVN Bot waits for approval, spider-sense for risky commands, flies, napping. By default it roams only its own overlay and reads nothing from the app; walking between the app's real buttons and links is an opt-in setting (off by default). Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — draws an animated overlay on the Desktop window and reads gateway events (tool runs, subagents, approval waits, risky-command flags) and the app's theme colours; the opt-in "Explore the app" setting (off by default) also scans the window's buttons, links and alert banners, including button labels, to walk to them.

name: web-deepseek
description: DeepSeek Search + Fetch — routes web_search and web_extract through DeepSeek's in-house AI search engine and server-side fetcher on api.deepseek.com (opened up in the vendor's 2026-10-17 changelog: AI-native engine indexing hundreds of billions of pages, multilingual, filters SEO spam / GEO manipulation / low-quality AIGC). Registers the provider id `deepseek-web`. Disclosure — each search/fetch is a separate billed DeepSeek call at $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests per endpoint, and only HTTP 200 responses that produce a result are billable (5 QPS per account per endpoint, plus a per-domain QPS limit on fetch); the provider reuses DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and sends it only to api.deepseek.com; extract returns Markdown only (no HTML variant, so web_extract(format="html") gets Markdown), and anti-bot or JS-rendered sites fail (zhihu.com, x.com, nytimes.com returned HTTP 404 in testing) while static pages work.

name: web-defuddle
description: Defuddle content extraction — local, free, no API key. Shells out to the defuddle CLI for clean article markdown. Extract-only; pair with SearXNG or another search provider.

name: web-local
description: Keyless local web extract: fetches pages from this machine with httpx and reduces them to readable text with trafilatura. No API key, no third-party service. Extract-only; pair with any search provider.

name: web-meta-ai
description: Meta web search — routes web_search through the server-side web_search tool on Meta's Responses API (Muse Spark); search-only. Disclosure — each search is a separate billed Meta Model API call (per-query web search fee plus tokens) on MODEL_API_KEY.

name: web-octen
description: Octen web search with query-focused highlights and page extraction.

name: web-ollama-cloud
description: Ollama Cloud web search + content extraction via Ollama's native REST API. Search returns web results; extract fetches page content. Reuses OLLAMA_API_KEY (https://ollama.com/settings/keys).

name: web-oxylabs
description: Oxylabs AI Studio web search and extraction provider for ViberVN Bot. Requires OXYLABS_API_KEY (sign up at https://aistudio.oxylabs.io/api-key).

name: web-search-plus
description: Multi-provider web search, URL extraction, quality reports, and opt-in research mode. Disclosure — reads the operator's VIBERVNBOT_HOME/config.yaml (read-only) for its own Desktop settings block (country, language, max_results, auto_routing, provider_order, searxng_url, donsetch_bin) and, in its status command, the web backend and keyless_rescue settings, and checks (without opening it) whether a pre-5.1 .env file exists in its plugin folder or VIBERVNBOT_HOME/plugins, to tell upgraders where their keys went; may spawn an operator-configured local donsetch CLI as a subprocess (argv, no shell).

name: web-serply
description: Serply web search provider for ViberVN Bot. Google web results via the Serply SERP API. Requires SERPLY_API_KEY (sign up at https://serply.io).

name: web-toon
description: Paid web extract over TOON: web_extract pays a TOON node about $0.001 per page from a local payer sidecar; the node fetches through an Anyone network exit and returns markdown with a wuzzy/crawl v1 content hash. Disclosure — with TOON_PAYER_URL set and web.extract_backend toon, every web_extract URL goes to the user's anonfetch payer sidecar and spends about $0.001 from its TOON payment channel with no per-call confirmation; the sidecar's daily cap and origin allowlist are the only spending controls; pages are fetched through Anyone network exits.

name: web-venice
description: Venice AI web search + extract — privacy-first, zero data retention, $0.01/request.

name: webly
description: Publish a website, or share files and folders, at a live *.webly.site URL from ViberVN Bot with no account, then sign in to claim it, edit it, and publish drafts the person approves through the hosted Webly MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — MCP tool calls go to api.webly.ai/v1/mcp, sending WEBLY_API_KEY as a bearer header when it is set, and the webly server is marked untrusted so ViberVN Bot asks before each Webly MCP tool that changes something. The bundled webly skill runs a local Node.js 20+ helper (scripts/webly.mjs) through the shell: it uploads only the files and folders the person asks to publish or share to api.webly.ai (sites are public unless password-protected), runs the project's npm/pnpm/yarn install and build first when the folder has a build script, opens the browser for sign-in and claim, and keeps its anonymous-site token and optional OAuth sign-in in ~/.webly (mode 0600). Its doctor command reads ~/.claude.json, ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.codex/config.toml only to see whether a webly MCP server is configured there. Publishing, deleting and replacing sites through that helper are gated by skill instructions, not by ViberVN Bot approvals. The catalog copy has no update check.

name: wechat-social-assistant
description: Local-first WeChat relationship memory assistant for macOS: captures only what is visible in the WeChat window via system OCR/Accessibility, stores everything in a local SQLite database (0600/0700 permissions, no cloud), and serves contact briefs, follow-up planning, outreach drafts and weekly relationship reports through 32 MCP tools. Engine pinned to the immutable PyPI release wechat-social-assistant==1.5.1 over uvx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs uv on PATH. All data confined to PLUGIN_DATA via WSA_ALLOWED_ROOT + path enforcement. Never reads WeChat databases, never injects into WeChat, never sends messages — outreach is drafts for human review only. Disclosure — reads WeChat only by screenshotting/OCR-ing and walking the macOS Accessibility tree of the frontmost window (not WeChat's databases or a bot API), compiles bundled Swift helpers with swiftc into ~/Library/Caches/wechat-social-assistant/bin on first use, and needs Screen Recording (optionally Accessibility) permission for the host terminal; no network egress, never sends messages.

name: whatsapp-agent-platform
description: Community platform plugin (not affiliated with Meta) connecting a WhatsApp Agent to ViberVN Bot through Meta's WhatsApp Agent Platform API (/agent/v1): long-poll inbound (no public URL), text and media. Disclosure — sends the API key and message content, files included, only to Meta: api.whatsapp.com, plus lookaside.fbsbx.com for downloads (per WhatsApp's Third-Party Agents Terms, agent chats are not end-to-end encrypted); stores the poll cursor, recent message ids and the creator's id under VIBERVNBOT_HOME; no other network egress, no telemetry, no self-update. Exception: ViberVN Bot fetches image URLs in replies (SSRF-guarded, no key), revealing the server's IP to that host. Files go only to the creator; Meta keeps uploads up to 30 days. Received files are cached under VIBERVNBOT_HOME (deleted after ~24 h while the gateway runs) and may reach the configured model, vision or speech-to-text provider. WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_MEDIA_ENABLED=false disables media. By default only the agent's creator (verified through Meta's API) can message ViberVN Bot; WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_ALLOWED_USERS or WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS widens that explicitly. The agent API key is saved to the ViberVN Bot .env; the state file under VIBERVNBOT_HOME is 0600 and never contains the key.

name: wicked-memory
description: Persistent, wallet-scoped long-term memory for ViberVN Bot: remember, semantic recall, versioned update, history and approved hard delete, backed by the hosted Wicked Memory service, plus skills for using it and for connecting the Wicked MCP server. Works with no setup (a wallet is generated on first use; search uses the service's shared free key). Disclosure — sends the memory text and search queries the agent chooses to memory.wickedapi.com (or your configured base_url), each request signed by the agent's wallet, plus one GET to /v1/status on first use to read the published community key; stores a generated private key unencrypted in the plugin data dir unless you supply WICKED_MEMORY_PRIVATE_KEY; no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry; every wicked_memory_forget asks for human approval. The bundled wicked-suite-mcp skill walks you through adding the author's hosted Wicked MCP server (https://mcp.wickedapi.com/mcp, 75 tools, some x402-priced); that server is a separate manual step and is not covered by this pin.

name: wiki-ref
description: @wiki:<title> context references: attach the lead section of a Wikipedia article to a message, or one section with @wiki:<title>#<section>, with title autocomplete in the TUI and Desktop composer. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to <language>.wikipedia.org/w/api.php only (the referenced title and the typed autocomplete prefix leave the machine; a section is cut locally); no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @wiki: reference provider.

name: wireguard
description: Read-only status and peer list for a WireGuard server running on the same Windows machine as ViberVN Bot. Two tools: vpn_status (service state, tunnel address and port, server public key, per-peer handshake and transfer) and vpn_peers (the peer list only). The plugin runs only wg.exe show, sc.exe query, and one PowerShell adapter lookup; it never changes the tunnel and never reads the tunnel configuration file or any private key material. Windows only (WireGuard for Windows). Disclosure — runs local wg.exe show, sc.exe query and one PowerShell Get-NetIPAddress lookup (read-only, never touches the tunnel config or private key); tool results put peer public keys, allowed IPs and peer endpoint IP addresses into the conversation sent to your model provider.

name: wolfmarkdown
description: Create, clean, and verify standalone Markdown with conservative semantic repair and deterministic artifact checks. Disclosure — skill-only plugin that has the agent run its bundled Node.js 22+ scripts through the terminal; on first use it runs `npm ci` in the plugin folder (lockfile-pinned packages from registry.npmjs.org), and the optional `/wolfmarkdown setup` also creates skill symlinks in ~/.agents/skills and ~/.claude/skills.

name: woof
description: Plan, launch, watch and compare WOOF weather simulations on your own NVIDIA GPU: size runs with WOOF's own planner, launch them locally or on an ssh/WSL GPU host, get maps in the chat while the forecast runs, compare physics or resolution, run multi-arm research campaigns and score runs against radar and surface observations. Disclosure — runs need Linux x86_64 with an NVIDIA GPU (plan-only elsewhere); the user-run vibervnbot woof install pip-installs recast-woof>=1.0.0,<1.1 into ~/woof-env and downloads WOOF tables and optional geography (about 1.6 GB); runs execute the WOOF CLI as detached background jobs writing to ~/woof-runs and fetch public weather data; run events are pushed into the chat as user-role messages; the optional serve/ scripts download llama.cpp and a Qwen GGUF and start an unauthenticated local model server.

name: world-clock
description: One time zone in your ViberVN Bot Desktop status bar, every other zone you work with a click away. Click the time for a drop-up of your enabled zones; Edit zones lists standard IANA zones with live UTC offsets. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no network, agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

name: wyoming-voice-bridge
description: Wyoming speech-to-text and text-to-speech for a Wyoming server you run (stt/tts provider `wyoming`), plus a wyoming_voice_status tool that lists the server's models and voices. Disclosure — Audio and text to speak go to the WYOMING_* host:port you set over cleartext, unauthenticated TCP (public addresses accepted). Once selected, the providers send speech in every session, including cron and webhooks. Non-WAV audio is converted with your local ffmpeg. wyoming_voice_status asks for approval on each call and refuses under cron, yolo, approvals off, -q and unattended platforms; answering "always" leaves a command_allowlist line in config.yaml. It calls internal ViberVN Bot approval, config and write-guard helpers, so a ViberVN Bot update can disable the status tool or speech file writes (both fail closed).

name: xmemo
description: Native XMemo memory provider for ViberVN Bot — durable, identity-aware cross-session memory with semantic search. Disclosure — cloud memory provider: sends each user prompt (for recall and the search tools), model-written memories and mirrored built-in ViberVN Bot memory writes, plus a stable install ID, to xmemo.dev (Yonro Co., Ltd.); keeps a local SQLite cache of recalled results and a queue of unsent writes in $VIBERVNBOT_HOME/xmemo_cache.db, partitioned by a hashed account identity; reads the key from XMEMO_KEY (also MEMORY_OS_API_KEY / MEMORY_OS_MCP_TOKEN) and, if none is set, falls back to the xmemo login token in ~/.config/xmemo/credentials.json (a catalog rule 11 deviation kept for existing users); workflow and destructive tools and timeline capture are off by default and opt-in.

name: yandex
description: Yandex Search API as a backend for the built-in web_search (provider name yandex), plus a yandex_generative_search tool for grounded answers with cited sources. Disclosure — sends web_search queries and yandex_generative_search questions to searchapi.api.cloud.yandex.net, or to the base URL in YANDEX_SEARCH_API_URL if you set one, with your YANDEX_API_KEY and YANDEX_FOLDER_ID read through ViberVN Bot; the Search API is a paid Yandex Cloud service billed to the folder that owns the key; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.

name: yandex-disk
description: Browse, search, read, write, upload, download, copy, move, share, delete and restore files on Yandex Disk over its REST API. Disclosure — sends every request to cloud-api.yandex.net, or to the https URL in YANDEX_DISK_BASE_URL if you set one, with your YANDEX_DISK_OAUTH_TOKEN read through ViberVN Bot; file bytes go to the upload and download hosts the API hands out, without the token; unless YANDEX_DISK_ACTIONS leaves search out, loading the plugin sends one search request to learn whether the token may search, and yadisk_search is registered only if it may; every tool, permanent delete, emptying the bin and public share links included, is offered unless YANDEX_DISK_ACTIONS narrows them (read gives a read-only Disk); yadisk_upload reads a local file and sends it unredacted, and yadisk_download writes one, after ViberVN Bot' shared file-safety rules and the plugin's own: upload refuses .env files, ViberVN Bot' credential stores, ViberVN Bot' own directory and the home directories that hold keys and logins; download refuses credential files, ViberVN Bot' own directory, .vibervnbot directories, agent instruction files such as AGENTS.md, system locations and paths outside VIBERVNBOT_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT; other local files are within reach; YANDEX_DISK_ROOT confines Disk paths, not local ones; an upload from a URL makes Yandex fetch that URL; file names and contents written by other people reach the agent as tool output; no telemetry, no shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.

name: yandex_calendar
description: List, create, update, RSVP to, move and delete Yandex Calendar events over CalDAV, with attendees, busy status and several calendars. Disclosure — sends every request to caldav.yandex.ru, or to the HTTPS URL in YANDEX_CALENDAR_BASE_URL if you set one, with your YANDEX_CALENDAR_LOGIN and YANDEX_CALENDAR_APP_PASSWORD read through ViberVN Bot; all seven tools, delete included, are offered unless YANDEX_CALENDAR_ACTIONS narrows them; the tools act as your Yandex account, so adding attendees makes Yandex email each of them an invitation from you, and changing, answering, moving or deleting a meeting may notify the people on it; delete removes the event from the server and the plugin keeps no copy; event text written by other people, such as whoever invites you, reaches the agent as tool output; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.

name: yantrikdb
description: Persistent memory for ViberVN Bot. Canonicalizes duplicate memories, surfaces contradictions between structured or recognized single-valued claims for review, and returns a why_retrieved reason list with every recall. Embedded by default: no server, no token, no GPU. Optional HTTP backend for HA clusters; pluggable embedders (bundled potion-2M default).

name: yantrikdb-vibervnbot-dashboard
description: Local-only YantrikDB dashboard for ViberVN Bot memory operations

name: yolo-auto
description: Yolo-Auto: flat-rate OpenAI-compatible API with plan-filtered live model discovery.

name: you
description: You.com skills for live web search, URL content extraction, cited research, finance research, and integration discovery via the You.com MCP servers (api.you.com). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/, five skills bundled); auth via YDC_API_KEY, OAuth, or MPP/x402 — the free profile works keyless.

name: youtube-dock
description: Open your signed-in YouTube Home recommendations and Shorts in the existing ViberVN Bot Desktop Browser beside your conversation, without pasting video URLs or launching an external browser. Desktop-only SDK launcher; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or API keys. Disclosure — explicit user clicks load YouTube and its normal service/CDN requests in the native Browser; this plugin does not read credentials, cookies, recommendations or watch history. No telemetry, shell commands, backend service or self-updater. Uses the native preview toggle (Hide for an already-open destination), not a dedicated PIP player.

name: zalo-platform
description: Zalo Bot Platform gateway adapter for ViberVN Bot — relays messages between Zalo DMs/groups and the agent over the official Bot API (bot-api.zaloplatforms.com), long-polling or webhook mode. Adds slash commands and moderation. Zero extra dependencies (uses httpx, already a ViberVN Bot dependency). Production-tested on multiple Vietnamese deployments. Disclosure — connects to the third-party Zalo Bot API (bot-api.zaloplatforms.com) with your bot token; long-polling by default, or opt-in webhook mode with a listener on 127.0.0.1 by default that checks the X-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header; the setup wizard writes ZALO_* values to ~/.vibervnbot/.env; group chat history is stored locally under <VIBERVNBOT_HOME>/zalo-history.

name: zerosignal
description: ZeroSignal — private, pay-per-request inference through the local zs-proxy; no API key, your wallet is the credential.
